# ArcheAge Chronicles Demo — protocol and feature coverage

Reviewed: 2026-10-29. Client native-log build: `40367e24241c9481bfc07fbf9ef1919f25fb0eaa`.

This is the maintained reference for every recovered client-facing message in the current descriptor set, every established world/native-WebSocket packet mapping, unresolved named wrappers, and known auth routes without request bodies. It is not proof that unknown packets or future builds do not exist. Internal/common protobuf DTOs are referenced by field type, rather than incorrectly counted as standalone network packets. REST files also contain helper DTOs; their rows explicitly retain an unverified route.

## Status and evidence policy

- **Implemented:** a concrete current runtime path exists for the stated bounded contract. It does not certify complete official semantics, deployment or stock-client compatibility.
- **Partial:** a subset, fixture, bootstrap, tutorial-only implementation, mixed-use packet, or transport path exists; the documented remaining work is still required.
- **Missing:** no current behavior-producing runtime path was established. Decoding, generated protobuf classes, extracted action data, rejecting a request, or ignoring a report do not count as implementing the feature.
- Packet status is independent of feature status. An implemented message can belong to an unfinished feature. Captured official success, static schemas, source/tests and observed local-client behavior are separate evidence layers.
- The 2026-11-03 tools cleanup retired Python/PowerShell test harnesses and obsolete tooling. Historical test results and commands remain dated evidence, not runnable checks in this checkout. Runtime contracts and packet/feature status labels are unchanged; C++ tests remain available.
- Database distribution now contains one complete schema and its installer. Historical upgrade, rollback and maintenance SQL references describe retired workflows; the inactive schema-45 experiment is not installed. Runtime contracts remain at schema 44.
- Test source references identify available checks; this documentation pass did not run the full emulator suite or a new original-client gameplay trial. Existing validation reports must retain their dates and limitations.

The 7 captures contain **104,993 complete frames across 159 packet types**, with 15,258 client frames and 89,735 server frames. Every included capture's complete frames decoded and passed semantic encode/decode round trips.

**Original three-capture baseline (T/P1/P2):** 70,972 complete frames across 153 packet types, with 9,788 client frames and 61,184 server frames. Those frames passed semantic encode/decode round trips. Eight map IDs, levels 1–8, 42 completed quest IDs, 173 NPC CMS types and 40 requested player/item skills were observed. Counts describe world traffic including nearby entities; they must not all be attributed to the player.

**Original baseline activity:** 22 equip requests, seven polishing operations, one dismantle, two discards, 77 loot requests, 57 dialogue starts, four buys, three sales, five repairs, nine cooking results for one recipe, gathering/mining/tool actions, five perk changes, five stat-allocation requests, four self deaths/revive requests, 12 gliding starts, seven teleport starts and 16 ranking list exchanges. Merchant requests were followed by shop-reason item/money updates; requests alone are not a general success criterion.

**Original baseline blind spots:** no chat sends/receives, no full party join/leave lifecycle, no leaderboard score submission, and no substantive housing/guild/mount/mail/market flows. Player skills primarily cover Wild handaxe/longbow. Empty login snapshots do not establish a working subsystem. No PC2S_MoveReq appeared; the log does contain root-motion, rollbacks, gliding and map changes. Auth and front WebSockets were not recorded by this world logger.

## Transport namespaces and serialization

- PC2S/PS2C: world TLS application frames. Little-endian length/opcode; client frames also contain a sequence. Native X5Packet.log adds elapsed milliseconds and a 57-byte header.
- WSC2A/WSA2C and WSC2F/WSF2C: separate auth/front WebSocket namespaces; four-byte length/ID envelope, no world sequence. A repeated numeric ID in another service is not a collision.
- HTTP_C2A/HTTP_A2C: native auth protobuf payloads. Only documented routes are established. REST_C2F/REST_F2C include schema-only REST shapes whose URLs remain unverified unless a row names its route. C2AE/AE2C/HTTP_C2AE are JSON agent-engine (AI chat) shapes on the client's separate agent-engine base URL; rows marked emulator-defined have no client caller.
- Field listings use descriptor field numbers, exact names and scalar/message/enum types. Repeated protobuf fields can include maps; nested structures and enums remain authoritative in protocol/descriptors.normalized.pb. Field presence/defaults must not be guessed from names.
- The native-log build identifier and dumped executable SHA-256 identify different artifacts. The opcode inputs record their dump provenance; revalidate matches for another client build.

## Maintenance contract

Read this reference and the relevant feature's source and evidence before implementation. Update protocol/feature-coverage.json and any affected packet overrides in the same change as a behavior, persistence, protocol or validation update. Update capture observations only from sanitized verified counts. Never publish raw packets, player IDs, names, chat text, credentials or access-bearing URLs.

After reviewing changed sources, refresh their recorded hashes deliberately and regenerate:

```powershell
python tools/build_protocol_reference.py --refresh-reviewed-sources
python tools/build_protocol_reference.py --check
```

Refreshing hashes records a human/agent review; it does not audit behavior or promote statuses automatically. Pure refactors may retain statuses but must record the preserved contract and relevant checks. Synchronize the linked Page using its current block IDs/hashes; if access is unavailable, retain the local update and explicitly report the Page as stale. Do not mark the task's documentation complete while silently leaving either copy outdated.

## Additional capture comparison — 2026-10-26

Capture A1 adds 16,671 complete frames against baseline T / P1 / P2. New packet types: `PS2C_AttachDoodadNoti` (3), `PS2C_DetachDoodadNoti` (3), `PS2C_DoodadInteractionCountNoti` (5).

Combined evidence now covers 8 maps, 44 completed quest IDs, 174 NPC CMS types and 40 requested player/item skills.

Newly completed quest IDs: 10000162, 90118004.

Newly observed NPC CMS types: 1001674.

Newly observed map IDs: none.

Newly requested player/item skill IDs: none.

### Sitting and seat occupancy

Animation/interaction 70 maps to Chair_Sit_01_INT and HoldAfterEnd; two own seat starts on slots 0 and 1 have matching attach/detach notifications. A third pair belongs to a nearby actor.

**Boundary:** No server-side seat ownership, contention or disconnect-release path was established. This is not evidence for player housing.

### Smelting and carpentry station processing

Two recipe-60203201 Smelting results and three recipe-60207101 Carpentry results match own count-1 craft starts, material/Gold updates and static recipe definitions. Earlier captures only had Cooking recipe 60190101.

**Boundary:** No new skill opcode is needed: existing dialogue/interaction/craft-result messages carry the flow. Static/runtime processing support is separate from original-client local acceptance.

### Counted item-consuming world-object contributions

Five own interaction-49039 requests consume item 49025 from quantity 5 to 0, report counters 1 through 5 and complete quest 10000162. Catalog phase flow specifies a 20-interaction threshold.

**Boundary:** Only five contributions were observed; the threshold transition, linked object 49040 and subsequent event completion were not established.

### Interaction-driven channel/map handoff

New interaction IDs 71 and 72 have ChannelMove tasks; each is followed by InteractUnitRes and MapMoveStart/Complete on map 9012. Completion delays were 69 ms and 121 ms.

**Boundary:** The map ID stays 9012; these logs do not establish a new map or a specific channel number/private-instance policy.

### Additional gathering and object-animation variants

Two animation-1010 gathering requests, seven animation-1031 sickle requests and two interaction-animation-11150 starts were absent from the original three captures.

**Boundary:** Animation 11150 has a generic Use task; its player-facing purpose was not established from these records.

### Unchanged blind spots

- No new client request packet names, player skill IDs or map IDs.
- No chat send/receive frames or complete party join/leave lifecycle.
- Housing inventory remains empty; seat/doodad attachments do not establish construction or land ownership.
- No new market, paid-shop, mail, mount or guild workflows.

**Validation:** All 16,671 complete frames replayed and round-tripped; original binary SHA-256 verified; original three binary hashes and record counts verified again. Eight raw trailing bytes remain preserved outside the canonical replay file.

The watcher exited on a Windows status-file replacement denial. The stop-time game log exactly extended the saved prefix; all complete records through that snapshot were recovered. The extra raw tail remains private.

## Mage combat capture comparison — 2026-10-26

Capture M1 adds 8,449 complete frames against baseline T / P1 / P2 / A1. New packet types: `PC2S_CharExitReq` (1).

Combined evidence now covers 8 maps, 45 completed quest IDs, 174 NPC CMS types and 62 requested player/item skills.

Newly completed quest IDs: 90104102.

Newly observed NPC CMS types: none.

Newly observed map IDs: none.

Newly requested player/item skill IDs: 2201, 2202, 2203, 2207, 2213, 2214, 2215, 2220, 2221, 2222, 2223, 2227, 2231, 2234, 2244, 2245, 2249, 2250, 2251, 2266, 2274, 2275.

### New mage combat observations rather than new combat packet formats

M1 contains 8,449 frames, 124 packet types and Magic levels 1-3. It adds 22 requested ElementalStaff skill IDs to the earlier 40 player/item IDs. The only newly observed packet name is PC2S_CharExitReq (one); skill, projectile and timing discoveries use previously known packet formats.

**Boundary:** Existing class/action extraction is not a complete mage implementation. No local original-client mage, NPC or timing acceptance trial was performed.

### Expanded NPC repertoires and defensive behavior

145 NPC cast notifications cover 63 NPC/skill pairs across 16 caster types, with 22 pairs new relative to the other four. The Recalling Grounds Warden 5001529 now shows skills 220210100/200/300/400/800 in addition to the prior 220210700. Skeleton Scout 5001010 adds melee skills 190100200/300. The Herald Knight adds sequence action 230240120. Backward evasion 190700800 and shield guard 194100100 are visible; no damage is inferred merely from casting them.

**Boundary:** Fourteen of the new pairs are absent from the reviewed shared NPC membership input. The selection weights, conditional chains, guard triggers, evasion triggers, threat, boss scripts and chase mechanism remain unresolved.

### Attack windup and combo cadence now have measurable samples

Rotting Skeleton Infantryman 5001084 skill 190100300 lands six hits at median 1,397.776 ms after start (1,395.730-1,461.718 ms). Bound Prowler 5001015 chains 210130100 to 200 at median 1,698.297 ms (three pairs), then 200 to 300 at median 1,447.171 ms (three pairs). Warden 5001529 lands 220210100 at 909.195 ms and 220210800 at 1,207.180 ms (one hit each).

**Boundary:** The current fixed initial 1,000 ms and repeat 3,000 ms scheduling is local policy, not recovered AI. Measured intervals cannot simply replace it with a universal average. Damage amounts, selection policy and interruption conditions still need separate reconstruction and local-client proof.

### Mage multi-hit combos and a stage-attribution conflict

Basic fire skills 2220/2221/2222 report effects near 300 ms; 410/630 ms; and 860/960/1,050 ms respectively, separated by unique event ID. Thunderbolt 2249 has 22 stage-1 inputs, then 15 effect-200004 reports at median 600.366 ms after that stage input. The old runtime observation input still contains two 2249 stage-0 samples at 608 ms despite no such catalog stage-0 effect.

**Boundary:** The older 2249 stage-0 attribution needs reconciliation before a deliberate profile rebuild; no runtime input or generated combat profile was changed by this analysis. Multi-hit suppression must preserve distinct unique events rather than treating every repeated effect ID as a duplicate.

### Unchanged blind spots

- No new maps, NPC CMS types, status-effect types, chat or complete party lifecycle.
- One additional completed quest ID, 90104102, raises the corpus total to 45; maps remain 8 and NPC types 174. Requested player/item skill IDs rise to 62.
- No complete player death/revive request flow occurs in M1. A small sample of each boss action cannot establish every phase, difficulty or skill-selection condition.

**Validation:** All five native binary hashes and decoded frame counts were rechecked. M1's 8,449 complete frames passed strict-tail decode/encode round trips; 182 raw trailing bytes remain preserved in its original segment. NPC memberships were cross-checked against the existing read-only capture importer. Timing samples retain counts/ranges and separate NPC damage, client reports and arrival-clock measurements.

## Wavesword and open-world NPC combat comparison — 2026-10-26

Capture W1 adds 3,953 complete frames against baseline T / P1 / P2 / A1 / M1. New packet types: `PS2C_HealNoti` (1).

Combined evidence now covers 8 maps, 45 completed quest IDs, 176 NPC CMS types and 74 requested player/item skills.

Newly completed quest IDs: none.

Newly observed NPC CMS types: 5001285, 5001287.

Newly observed map IDs: none.

Newly requested player/item skill IDs: 2101, 2102, 2103, 2104, 2112, 2113, 2126, 2127, 2128, 2129, 2130, 2145.

### Twelve Wavesword actions with successful starts and distinct effect outcomes

W1 adds 3,953 frames and 72 packet types: 183 own skill starts, 152 mapped NPC starts and 21 nearby-player starts. Twelve newly requested CurvedSword IDs cover sheathing, directional dodge, basic and strong slashes, dodge-linked attacks, forward/back-input command combos and humanoid execution. There are 342 effect reports, 163 correlated effect-failure responses and 129 own direct damage notifications.

**Boundary:** All twelve actions were already statically indexed. Starts, effect reports, effect refusal and damage must remain separate. Captured official success is not local emulator acceptance or general execution/AOE support.

### Two new NPC templates and expanded Pallatius behavior

New NPC CMS types 5001285 and 5001287 both use the catalog name Leopard Battalion Heavy Infantryman, with different rifle/sword repertoires. W1 adds 15 NPC/skill associations and eight globally new NPC skill IDs. Pallatius the Severer 5001535 adds sheath action 5005022 and attack 140641200 to its prior observed repertoire.

**Boundary:** The two new Pallatius casts have no matching hit on the recording player. All 15 associations are missing from the reviewed runtime membership input. Ordinary weapon handling and Dodge are not automatically damaging attacks.

### Measured wolf and boss hit timing and repeated boss chains

All 19 direct mob hits on the player have matching cast timing. Alpha Wolf 362110100 hits near 690 ms (four samples); Seashore Wolf uses the same skill near 699 ms (two). Pallatius 140640100→110, 110→120 and 120→130 repeat at medians 1,792.971, 1,993.279 and 1,257.274 ms (five/three/two pairs). Its 140641300 hits near 1,994.941 ms after start (two samples).

**Boundary:** These measured chains refute treating every skill as a three-second attack. They do not recover conditional AI selection, telegraph/contact rules, perception cadence, damage mitigation or all boss phases.

### Sword contact windows and effect-refusal parity

Skill 2103 reports effect 210300 around 591/641/691/741 ms, but its catalog has one overlap group. Skill 2104 separates effect groups around 527-630 and 1,073-1,142 ms. Strong slash 2113 has 23 damage packets near 900 ms; follow-up 2145 has eight near 330 ms. The ordinary-effect failure response shape appears 163 times, with exact cast/unique-event request matches and no encoded reason field.

**Boundary:** Do not turn each contact poll into a new hit. Current refusal acknowledgement differs from the official capture; the cause and retry rules need reconstruction before changing protocol behavior or authoritative timers.

### First damage-linked self-heal notification in the corpus

PS2C_HealNoti is the only new packet name. It is a nearby player's self-directed notification paired with damage effect 111211, whose LongSword catalog definition has healHpPerDamage=15.

**Boundary:** This is not a Wavesword heal. A positive restored amount, rounding and cap behavior are not established, and no HealNoti output path was found in the current combat runtime.

### Unchanged blind spots

- No new maps, NPC types, completed quests, status-effect types or projectile types: the combined corpus remains eight maps, 176 NPC types and 45 completed quests.
- Six prior captures are used, including Wavesword, rather than dropping the newest baseline.
- Pre-start context establishes initial state but contributes none of its 17,061 frames to new metrics or novelty. Context contains earlier gameplay, not additional Warrior evidence.
- Threat, AI weights, navigation, general boss scripts, mitigation, parry windows, cooldown-reset readiness and full original-client acceptance remain unresolved.

**Validation:** All seven capture hashes and decoded counts were checked. Strict replay decoded and semantically round-tripped 4,948 R1 frames and, separately, 17,061 context frames. The raw segment retains 170 incomplete trailing bytes. Independent actor reconstruction reproduces 344/63/5 starts, 42 NPC associations, 36 positive hits and five zero contacts, and independently checks server-tick timing and the cooldown reset counter action. No runtime profiles, C++ implementation, deployment or game-client trial changed.

## Accounts, authentication and realm discovery

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Native HTTP authentication, auth WebSocket world entry, local accounts, launch grants and opt-in Discord launcher sign-in. Separate login authority and game processes preserve the recovered player-facing wire contract.

**Current implementation**

- Password-hashed local accounts, sessions, one-use handoffs and named-account launch grants exist.
- A named-account launch grant has a five-minute in-memory activation window and survives launcher session renewal during the intro. Initial activation stores only the SHA-256 digest of the same URL as a fixed 24-hour, account-bound reconnect bearer credential. PostgreSQL schema 32 persists it across server restarts; a new launch, password reset, ban or operator sign-out revokes it. Launcher and game logout preserve an activated credential so the running client can reauthenticate.
- Bootstrap, public world discovery, Steam local mapping, login upgrade, logout and world entry have handlers.
- The single realm lists a configurable world name (default Project Chronicles Private Server), site display name, label and character-creation restriction. Its state is derived from the accepted world-connection population: Normal, Congested from 80% of the configured capacity (default 500), Overloaded at capacity, GmOnly in maintenance.
- Realm entry returns ServerOverload at capacity and WorldIsUnderMaintenance in maintenance. WorldListRes.last_world_id is set once the account owns a character on the realm. GET /health and the launcher realm panel report the realm name, population, capacity and state.
- Operator-assigned account roles (player, gm) persist in emulator_accounts.account_role and change only through `chronicles-account role ACCOUNT player|gm` or the optional CHRONICLES_BOOTSTRAP_ACCOUNT_ROLE. Login, launch grants and session rotation set AuthChallengeRes.gm from the role, and the role is copied into the world handoff. Game masters may enter the realm in maintenance (listed as GmOnly) and at capacity.
- Operator console API (/admin/v1, emulator-owned; bearer token from --admin-token-file, loopback-only unless --admin-allow-remote with HTTPS) changes the realm name, site display name, capacity, label, maintenance and character-creation restriction while the server runs. Values persist atomically in --admin-settings-file and override the matching command-line options at the next start.
- Operator account management: list/search, create (player or gm), password reset (revokes sessions, tickets and launch grants), role change (applies at next login), ban/unban and sign-out everywhere. emulator_accounts.banned (schema version 14) makes a correct-password login return LoginDenyRestrictedAccount; banning revokes the account's sessions and closes its world connections.
- A shared 8-256 UTF-8 byte password policy governs new accounts and password resets in the backend, player launcher and admin UI. Existing hashes and password-login behavior are preserved.
- The admin console connects immediately when Local testing or an operator-configured preset is selected, using existing operator token/SSH references from its private app-data catalog, adjacent catalog or packaged development fallback. Existing default Custom settings migrate to the matching preset, the last successful server is remembered, and preset mode hides address/token inputs. Native and UI attempt guards prevent late connection results from replacing a newer selection. Explicit custom/command-line connections remain available; server authentication and loopback-only admin policy are unchanged.
- The realm editor fills cached values immediately, protects dirty drafts against delayed remote overviews, retains newer edits made during save and pauses background chat polling while editing. It reports durable save only for settings_saved=true. The hosted deployment enables an admin settings file in a dedicated Local Service-writable state directory; no credential or executable directories gain write access. Realm-list labels remain the native None/New/Recommended enum.
- Admin capacity uses a plain numeric text editor and validates decimal digits in the inclusive 1-100000 range on Save. The admin host explicitly forwards window focus to the WebView control, preserving the prior focused editor after activation. This host option is enabled only for the admin console; player-launcher defaults are preserved.
- The admin Rates page hydrates from the selected server connection overview while refreshing; unloaded values show Loading instead of a hardcoded 1.0x. Request revisions and connection guards prevent older settings/overview replies from replacing a newer rate save or another server state. Percentage drafts survive refreshes, and rate save feedback checks settings_saved rather than claiming every applied update is durable.
- Project Chronicles 0.2.2 checks signed Steam v161 compatibility files on managed-game startup and before Play. Large existing game archives report progress during SHA-256 reads. Installation scans under its lock once instead of repeating a preflight full scan; explicit Verify / repair still checks every signed file.
- An isolated 0.2.5 player-launcher candidate checks a separate signed launcher-stable channel at startup, stages verified player files, then hands replacement to a second process. The existing journal provides rollback and recovery; the allowlist excludes game files and stored settings. This is source-level candidate behavior and has not been published.
- The launcher stores a per-realm Project Chronicles account and session in Windows Credential Manager for the current Windows user, independently of launcher settings files; password sign-in can also save the password. It migrates a previous protected login file after vault readback, retains separate credentials on realm changes and removes the selected realm's credential on sign-out. The simplified sign-in panel offers one persistence choice and retains Discord sign-in and linking.
- The launcher selects the registered Steam installation by default, otherwise an existing Project Chronicles or ArcheAge installation in bounded local locations. A player-selected folder takes precedence. The updater adopts an existing game in place, verifies signed files, and stages and backs up only changed files; Steam can later replace Project Chronicles compatibility files.
- The launcher records a fingerprint of each verified signed game-file set. Normal startup, Play and update checks reuse it across realm catalogs with the same files while maintaining per-origin rollback history. Fast checks still validate file presence, sizes and launch-critical Steam compatibility hashes; explicit repair performs a full hash scan.
- Opt-in Discord authorization-code sign-in uses identify-only scope, S256 PKCE, five-minute one-use state, a private polling secret and proof returned through an automatically bound IPv4 loopback browser listener on the initiating PC. Issuer, application, scope and stable user ID are verified before proof-gated account creation/session issuance. Explicit linking requires a current launcher session at redemption and never infers ownership from names or email. Schema version 30 stores unique account/Discord identity links atomically; new identities receive player accounts and existing bans/session/launch-grant rules apply. GET /emulator/v1/auth-options, POST /emulator/v1/discord/start, GET /emulator/v1/discord/callback and POST /emulator/v1/discord/poll are emulator-owned JSON/browser routes, not recovered native packets. Secrets stay in a private backend configuration; the launcher stores only its own Project Chronicles session in Windows Credential Manager, without saving the Discord access token.
- Both packaged launcher entrypoints default to the loopback server (HTTP 8080, world 8081). An explicit operator-owned launcher-config.json can supply up to 32 unique server entries with world endpoints and channels. Hosted entries require HTTPS and their own pinned signing public key. No hosted service, signing identity or Discord community is built in. Realm switching preserves the existing separate-origin session and update behavior.
- Password reset, ban and kick invalidate the account's in-memory sessions, selection tickets, unactivated launch grants and any consumed-but-not-yet-admitted world handoff, delete durable reconnect credentials (atomically with the password/ban update) and request closure of the account's world connections before returning success. A storage error, including an uncertain COMMIT, returns an error and quarantines the account in this process until a later successful password login revokes durable credentials.
- HTTP authentication work (password login, registration, launch grants, Discord routes, native /api/auth/*, /launch/*, /native/bootstrap and WebSocket upgrades) runs on a four-thread pool limited to 16 concurrent requests and 4 per socket peer (HTTP 503 with Retry-After). Bad passwords and registrations are rate limited per peer/account (HTTP 429); forwarded IP headers are ignored. --max-http-connections (default 1280) bounds HTTP/WebSocket connections.
- Fresh database installation: tools/install_database.ps1 creates a dedicated PostgreSQL 16 login/database and applies the single complete migrations/001_accounts_characters.sql baseline. Repeated installation preserves current-schema data and login passwords; older, missing-table and unrelated schemas are rejected. The baseline retains schema-44 runtime contracts without replaying historical updates.
- Autonomous login service owns account authentication, sessions, launcher grants and pending world admissions. The game process owns character and world state and authenticates through a private versioned authority connection. Both services verify the same PostgreSQL identity and use separate exclusive process leases.
- Private loopback authority requests and replies use authenticated encryption, operation/database/request binding, freshness checks and a bounded replay guard. Lost mutation replies are not automatically replayed. Game session lookup fails closed on authority outage; uncertain account mutations retain local quarantine until acknowledged operator reconciliation.
- Character selection registers one account/character/world-bound admission. Both existing world credential formats consume the same ticket, with a private login-incarnation identifier preventing restart collisions. The remote commit on a worker is the cross-service authorization point; the final socket continuation claims only its matching prepared local result without network I/O.
- The game publishes population heartbeats. Login marks the realm offline and refuses entry after five seconds without a fresh heartbeat. Public login defaults to port 8080, game/operator HTTP to 8082, world TLS to 8081 and private authority to loopback 8090.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Official Steam ticket validation and the native password challenge calculation are not implemented.
- Hosted launch-grant/TLS entry has one packaged original-client acceptance trial on the researched build; other client builds and general platform identity remain unverified. Local aliases are not trusted platform identity.
- The WorldEnterRes.QueueTicket waiting queue is not implemented; a full realm refuses entry instead. Capacity is checked at realm entry, so lobby players can briefly exceed it. Congestion thresholds are emulator policy, not recovered official values.
- Original-client rendering of the realm label, congestion/maintenance state and creation restriction has not been observed.
- A role change applies at the next login. The client stores AuthChallengeRes.gm, but no reader was found, so its effect beyond the world console is unknown. LobbyCharacter/WorldCharacter.gm_command_flag is not set because no consumer was traced. The capacity bypass for game masters is emulator policy.
- Console realm changes reach clients only through the next realm list and realm entry; no unsolicited lobby/realm update (WSF2C_LobbyUpdateNoti) is sent. Original-client display of LoginDenyRestrictedAccount has not been observed.
- Discord sign-in is enabled on the live Windows backend and has real browser, persistent-link, fresh-login and original-client world-entry acceptance through the packaged player launcher. Other server platforms still require an outbound HTTPS adapter. Identity unlinking is not exposed; general gameplay and capacity are not established by this account-flow trial.
- Reconnect is implemented for an activated game URL; an unactivated grant and a game launched before this change cannot survive a server restart. The activated URL remains a replayable bearer secret until its 24-hour expiry or revocation, so HTTPS and proxy path redaction are required. Original-client reconnect and TLS-helper re-entry are not yet observed.
- Launcher self-update requires an initial manual installation of an updater-capable version. Public channel publication, a packaged production old-to-new trial and installed/portable recovery acceptance remain pending.
- Revocation quarantine and pending world admissions are process-local: there is no crash-durable revocation journal, so an uncertain revocation followed by a process restart can leave an old reconnect credential usable; replicated login authorities, multiple game authorities and independent hosts are not supported. The supported split coordinates one login and one game process over one database. Users behind one NAT or proxy share socket-peer budgets.
- The service split has synthetic two-process PostgreSQL/TLS acceptance only; original-client gameplay after this split remains unobserved. Login sessions remain process-local and restart requires reauthentication. The private authority currently requires same-host loopback deployment and a shared database; multi-host TLS, independent databases and session replication are not implemented. Revocation after the remote admission commit is handled by existing game-side connection controls, not a distributed final-socket transaction.

**Evidence and verification**

Local original-client trial on build v26.10.18.734 with the clean Release Steam API compatibility DLL and a fresh named-account grant: the client displayed the NA realm Project Chronicles Private Server and reached its existing character selection. The loopback server logged successful native Steam AuthReq, realm discovery, login upgrade and front WebSocket traffic; no Steam client was used for this isolated trial. An earlier grant returned HTTP 401 after the launcher renewed its expiring password session during the intro. Three focused C++ auth tests pass for grant lifetime, launcher renewal and one-use handoff. The live loopback server still runs the older binary; the grant fix needs deployment. A separate local original-client trial with the guarded user-mode world helper completed TLS 1.3, accepted the native world credential, sent map/bootstrap data, and rendered a world HUD and action. The helper restored the verified two-byte startup gate and the SSL callback field. The unassisted connection had failed the TLS handshake. This is limited to the researched v26.10.18.734 client and loopback service; hosted world entry remains open. Native password challenge and general remote compatibility remain open. A fresh launcher-driven trial then started the same client while steam.exe was absent, displayed the NA realm and entered a playable overworld. The game loaded the local compatibility DLL. A Windows host with no Steam installation or service was not tested. Public-access check (2026-10-27 UTC): at the operator's explicit request, public player ports were opened. A synthetic new account registered over hosted HTTPS (201), duplicate creation was rejected (409), login/realm list/character roster succeeded (200) and logout succeeded (204). No account or credential values are published. This establishes self-service registration and launcher API access, not original-client hosted world entry. Local Discord/password validation (2026-10-27 UTC): ten synthetic backend OAuth/password tests, 26 launcher/account/saved-login tests and 14 native-auth regressions passed; real loopback TCP covers browser confirmation, wrong-state refusal and retry. An isolated PostgreSQL test passed durable identity reconnect and concurrent first-login atomicity after additive migration 30. Backend and launcher entry points compile with zero warnings/errors; JavaScript syntax and whitespace checks pass. Existing password sessions, bans, logout, grants and explicit account ownership are preserved. Active executables/services and existing databases were not replaced; no live provider, release-package or game-client acceptance is claimed. See docs/discord-sign-in.md. Admin preset connection repair (2026-10-26, America/Sao_Paulo): Release admin build and JavaScript syntax/DOM/mail/message/preset regression checks passed. The rebuilt console connected to both existing servers with only Local/Live profile IDs; the running desktop UI displayed Connected on the live preset without manual credentials. Private local catalog provisioning and the admin executable/interface were updated; server processes, permissions, account data and stored credentials were preserved. No native packet behavior changed. See docs/admin-console.md. Realm edit/persistence repair (2026-10-26, America/Sao_Paulo): three existing backend realm-save/reload, invalid-input and message-persistence cases passed, and UI delayed-reply/draft/save feedback regressions passed. A guarded live configuration update preserved realm, rates/events and messages, and one restart occurred only with an enabled task and zero world connections. The live backend reported settings_persisted=true; two unchanged realm saves returned settings_saved=true and disk readback verified replacement. Current capacity 64 and label None were preserved. The initial automation pass could not obtain actionable control geometry; later operator keyboard acceptance is recorded in the capacity follow-up below. No native protocol or game/server binary change was made. Capacity keyboard follow-up: Release admin rebuilt and installed with the plain text control and explicit WebView focus forwarding. UI checks reject empty/zero/signed/fractional/scientific/oversized/nonnumeric capacity without sending requests, and accept boundary/intermediate values 1, 64, 99999 and 100000. The operator then confirmed direct native typing works: selecting 64 and entering a replacement number without arrows succeeds in the reopened admin. No server or protocol behavior changed in this follow-up. Project Chronicles 0.2.1 production acceptance (2026-10-27 UTC): source a9bb609 was built and pushed; 127 focused C++ cases passed and four optional fixtures skipped. The isolated PostgreSQL identity/concurrent-first-login check and 16 signed-distribution/backend/updater checks passed. A fresh offsite database backup passed SHA-256 and disposable restore verification; additive migration 30 preserved existing account, character and exploration records. An initial readiness failure rolled back safely; an isolated candidate then passed and the retry finished the old service wrapper before launching the new backend. Live health/auth-options/news/content/catalog routes return 200, Discord is enabled and public administration returns 403. The operator completed real browser authorization, verified an existing-account link, signed out and signed in with Discord in the packaged player launcher. That session launched the original client into the hosted world. The helper checked the selected hostname, observed both network threads with verify_result zero and restored both temporary changes; the server reported the world session and the operator confirmed playable entry. Installer, portable ZIP, checksums, changelog and sanitized release-check log were published by the Project Chronicles bot; independent Discord downloads matched all five local hashes. This is bounded account/entry/release acceptance, not full gameplay or a load-test claim. Rate display/reopen repair (2026-10-27, America/Sao_Paulo): live API and disk both reported 500% before and after reopening the updated admin, with no rate mutation or backend restart. The separate local realm retained 100%. Two existing rate/event persistence tests and UI cached-hydration, late-1x refusal after a 5x save, draft/reopen and nonpersistent-feedback checks passed, alongside syntax/whitespace checks. The hardcoded loading display, not a lost live setting, explained the observed 1.0x screenshot. Project Chronicles 0.2.2 player-report repair (2026-10-27): the live signed game catalog listed a 41,065,461,616-byte X5-Windows.ucas and the Steam v161 compatibility payload. The prior checker could appear fixed at 5.39 GB while hashing that archive. The local managed copy matched all six signed compatibility hashes; the Steam source DLL differed as expected. A focused launcher build passed, 12 installer/compatibility tests passed, and the full launcher suite passed 99 cases with four optional fixtures skipped. These are local source and signed-catalog checks, not a trial on the reporting player machine; its path and file state are still unconfirmed. Backend and signed game catalog did not change. Reconnect fix (2026-10-27): 29 focused Auth/NativeAuth cases and three admin ban/password/authorization cases passed. Native HTTP smoke passed. An isolated PostgreSQL-backed server process was restarted with the same account and accepted the activated credential, returned world list, login upgrade and world-entry authorization; a further restart rejected an expired credential. Its database contained only the SHA-256 digest, and PostgreSQL revocation and expiry tests passed. No running service was replaced and no original-client reconnect was observed. Launcher self-update candidate (2026-10-27): 15 focused version, allowlist and transactional installer checks passed. A disposable signed loopback service rejected a corrupted blob and completed a real process handoff, executable replacement and restart while preserving synthetic settings and game files. Three publisher checks passed. This test uses a fixture signing key and test process; no published 0.2.5 installer, production channel or actual player upgrade is established. Hosted deployment (2026-10-27): reconnect-only source was built on the deployed 0.2.4 baseline. Native HTTP smoke, 29 focused auth tests, three admin regressions and isolated PostgreSQL restart, expiry and revocation tests passed. A restored production backup accepted the additive migration, and a separate hosted candidate passed before switching. The new binary, schema 32, listeners, health and auth options were verified after deployment. Original-client restart acceptance remains pending. Existing-game adoption (2026-10-27): the Release launcher built and a fresh isolated profile selected the installed Steam game. Thirty-two focused launcher, discovery and patch tests passed, including existing-file reuse, preserved unlisted files, adoption failure and rollback. An actual Steam installation was then updated in place and the launcher reported successful verification of signed game release 0.2.0; no original-client trial is claimed. Repeated-scan repair (2026-10-27): 33 focused launcher and updater cases passed, including cross-realm reuse, changed file sets and rollback conflicts. Against the installed Steam game, local, live and local update checks each used the installed-metadata path in 0.11, 1.22 and 0.11 seconds, and a reopened launcher reported the release current. No new original-client gameplay trial is claimed. Credential Manager and login UX (2026-10-27): 41 focused C++ tests passed, including migration, separate origins, sign-out, storage failure and synthetic Discord callback and linking. A local saved login migrated and restored in the reopened launcher. An isolated live-realm launcher displayed the complete signed-out dialog and an enabled Discord button; no new live Discord authorization or gameplay trial was completed. Project Chronicles 0.2.5 integration (2026-10-27): reviewed auth revocation/world-admission barrier, guild-housing reconciliation and raised connection bounds integrated into one candidate. Release build; full CTest 1,536 registered with 1,421 passed, 114 environment-gated skips and one launcher saved-login case that failed only under parallel Credential Manager use (passes 3/3 serially; launcher tests now take a CTest resource lock). Disposable PostgreSQL: main persistence suite including the housing restart-repair regression, reconnect across a real restart, Discord identity and registration all passed. Synthetic and disposable-database evidence only; no original-client observation and no load test. Historical unified-launcher candidate (2026-10-27): local source/build and focused selection checks were recorded in docs/launcher-release.md; published 0.2.4 artifacts were unchanged and no original-client trial was claimed. The candidate was superseded by the published player/operator profiles during this merge. Source layout move (phase 1a of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-modular-emulator-architecture-design.md): every src/ file moved into its module folder listed in tools/source_layout.json; only includes, src/CMakeLists.txt source paths and src/ path references changed. No packet, persistence or gameplay behavior changed. Checks: Release build, the full CTest run with the same test names and results as before the move (including the registered Python smoke tests), and tools/test_move_sources.py. Build configuration (phases 0 and 1a of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-modular-emulator-architecture-design.md): CMakeLists.txt and src/CMakeLists.txt changed only in build scheduling (Ninja Multi-Config; /MP and /MP2 removed), per-target precompiled headers of standard, nlohmann/json, spdlog and GoogleTest headers, and the tools.module_includes CTest registration. No runtime, packet, persistence or gameplay behavior changed. Checks: Release build, the full CTest run with unchanged test names (1567 registered, 1449 passed, 118 environment-gated skips, 0 failed), and tools.module_includes. Persistence split (phase 1b-1): Discord AuthService methods, company and friend store implementations moved out of persistence files into auth and their features; CompanyRecord and the market state constants moved down into persistence headers. Definitions moved verbatim; no packet, SQL, persistence or gameplay behavior changed. Checks: Release build, full CTest with unchanged test names and no failures, tools.module_includes. Phase 1b-1 review fixes: comment and documentation paths corrected after the persistence split, include blocks re-sorted, and progress_packets.hpp includes nlohmann/json directly. No behavior change. Checks: Release build, full CTest (1568 tests, 0 failures), tools.module_includes. Module build helpers (phase 1b-2): cmake/ChroniclesModules.cmake adds per-module library and test helpers; /bigobj is applied to every MSVC C++ target instead of per target. No runtime behavior change. Checks: Release build, full CTest with unchanged test names and no failures, tools.module_includes. Portal storage module (phase 1b-2): portal_store and its tests moved from services/portal to services/portal_storage so the launcher's portal content module needs no PostgreSQL. The chronicles-portal-storage library, the chronicles-portal-tests program and its CTest names are unchanged; only include paths, src/CMakeLists.txt source paths, the tools/source_layout.json module list and its declared same-layer edge changed. No packet, persistence or gameplay behavior changed. Checks: Release build, full CTest (1568 tests, 0 failures), tools.module_includes. Launcher portal link retarget (phase 1b-2 Task 5): chronicles-launcher-core links chronicles-services-portal, the module library that now builds services/portal/portal_content.cpp, in place of the removed chronicles-portal-content; the portal headers, the launcher's other libraries and its package contents are unchanged. Checks: Release build, full CTest (1568 tests, 0 failures), release package file list identical to the phase 0 baseline. PostgreSQL reconnect tool (phase 1b-2): tools/test_reconnect_postgres.py now runs the NativeAuthPostgres filter through tools/gtest_programs.run_filtered across the per-module test programs; native_auth_tests.cpp is compiled into the roster and auth-flow programs (unprefixed and AuthFlow. CTest names), so the filter expects two passing runs. Verified on a disposable cluster: reconnect across a real server restart passed. Test split (phase 1b-2): these suites moved verbatim from the aggregated src/testing/tests.cpp when one test program per module replaced the chronicles-tests executable; suite and case names are unchanged. Checks: Release build and the full CTest run keep the same 1568 registered names with zero failures; tools.module_includes passes. Repository interfaces (phase 2): the Store interface was split verbatim into AccountRepository, CharacterRepository, CharacterStateRepository, MarketRepository, MailRepository, RankingRepository, HotKeyRepository and FogRepository headers under src/persistence, with their record types; Store now inherits all eight and MemoryStore/PostgresStore are unchanged. No packet, SQL, persistence or gameplay behavior changed. Checks: Release build, full CTest with the 1568 reference names plus Storage.StoreImplementsEveryRepository and zero failures, tools.module_includes. Refactor: the monolithic MemoryStore was split into MemoryAccountRepository, MemoryCharacterRepository and MemoryCharacterStateRepository over one shared MemoryDatabase; method bodies and validation moved verbatim, one database mutex still guards every table, and delete_character ordering (market-escrow veto, then fog and recipient-mail erasure) is preserved through the registered deletion hook. MemoryStore forwards all 36 repository methods and keeps the feature tables and behavior unchanged; ctest --preset release passes 1571/1571. Refactor: the monolithic PostgresStore was split into PostgresAccountRepository, PostgresCharacterRepository and PostgresCharacterStateRepository (src/persistence/postgres_repositories.hpp); method bodies, SQL text, revision guards and the character-row-first locking order moved verbatim, and migrate_postgres keeps advisory lock 7342091001. PostgresStore forwards all 36 repository methods and keeps its 15 feature methods unchanged; Release ctest passes 1572/1572 and both disposable-cluster PostgreSQL tools pass. Refactor: AuthService and server/account_main wiring now use the narrow AccountRepository, CharacterRepository and CharacterStateRepository interfaces (src/persistence/character_repositories.hpp) instead of Store; the shared_ptr<Store> constructor remains as a delegating view until Store is removed. Session, ownership, admission, revocation and roster behavior are unchanged. Checks: Release build, full CTest (1573 tests including the new AuthTest.CharacterOwnerFollowsSelection, 0 failures), tools.module_includes, and the disposable-cluster PostgreSQL and reconnect tools. Refactor: the world-session GM map reveal now calls the fog feature's reveal_world_map through the world's fog store instead of AuthService; the GM-only check, catalog merge and GM replies are unchanged. Refactor: AdminServices now carries CharacterRepositories plus a shared MailRepository pointer instead of shared_ptr<Store>; every console account, character, progress and mail call goes to the same implementation through its repository unchanged. Checks: full CTest (1573, 0 failures) and the disposable-cluster PostgreSQL and reconnect tools. Refactor: the server builds one repository set (apps/repositories.cpp) over a single memory or PostgreSQL store and hands each service only the members it uses; WorldListener::set_repositories replaces set_mail_store and WorldState::repositories replaces mail_store - each session path uses its own repository member with the same unset-store refusal behavior, and startup order and messages are unchanged. Checks: full CTest (1573, 0 failures), the mail and market smoke tools, and the disposable-cluster PostgreSQL and reconnect tools. Refactor: Store drops the HotKeyRepository and FogRepository bases and the facades drop the four methods and the two feature tables; create_repositories builds MemoryHotKeyRepository and MemoryFogRepository over the store's shared database (PostgreSQL builds the connection-string repositories), so one shared database and identical startup order are preserved. Checks: Release build, full CTest (1575, 0 failures), tools.module_includes, and the disposable-cluster PostgreSQL, reconnect and fog smoke tools. Refactor: Store drops the MarketRepository and RankingRepository bases and the facades drop the seven methods and the three feature tables; create_repositories builds MemoryMarketRepository and MemoryRankingRepository over the store's shared database (PostgreSQL builds the connection-string repositories), so one shared database, the escrow veto on character deletion and identical startup order are preserved. Checks: Release build, full CTest (1576, 0 failures), tools.module_includes, and the disposable-cluster PostgreSQL, reconnect and market smoke tools. Storage split (phase 2): Store now inherits only AccountRepository, CharacterRepository and CharacterStateRepository; MemoryStore and PostgresStore dropped the four mail methods and the last feature table, and MemoryStore registers no deletion hook because the recipient-mail erase moved into MemoryMailRepository's own hook on the shared database. create_repositories builds the mail repository over the shared MemoryDatabase in memory mode and over the shared connection string in postgres mode; MailRest, tutorial-completion delivery, WorldRepositories.mail and AdminServices.mail take the narrow interface. No behavior change. Checks: Release build, full CTest, the mail and market smoke tools, the disposable PostgreSQL and reconnect runs, tools.module_includes. Tests build repositories instead of the Store facades: MemoryRepositories over a shared MemoryDatabase (accounts member replaceable by the fault-injecting repository) and make_postgres_character_repositories(url); assertions, suites and test names unchanged (ctest 1577/1577). The Store, MemoryStore and PostgresStore facades, character_repositories_of, the Store AuthService constructor and persistence/storage.hpp are deleted; callers use the account, character and character-state repositories over one shared MemoryDatabase or one PostgreSQL connection string, and tests use MemoryRepositories/make_postgres_character_repositories. Method bodies, SQL text, revision guards and locking order unchanged; assertions, suites and test names unchanged. Checks: Release build, full CTest, mail/market/fog smoke tools, disposable-cluster PostgreSQL, reconnect and Discord runs, tools.module_includes. Follow-up hardening preserves every gameplay, packet, persistence and ordering contract: the world request IDs shared by the frame pipeline, native world and owning features are defined once in world/core/world_request_opcodes.hpp with unchanged values, frame-pipeline route sets for loot, revival, housing, chat, companion/trade, item use, company, equipment, progression, merchant, processing, gathering, utility bag and private combat are asserted across the whole 16-bit opcode range, the full pipeline step order is pinned by literal traces, native world statically ties its credential slice sizes to the transport constants, and party, gathering and guild report once (spdlog error) when a non-empty update is dropped because no delivery is installed. Checked by the default Release suite (0 failures) and the native world smoke; no feature status or packet override changes. Project branding and local-default configuration (2026-11-02): the applications, installer, resource metadata, scripts and documentation now use Project Chronicles; the distributed catalog has no built-in hosted destination or signing key. Credential-store, process-lease and Discord first-login lock namespaces are separate from older builds. Database schemas, numeric opcodes, gameplay feature names and recovered payload fields are unchanged. Historical validation wording is normalized to the current project name and does not establish a new release or hosted acceptance. See docs/project-configuration.md. Local validation results are recorded there. Database packaging consolidation: isolated PostgreSQL 16 schema-only dumps before and after consolidation matched exactly (57 tables, 40 foreign keys, 23 additional indexes). Fresh/repeated installer runs, account preservation, quoted password authentication, wrong-password rejection, and non-destructive rejection of older/unrelated schemas passed. Both existing PostgreSQL death/revival/reconnect and shared-repository tests passed. No live database was changed and no original-client trial was performed. Autonomous login/game split: the 69-test standalone authentication suite passed including isolated PostgreSQL credential durability. Real two-process checks with the normal database role covered registration, launcher login/grant, native realm entry returning the game front address, character creation/selection, both TLS admission credentials, cross-format ticket replay rejection, private encrypted replies/replay rejection, public/private listener isolation, login outage and restart. These are synthetic service/transport checks and do not establish original-client gameplay compatibility. Fresh split-service installation trial (2026-11-03): the researched compatible private client accepted the corrected login fingerprint, entered tutorial map 8000 through separate login/game processes and displayed health/stamina after the private catalog and tutorial/combat profile were loaded. Weapon actions (CMS 1000000 and 1101), root-motion updates and continued keepalives were observed; the guarded local helper restored both temporary changes. Missing data had allowed map rendering with incomplete stats/actions. This bounded local trial does not establish full tutorial, damage/recovery, all skills, hosted or stock-client compatibility. See docs/fresh-install-validation-20261103.md.

**Dependencies:** Authenticated ownership, authoritative state and bounded execution.

**Packet inventory** — counts follow capture keys T / P1 / P2 / A1 / M1 / W1 / R1. Zero means absent from these world logs, not impossible or unsupported by the game.

## Character lobby and identity

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Front WebSocket character list/create/select/delete and character-name lookup.

**Current implementation**

- List, create and select persist ownership, slots, class, customization and starter equipment.
- Selection establishes authenticated chat identity and a one-use world handoff.
- When the realm restricts character creation, WorldEnterRes grants allow_char_create=false and CharCreateReq returns CharCreationRestricted.
- Operator console character management for offline characters: list/search by character or account, details with items, stackables, currency, quests and saved/live position, and edits of level/EXP, gold/Hersander tokens, saved position, name (lobby name rule, unique per world ignoring case) and deletion (typed-name confirmation; owned rows cascade). Edits to a character with a live world session are refused.
- CharDeletePreCheckReq reports name and level for the caller's own characters only, with guild-master and guild-housing block reasons and CharDeleteGuildMember for plain guild members. CharDeleteReq checks ownership, the typed name and those blockers, then refuses with CharDeleteInvalid without removing data; CharDeleteCancelReq and CharDeleteImmediateReq report CharDeleteNotPending.
- LookupCharIdByNameReq resolves any character of the entered realm by exact, case-sensitive name (3-16 bytes) through the store's character_summary_by_name and returns its ID; unknown names return InvalidChar and out-of-range names BadRequest.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Pending deletion (grace period, delete_scheduled_epochtime, CharDeleteAlreadyPending) is not modeled, so the client's CharDeleteReq always refuses and cancel/immediate never find a pending deletion. Marketplace blockers are not reported by the precheck.
- All class enums can be represented; playable world/bootstrap support is narrower.
- Console deletion is an operator action without the official pending-deletion period; the client's own CharDeleteReq flow remains unimplemented.

## World connection, clock and session lifecycle

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

TLS negotiation, initial credential, world entry/exit, clock, ping and framing.

**Current implementation**

- Bounded TLS framing, sequence validation, entry/exit and ping/clock responses exist.
- The local world-entry helper has explicit build guards; standard certificate acceptance remains separate.
- Server-generated monotonic wire ticks use native nanoseconds while internal deadlines remain in 100 ns units; epoch timestamps and client-forwarded ticks retain their existing units.
- Operator console live-player view: every world connection with account/character, GM flag, live position, peer address and connected time. An operator kick (one connection, or every connection of a banned/signed-out account) runs the normal close path, which saves the position and releases the population lease.
- Launcher desktop lifecycle: detecting a running client hides the launcher in the Windows notification area; the transition to no matching clients restores its window and previous normal/maximized size. Manual tray restore remains visible during play. The executable, window, taskbar and tray use an embedded multi-resolution gold Project Chronicles compass icon.
- Launcher process detection requires the configured executable path and a live process handle; exited processes with retained handles are excluded. The controller publishes client status before optional scans, and bridge requests have a 30-second response limit.
- Distribution profiles use the bundled Windows user-mode memory library and a managed game destination. Player Settings expose game-folder and file-update controls; native actions reject hidden developer settings. Account sign-in has no development-account prefill. Release packaging stages an explicit player-file allowlist.
- An adjacent launcher-player-ui.flag previews the restricted player Settings on an existing local launcher without changing its server, memory backend, game launch target or account session. This marker is a UI preview, not a distribution profile.
- The guarded local world-entry helper can use ordinary Windows user-mode process access for the researched client build. It verifies code bytes and process identity before temporary startup-gate and TLS-callback changes, then restores them after the connection. The local launcher passes its selected backend to the helper.
- Opening the launcher while a matching game is already running keeps the launcher window visible, including when a late status update first detects it. Only a game launch requested in that launcher window moves it to the tray.
- The hosted world helper matches the selected game-owned TCP peer and requires the researched executable SHA-256, live code signatures, SSL_VERIFY_PEER, and exactly one native X509 expected hostname matching the selected world DNS name. It applies both the startup gate and OpenSSL default verification callback, retaining chain and hostname checks, then restores both fields with readback. Missing identity or unsupported verification flags fail closed. The local development path retains its existing behavior. A failed attempt is not retried for that client process.
- The player and operator entrypoints share one launcher core and both allow the local server by default. Operator-supplied catalogs provide additional endpoints and signing keys; selection persists and resets account context on switching. Historical production-only catalogs are not included.
- Steam library and app-manifest discovery selects an existing game for in-place signed-file verification and updates. A native folder picker supports manual changes. Managed installs track rollback protection separately per service origin.
- Installer and portable packages include the user-mode world helper, app-local C++ runtimes, WebView2 loader, pinned Microsoft Evergreen bootstrapper and dependency notices. Missing WebView2 is prepared per user before GUI startup; the signed game release installs compatibility DLLs and corresponding source automatically.
- The admin console selects local token-file access or live SSH with a pinned host and existing operator key. The live admin token stays on the server and its HTTP API remains loopback-only. Chronicles-owned processes include role icons and 0.2.0 version resources.
- Public launcher communication literals use Apache-licensed xorstr_ with an SSE2 baseline. This is binary string obfuscation, not credential secrecy; private signing keys, SSH keys and account credentials are excluded from player artifacts.
- Launcher 0.2.1 publishes startup state only after the trusted WebView listener is ready, replays startup errors, bundles matching build profiles, and makes catalog selection independent of optional network requests. Offline realms skip account/content/update polling; three consecutive failed health checks report a connection failure, cleared on realm change or recovery.
- Update cancellation is observed during signed-release inspection and each 64 KiB file-hash read, including reuse verification. The UI acknowledges cancellation immediately and reports the current verification file. Synchronous network waits are bounded; final installation retains transactional completion and recovery.
- For a previously verified signed game-file set, normal launcher startup and Play check the completed installation marker, file presence, sizes and launch-critical compatibility hashes without rereading all game content, including across realms with the same files. Explicit Verify / repair performs full SHA-256 checks, including same-size local modifications. Changed file sets, missing files and pending transactions still require inspection; rollback history remains per service origin. Verification and network downloading have distinct UI headings; manual cancellation consumes the scheduled startup check.
- Latency correction (2026-10-27): world sockets set TCP_NODELAY so Pong and other small frames are not held behind earlier unacknowledged frames, and the four per-frame transport traces (awaiting, frame read, write, written) moved from info to debug. Hosted evidence before the change: about 0.9 CPU core for one player, 40-175 ms between reading a client frame and finishing it (a Ping took 114 ms), and about 130 info log lines per second.
- Ping, clock and movement requests skip authored-patrol registry synchronization; requests that can target an NPC still synchronize before range checks. Framing, response opcodes and the shared patrol timeline are preserved.
- World admission is ordered against reselection and account revocation: after entry preparation the world worker publishes the operator-visible identity and the stream executor claims the account's current character selection once. The claim fails after a newer selection, ticket expiry (default 60 s) or revocation, and the connection closes without an entry frame. A failed entry preparation on the native token path closes instead of admitting.
- Default connection bounds were raised for the 500-player realm target: 512 world sockets (--max-world-connections), 1280 HTTP/WebSocket connections and 1024 front chat registrations. These are resource bounds, not measured capacity.
- Saved-death reconnect repair: bootstrap and later observer nubs carry the authoritative Demise/Idle state. After the first StartPlayingReq of a loaded map, a saved-dead character receives Demise then DeathNoti once, without replaying damage, durability loss, rewards or a death transaction. Completed death/revival commits refresh later observer life snapshots. See docs/dead-reconnect.md; original-client acceptance is pending.
- Gameplay timer backpressure repair (2026-10-29): one tick can be queued or running per session until its I/O completion. Generation checks reject canceled waits whose success callback was already ready. Slow frames cannot create parallel overdue timer chains; map-loading early returns release the gate. Optional debug logs identify processing steps exceeding 100 ms using opcode, static step name and duration only.
- NetworkDelay (20004) reports are bounded (at most 60 s) and recorded in the client_reported_round_trip_us histogram; the protocol has no reply.
- Operator SSH proxy hardening (2026-10-30): tools/admin_remote_proxy.ps1 reads its request with a 30 s deadline from the raw input stream and exits when it expires. Abandoned operator requests used to leave the proxy blocked forever; 373 such PowerShell processes exhausted the live host's memory and stopped PostgreSQL on 2026-10-30. The running copies were stopped, PostgreSQL restarted and the fixed proxy deployed with hash verification.
- Re-entry admission wait (2026-11-02): a world entry whose character is still admitted to its closing previous session keeps its credential and retries the same ticket every 100 ms instead of being closed. NativeWorldListener::set_entry_admission_wait bounds the wait; the hosted server sets 10 s, while listeners without that call (embedded and test servers) refuse at once as before. The wait and the admission after it are logged.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- The official credential prefix and stock certificate policy are not fully reproduced.
- Captured monotonic tick units differ from the current emulator clock; all timing paths need a coordinated correction.
- Two-client movement interpolation and original-client clock acceptance remain unverified.
- Server teardown does not close or drain active sessions before the io_context is destroyed; only the declaration order (worker pool destroyed last) was fixed in a6dde5e6. An idle-server graceful shutdown exits normally in the author and independent smoke runs, but shutdown with open world connections or pending session teardown is untested and a full connection drain is backlog.
- A kicked client receives only a closed socket; no recovered disconnect-reason packet is sent and the original client's reaction is unobserved. In-game time of day is not controlled: PS2C_WorldGameTimeNoti is a debug schema with no captures or established units, so the console shows only the server clock.
- Launcher tray restoration follows the controller's polled client.running state, including all matching clients in the configured game directory. A live process with no playable game window still counts as running. No corrected-launcher original-game exit trial is claimed; desktop lifecycle and icon checks do not establish protocol compatibility.
- The guarded helper has original-client loopback and hosted world-entry observations on the researched build. This does not establish other game builds, extended hosted gameplay, reconnect behavior or multi-player capacity. Developer builds retain the legacy PlaySharp bridge; player packages include no bridge executable, MCP service or driver.
- Operator disconnect remains an asynchronous close; packets already queued on an admitted session may still be processed. Lobby logout, a new login or session rotation during world entry do not cancel an in-flight admission. No representative 500-player load test has been run against the raised connection bounds.
- A waiting re-entry cannot detect a client that gave up; such a connection may still be admitted and then closed normally. The stock client's world-entry response timeout and the cause of its repeated TLS handshake failures after a refused entry are not established; the wait avoids the refusal rather than repairing the client state.

**Evidence and verification**

Synthetic TimeSync/Pong and combat/tutorial TLS checks cover server-generated nanosecond wire ticks; official capture deltas support the wire unit. Original-client clock and gameplay compatibility remain unverified. Teardown ordering: the production worker pool is now declared before the io_context (a6dde5e6); the build-and-test review of that head is described under combat. Isolated graceful-shutdown smoke of the real server on throwaway ports 18090/18091 and a disposable PostgreSQL 55433; the live service was never signalled. Author results (builder, evidence under out/agent-team-reports/shutdown-gate-20261025/): with a logged Ctrl+C helper that attaches to the server console, the candidate a6dde5e6 binary (SHA-256 CAC0359D) exited with code 0 in 3 of 3 runs, a normal return from main after the signal (server.cpp registers an asio signal_set for SIGINT and SIGTERM), and the baseline 46839f1 binary (SHA-256 6549E312) did the same in 3 of 3 runs; /health and /launcher/v1/content answered 200 and all test listeners were freed. Independent reviewer results (reviewer agent, own run of the same candidate binary, evidence under out/agent-team-reports/reviewer-shutdown-20261025/run/): exit code 0 in 3 of 3 runs through the Ctrl+C helper, /health and /launcher/v1/content 200, ports freed, live service untouched and no crash. Earlier candidate runs that did not exit used an unlogged inline helper and are attributed to harness signal delivery, consistent with the same-helper parity of candidate and baseline; the old scripts were not diffed, so this is not proven. Scope limit for all runs: idle server only, no client connected, no world TLS connection, no pending gameplay-tick or session teardown exercised, no connection drain.
