Canonical clean/source/header/shared-header timings are 283.9/15.7/22.7/211.4s, on 24 logical CPUs with 26 default jobs and private compilation paused; observed CPU load is 54% before and 35% after. This single loaded run does not establish the 3x clean-build target. All 599 source contents stay identical, timestamps restore and prior logs are preserved. Initial environment-harness and outer-wrapper errors remain recorded separately from successful actual gates. Core presence, neutral observer/lifetime composition, named capabilities/WorldState, two final owner-policy moves and focused GM ports remain explicit Phase 5 work. No gameplay, packet/status, schema or new original-client acceptance change. See docs/modular-migration-phase-4.md and the Phase 5 plan. Phase 5 Core presence and lower fixtures: Core owns the unchanged presence/projection/unit-ID bodies and lower memory fixtures; its actual test link uses only lower archives. ALL passes; 404 of 409 selected checks pass with five old PG skips, all Core78 and World39/Market7 pass. All 1943 names/old bodies remain with two NPC-to-Core identity moves. Full contract and evidence: docs/modular-migration-phase-5.md. Phase 5 neutral event composition: thirteen ordered observers use five required/eight optional slots; generic GM sinks are removed. Handshake, bus, 25 owners and pipeline have explicit inverse teardown; borrowed payloads and original owned caches remain. Earlier allocation/validation precedence is disclosed. ALL passes; 374 of 377 checks pass with three old PG skips, all51 regressions and World39/Market7 pass. 1947 names/old bodies remain. Full evidence: docs/modular-migration-phase-5.md. Phase 5 named capabilities and State repository closure: Project Chronicles and Gathering keep their original codec locks, peer retention, catches and post-unlock delivery through named operations. Gathering callback conversion/destruction timing and removed duplicate repository use counts are explicit limits. Startup DTO/set order and lifecycle bodies remain. ALL passes; 354 of 356 checks pass with two old PG skips, all 29 owner cases and rebuilt World39/Market7 pass; 1947 names/bodies stay exact. No gameplay/status/schema change. Full contract/evidence: docs/modular-migration-phase-5.md. Phase 5 final owner policies and cleanup: Final Expression/GM policy routing, public compatibility and scoped cleanup preserve locks, lifetime and old bodies. ALL passes; 302 of 303 checks pass with one old PG skip, all three new seams and World39/Market7 pass. 1950 names remain unique. Focused GM and final gates remain. See docs/modular-migration-phase-5.md. Phase 5 focused GM capabilities: Production directly binds eight focused references; no broad context or temporary-bundle reference is retained. Constructors only bind references; lifecycle/bus order stays exact. ALL and real regression/native checks pass; 1951 names remain unique. Final style and full boundary gates remain. See docs/modular-migration-phase-5.md. Phase 5 final boundary: All 28 owners, 610 source files and 43 contracts verified. The 1,951 names preserve Phase 4's 1,943 plus eight, all 116 Native/16 graduation bodies and Core78. Default: 1,832 passes, 119 skips, zero failures; current fixtures: 64 passes. Seven saved failures reproduce; 46 optional limits remain. Fresh final-binary replay and disposable Fog pass. Feature-source build: 12s; clean: 260.4s, missing the 3x speedup target. Source migration complete; client/implementation limits unchanged. See docs/modular-migration-phase-5.md. Follow-up hardening preserves every gameplay, packet, persistence and ordering contract: the world request IDs shared by the frame pipeline, native world and owning features are defined once in world/core/world_request_opcodes.hpp with unchanged values, frame-pipeline route sets for loot, revival, housing, chat, companion/trade, item use, company, equipment, progression, merchant, processing, gathering, utility bag and private combat are asserted across the whole 16-bit opcode range, the full pipeline step order is pinned by literal traces, native world statically ties its credential slice sizes to the transport constants, and party, gathering and guild report once (spdlog error) when a non-empty update is dropped because no delivery is installed. Checked by the default Release suite (0 failures) and the native world smoke; no feature status or packet override changes. Review follow-up preserves every gameplay, packet, persistence and ordering contract: the frame pipeline now exposes its step names so tests pin every composed step in order and dispatch traces for each handler group, the GM and item-use request IDs join the shared request-ID header (private copies alias it), the log-capture test helper drops its logger on destruction, and party, gathering and guild document where their dropped-delivery methods may be called. Checked by the default Release suite (0 failures) and the native world smoke; no feature status or packet override changes. Session latency repair 2026-10-29: mounted movement/read-count, committed life, reentry and debug timing regressions pass; three real-catalog TLS companion scenarios pass. The original client exposed a growing pre-repair backlog after boarding; post-deployment driving acceptance remains pending. See docs/session-delay-repair-20261029.md. Original-client acceptance of session repair f44f51f: after deployment the player confirmed driving, dismounting, NPC interaction and character selection work. A 65-frame debug sample measured 0-181 ms movement processing, including two 180 ms durable position checkpoints; normal sampled movement took approximately 1-2 ms. No general capacity claim. See docs/session-delay-repair-20261029.md. Received request batch 2026-10-29 (integrated on the accepted session repair f44f51f): default Release suite 2,061 cases, 0 failures, 127 environment-gated skips; with the real catalog and regenerated profiles 1,991 executed with one pre-existing placement-data failure (trade-run test, also failing without this batch); isolated PostgreSQL migration, restart smoke and 12 repository cases passed; exporter tests passed. No original-client trial before deployment. See docs/received-packet-features-20261029.md. Metrics configuration (2026-11-02): --metrics now accepts the value 'true' that a backend config boolean expands to, so "metrics": true enables the loopback-only /internal/metrics endpoint for the hosted service. The 559 ms HUD RTT report has no established cause; see docs/live-issues-20261102.md. Refused re-entry (2026-11-02, docs/live-issues-20261102.md): the hosted log showed CharacterExitReq, a new selection 2.7 s later and 'Native world credential rejected' for the next connection 1 ms after TLS, followed by client-sent TLS handshake failures until the game restarted. Native TLS test NativeWorld.ReconnectWaitsForTheClosingSessionWhenTheListenerAllowsAWait pauses the closing session's position settlement, checks that the same-ticket reconnect is not admitted meanwhile, and receives the key-exchange answer after the release with the saved position intact. Auth.NativeKeyAndDevelopmentTokenShareSingleUseHandoff covers admission_busy for the token path. Existing busy-refusal tests keep the zero wait. Synthetic only; no original-client re-entry on the corrected server yet. Fresh split-service installation trial (2026-11-03): the researched compatible private client accepted the corrected login fingerprint, entered tutorial map 8000 through separate login/game processes and displayed health/stamina after the private catalog and tutorial/combat profile were loaded. Weapon actions (CMS 1000000 and 1101), root-motion updates and continued keepalives were observed; the guarded local helper restored both temporary changes. Missing data had allowed map rendering with incomplete stats/actions. This bounded local trial does not establish full tutorial, damage/recovery, all skills, hosted or stock-client compatibility. See docs/fresh-install-validation-20261103.md. Region recovery 2026-11-03: reconnects use authored public field bounds and child-to-parent relationships before configuring map-owned populations. User confirms the affected region works; all-region gameplay acceptance remains unverified.

**Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`PC2S_ForceAck`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_c2s.session.proto`. Fields: Empty protobuf body.
- **`PC2S_TimeSyncReq`** — Tutorial bootstrap or bounded generic presence/movement only; no general map/simulation authority. Schema file: `timesync_req.proto`. Fields: 1:try_count (int32); 2:try_ticks (sfixed64); 3:try_cycles64 (fixed64); 4:last_round_trip_nanoseconds (sfixed64)
- **`PC2S_CharExitReq`** — Current bounded session handler exists; see world TLS/credential compatibility limits. Schema file: `p_c2s.session.proto`. Fields: 1:logout (bool)
- **`PC2S_Ping`** — Current bounded session handler exists; see world TLS/credential compatibility limits. The latency refactor preserves the frame contract while skipping unrelated patrol synchronization and enabling TCP_NODELAY. Live 0.2.4 original-client HUD RTT was observed at 135 ms on tutorial map 8000 and 132 ms on public map 9012 with one player; sustained movement, casting and many-player acceptance remain pending. See docs/world-latency-release-20261027.md. Schema file: `p_c2s.session.proto`. Fields: 1:ping_cycles64 (fixed64); 2:tick (fixed64); 3:last_round_trip_nanoseconds (sfixed64)
- **`PC2S_NetworkDelay`** — Bounded client round trip (at most 60 s) recorded as telemetry; the protocol defines no reply. Schema file: `p_c2s.session.proto`. Fields: 1:client_round_trip_nanoseconds (sfixed64)
- **`PS2C_TimeSyncRes`** — Tutorial bootstrap or bounded generic presence/movement only; no general map/simulation authority. Schema file: `timesync_res.proto`. Fields: 1:try_count (int32); 2:ticks (sfixed64); 3:timestamp (sfixed64); 4:try_ticks (sfixed64); 5:try_cycles64 (fixed64); 6:last_round_trip_nanoseconds (sfixed64)
- **`PS2C_Pong`** — Current bounded session handler exists; see world TLS/credential compatibility limits. The latency refactor preserves the frame contract while skipping unrelated patrol synchronization and enabling TCP_NODELAY. Live 0.2.4 original-client HUD RTT was observed at 135 ms on tutorial map 8000 and 132 ms on public map 9012 with one player; sustained movement, casting and many-player acceptance remain pending. See docs/world-latency-release-20261027.md. Schema file: `p_s2c.session.proto`. Fields: 1:ping_cycles64 (fixed64); 2:server_send_tick (fixed64); 3:timestamp (sfixed64); 4:last_round_trip_nanoseconds (sfixed64)
- **`PS2C_CharEntryRes`** — Current bounded session handler exists; see world TLS/credential compatibility limits. Schema file: `p_s2c.session.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode)
- **`PS2C_CharExitRes`** — Current bounded session handler exists; see world TLS/credential compatibility limits. Schema file: `p_s2c.session.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode)

## Movement, map travel, gliding and teleportation

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

World map handoff, ordinary/root movement, gliding, channels, teleport, escape and home travel.

**Current implementation**

- Map-8000 initial load/start-playing, movement checkpoints and basic nearby movement relay exist.
- Server-owned tutorial cutscene handoffs connect map 8000 -> 10117 -> the hosted overworld on the same TLS connection. Gameplay timers queued before a map change defer while MapLoadCompleteReq has not restored the world position; packet processing re-arms current service deadlines after loading.
- Server-side NPC MoveNoti (177) emission for tutorial monster pursuit: Run with pred_milli/pred_pos at a Candidate cadence, Stop at arrival, leash/home return and the monster's own attack (monster death mid-route untested); synthetic and native-socket tested, original-client following NOT observed.
- Player fall impacts (docs/fall-damage.md): accepted Falling -> Normal/Crouching movement tracks ledge/apex Z and applies one server-calculated maximum-HP-scaled damage event. Candidate safe height is catalog FallHeightSafe * 10 mm (default 10 m); the explicit local curve costs 5% maximum HP per excess meter and is lethal at safe height + 20 m. Swimming/gliding/climbing/flying/parkour/root motion, ordinary map changes, completed teleports and revival reset fall tracking; natural region handoffs preserve existing fall state. Tutorial, followup and supported shared-map sessions with verified stats/combat data share vitals, durable lethal death/durability and in-place revival.
- CANDIDATE player escape (docs/player-escape.md): a non-trading PC2S_EscapeReq inside EscapeCandidateMaxDistance (500 cm = 5,000 mm) of the server position receives PS2C_TeleportReq to the client navmesh candidate and the 300 s hidden cooldown status 50030003. The TeleportStartReq echoing that tick toggles Invincible attribute 2 to 1; the completion adds/removes 50030002, resets the attribute and makes the destination the authoritative (saved) position. A session timer removes 50030003 at expiry. Dead, busy, riding, cooling-down, pending, missing-candidate and too-far requests are refused without frames.
- Movement stamina and swimming/diving (docs/movement-vitals.md): accepted ground Sprint and Swimming movement share combat stat 72. Catalog defaults consume 3 SP per 600 ms for sprint, 10 SP per second for swimming and 20 for swim sprint; ground sprint requires 50 SP. Per-session server deadlines continue without movement packets; repeated packets and activity toggles cannot reset fractional cost. Refused/exhausted sprints emit SprintEndNoti once. SurfaceIdle is resting afloat. SW_Dive enters sticky underwater state until SurfaceIdle or leaving Swimming; local drowning removes 5% maximum HP each second, with Drowned origin 16, and stops at accepted surfacing. Natural stamina/health recovery is gated during exertion/submersion; resting resumes the existing regen cadence. Tutorial, follow-up and supported shared-map sessions use the same timers and persisted lethal death/revival path.
- NPC locomotion repair (2026-10-26): ordinary pursuit uses Run/Stop MoveNoti 177 with prediction and increasing ns ticks, never orphan skill-only 64/106. GM-created private encounters use complete catalog locomotion on tutorial and open-world maps, face their route, stop before casting and settle position before return/cast interruption. The generator exports 71 locomotion blocks, including passive zero-cone rows. Private GM kills do not count as authored tutorial quest kills; despawn cancels owned effects and releases actor state. Ambient public/shared-world monster authority, navmesh routing and candidate original-client acceptance remain open. See docs/npc-locomotion-fix-20261026.md.
- Zone boundary repair (2026-10-26): PC2S_ZoneChannelMoveReq now resolves unique active authored channelSession boxes with spawn zero between ungated ArcheWorld maps. It validates the current/reported positions, retains the authoritative pose, completes the existing in-connection map lifecycle, clears old presence/population and supports persisted channel reconnect. Natural travel retains player HP/SP/status/cooldown state; map identity no longer depends on optional NPC population. See docs/zone-channel-travel.md.
- Local all-zone exploration (2026-10-26): the chronicles-zone-unlock helper uses ordinary Windows OpenProcess/ReadProcessMemory/WriteProcessMemory to enable every researched Zone row's activation and derived public-map eligibility gates. It preserves both original bytes per process, verifies code and row identity, reads back every write, rolls back failures and clears only the transient inactive-zone anchor. Private-copy launches can opt in; the managed player launcher now invokes it for the newly launched client and ships the helper in its package. No PlaySharp backend, quest grant or game-file patch is involved. 2026-10-27 timing fix: a 0.2.5 launch failed with 'Invalid zone catalog pointer' because the launcher waited only 20 s while the client builds its catalog after loading; the launcher now starts the helper in the background and the helper retries up to 1800 s, exiting early if the client closes (Release build only; fresh-client movement not yet observed). That helper reported success yet the wall persisted, so the same unlock now also runs as a re-applying thread inside the patched Steam compatibility library (launcher/src/zone_unlock_inproc.cpp); it needs a signed game release to ship and is unobserved in the original client. 2026-10-27: the in-process unlock was confirmed by the user in the original client (invisible wall no longer blocks movement) and shipped in signed game catalog 0.2.6 sequence 3; launcher 0.2.6 no longer starts the helper at Play. 2026-10-28: the wall returned; live kernel inspection found the researched zone-table buffer holding JSON text fragments in later rows (identical bytes across two client processes), so the thread's fail-closed row validation rejected every pass while early rows stayed unlocked. The thread now runs the movement clears even when the catalog pass fails, and additionally clears a stale pending zone-channel transition (map-move manager +568..570) after it stayed set for 20 s. The real XIGNCODE module (handle stripping) was replaced by the signed 10 KB shim at X5/Binaries/Win64/XIGNCODE/x3_x64.xem in catalog 0.2.7 sequence 4; the stale-transition clear shipped in sequence 5 (steam_api64.dll SHA-256 4985e9d4d129bbcd168bc6e05b915b2ac66378e8bc01a6fbf88219bb71b472ba). The operator confirmed live that clearing the pending bytes released movement at a refused map 9021 crossing. See docs/local-zone-unlock.md.
- 2026-10-29 regional crossing repair: optional ArcheWorld-zone-channels.json exports 11 ungated public fields and 15,976 non-overlapping occupied 5100-cm cells. Unique eligible trigger boxes retain precedence; spatial-only crossings resolve from the bounded reported point and preserve authoritative pose/vitals/status/cooldowns through 175/20085/176/20086/183. Unresolved eligible idle requests receive that same-map lifecycle rather than silence. Routing loads independently of NPC populations. This is Candidate selection policy from static callers/catalog grids; no official 20090 capture or original-client UI acceptance.
- StartGlidingReq (20032) is owned by the combat player session: it is accepted only after a Falling or predicted Gliding movement report, with a finite pose within 5 m of the server position. Death, riding, the stun ailment, an active skill or interaction, a duplicate start and a grounded start answer StartGlidingFailNoti (180) with the server pose and clock. Success is silent; landing or a map reset ends the glide.
- Teleport region repair (2026-10-29): MapChannels::region_map_for maps an open-world GM destination (tp, tp_map with coordinates, relative moves, goto/summon) on main-world map 1, or on a public field whose own Map.area does not hold it, to the ungated zone field whose area does (nearest centre in overlaps), so the destination region's channel, NPCs and monsters load; instances keep their map. tp_map <id> without coordinates keeps the named public channel, but map 1 is always routed. Seamless ZoneChannelMoveReq crossings keep occupied-cell precedence and fall back to the authored region area outside every cell.
- Instances, dungeons and portals (2026-11-01, docs/instances-and-dungeons.md): the client reports entering a channelSession, channel or portal level-trigger volume with PC2S_LevelTriggerReq and waits for a server map move (static analysis: AAC_MapMove_LevelTriggerReq_BeginPendingAndSend starts the pending transition). tools/build_map_travel.py exports every world's travel volumes (ArcheWorld and the 15 MazeDungeons levels), the Map entrance/exit MapCondition rows, Portal rows, LevelTriggerVolume rules and MapMoveCutScene rows; world/features/travel evaluates the conditions (quest, item, adventure object, level, play record, party state, map enter/leave; CUSTOM: kinds the server does not track are trusted because the client checked them) and moves the character with MapMoveStartNoti.cut_scene_id from MapMoveCutScene. CUSTOM arrival: the character keeps its position when the destination's authored area contains it (every field dungeon entrance lies inside its dungeon area), else the dungeon level origin. A refused travel the client waits for gets a same-map handoff. ChannelTriggerEntryReq (map_id, 0 = parent) uses the same planner; scripted volumes play their server cutscenes; gated instances, dungeons and points of interest resume on reconnect (Map.retainOnDisconnect). Instance and dungeon copies (2026-11-01, world/core/instance_copies; CUSTOM policy): every Instance and Dungeon map has separate copies; a character in an established party enters its party's copy and a character without one its own, chosen when the map move starts or at login. A copy owns its monsters (WorldMobs) and its gathering and doodad node state; presence uses a synthetic negative map per copy, and PvP, party kill credit, loot sharing and companion visibility use the copy's keys, so players in other copies of the map see none of it. Same-map handoffs keep the copy; it ends when its last character leaves. Dungeon GoBoss/GoExit portal rows (11/12) get the arrival of the dungeon's own boss/exit doodad MapMove interaction (<prefix>01/<prefix>02, checked against the exit volume; Candidate): all 24 rows of 12 dungeons resolve and a volume naming one moves the character within the map. Every CutScene row is exported with its end point; when a shared-world server cutscene ends (CutSceneEndReq) the character moves there with MapMoveStartNoti: captured position, else the single doodad of the end point id placed on the end map (Candidate, 7 rows), else the arrival rule (CUSTOM); raid end maps and no-op end points do not move. Scripted volume doodad phases are recorded in the map or copy doodad state, sent to the character and the other players there, carried by later SectorUpdateNoti doodads, not repeated on re-entry, saved in WorldProgress.doodad_phases and restored (without overriding live state) when the character re-enters the map. Tests: InstanceCopies.*, MapTravel.*, MapTravelProfile.*, SharedCombatOwner.InstanceCopiesOwnTheirMonstersForEveryoneInside, GatheringFeature copy and volume-doodad tests, CompanionWorldTest.ARiderEnteringAnotherCopyTakesItsMountAlong, NativeWorld.InstanceVolumeEntersTheCaveAndChannelEntryLeavesIt, NativeWorld.SoloCharactersEnterSeparateCopiesOfTheCave, NativeWorld.EntranceDoorPhaseIsSavedAndReturnsWithTheMap, NativeWorld.AuthoredInstanceMonsterPopulationsArePrivatePerCharacter, NativeWorld.DungeonMonsterPopulationsArePrivatePerSoloCharacter and tools/test_build_map_travel.py.
- Cliffs of Madness entrance: the authored pirate-hideout gate requires Missing Husband and a solo player or party leader, plays captured cutscene 1565, and moves to map 30104 after the matching cutscene end. The destination is the fixed entrance observed in the official P2 capture. Gate and TLS handoff have synthetic coverage; original-client acceptance is not observed.
- Player !unstuck command (candidate): the authenticated world session selects a catalog-backed Nui idol or flame on the current map, or its parent if an instance has no local shrine. Both same-map and parent-map recovery use the map-move lifecycle so destination visibility is refreshed. The command refuses while dead, riding, busy, trading, in housing or during a pending teleport/cutscene, and has a five-minute session-local cooldown. TLS fixture checks cover same-map reload, cooldown and instance exit.
- Swimming announces the captured continuous SP flow and suspends client regeneration; server spending remains authoritative. Surfacing stops the flow. Original-client acceptance of this change is pending.
- Resetting movement vitals stops a running swimming flow, and entering water at zero stamina still suppresses client regeneration.
- Natural region handoffs retain accepted server-side gliding, fall tracking and movement-vitals state; when gliding, MapMoveComplete includes the local player glide mode recovered from the researched client.
- Deferred travel (2026-11-02): a LevelTriggerReq/ChannelTriggerEntryReq travel, its owed same-map release handoff, or a ZoneChannelMoveReq refused because the character is busy, dead or has GM-spawned map actors is kept per session (latest request wins). Gameplay ticks retry it every 250 ms while the character stays on the same map; it starts once the blocking state ends, expires after two minutes and is cleared by any started map move. Before, the waiting client stayed blocked at the volume (live invisible-wall report).
- Seamless nested zones (2026-11-02): the spatial zone export (format 2) covers every ArcheWorld zone with one field, point of interest or housing-area map, with parent, nesting depth and condition flag. ZoneChannelMoveReq resolves the deepest zone cell; a character on a nested map whose position leaves it travels to the parent first, as the client asks. The destination is the reported request point (bounded to 5 m) with the tracked yaw. Gated crossings use the travel profile's MapCondition check. Walking into the housing area enters the character's channel in place. Static analysis: a same-root MapMoveStartNoti stays seamless only when it names the client's pending target and, for a parent return, a spawn within 50 cm of the pawn; a same-map answer to a nested-zone request therefore showed a loading screen.

**Custom / guessed behavior (not official)**

Our own guesses, because the data to reproduce the official behavior does not exist. They add no capture evidence and do not promote any status.

- The 5 m start-position tolerance for StartGlidingReq is a local network allowance, not an official rule.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- General map/portal handoff remains unfinished. The bounded tutorial route has a reported original-client world arrival, but the 2026-10-26 live exit disconnected during loading; original-client acceptance of the timer correction remains pending.
- Home and complete channel-travel handling remain unfinished; gliding starts are validated without flight physics. Server teleports exist only for tutorial cutscenes and the player escape.
- Collision/navmesh, speed authority and root-motion reconciliation are incomplete; no MoveReq appeared in these captures.
- Original-client visible following of NPC MoveNoti is not observed; the 600 mm / 900 ms cadence and 16-900 ms pred_milli are Candidate values from the decoded client snap radius and blend window; original-client mid-route death and removal/despawn presentation remain unverified; private GM despawn cancellation has synthetic coverage.
- The newly observed ChannelMove interaction variants 71/72 still need a general interaction-driven handoff handler.
- Fall limits: client-reported positions/modes, no authoritative terrain or ground contact, no mid-fall reconnect continuation, no reconstructed mounted/vehicle/root-motion impacts or fall immunity rules. Safe-height unit conversion, damage curve and default environmental caster/skill fields are Candidate/local policy; no official fall capture or original-client fall acceptance.
- Escape limits: the official destination differed from the client candidate by about 2.2 m (server navigation choice unresolved), so the emulator's use of the candidate is Candidate; no post-teleport sight refresh or observer TeleportNoti (182); the cooldown is session-only and is lost on reconnect; refusal conditions are local policy; the 50030002 removal is immediate instead of ~36 ms later; original-client acceptance is not observed.
- Swimming/drowning limits: movement details and water contact are client-reported, with no water volumes, depth authority, forced ascent or speed enforcement. SW_Dive/SurfaceIdle interpretation and tick-unit conversion remain Candidate; surface-floating exemptions, swim-sprint entry threshold 1 SP and 5%-HP/second immediate drowning are local policy. No oxygen meter/grace period, swimming expertise cost modifiers, mounted/vehicle player drain or official exhaustion/observer presentation is reconstructed. Underwater state is transient across disconnect; no original-client acceptance or live deployment is claimed.
- Zone travel limits: instance zones reached by walking, spherical/nonzero-spawn/interaction-driven routes and general channel allocation remain unresolved. Busy/dead and private-GM requests are deferred and retried until the state ends (at most two minutes) instead of receiving a reconstructed reset reply; original-client acceptance of the deferral is pending. The idle same-map recovery is synthetic-only. Static inactive-zone flags remain a separate launcher patch; supported map routing does not implement absent NPC populations or all-region gameplay.
- Local all-zone exploration: catalog access does not implement server content, physical collision, regional channel allocation or gated quest progression. Windows permissions must allow ordinary process access. Only the researched client signatures and layouts are supported. The separate background-helper path did not resolve the wall; the user confirmed the signed in-process 0.2.6 unlock removed it. Traversal and gameplay in every region remain unobserved.
- Gliding has no authoritative flight physics, flight-tool, combat-state or zone restriction; only the modelled stun ailment counts as crowd control.
- Pre-existing presence leave commits before legacy fanout; an exceptional partial fanout can leave an observer stale. This is unresolved and is not identified as a regression introduced by the candidate.
- Instance and dungeon copies follow a CUSTOM party-or-solo policy: the official channel allocation (Map.chMaxCount), the channel-invite flow and the reset timer of an emptied instance are not recovered, and a copy ends when its last character leaves. Dungeon jump arrivals and doodad cutscene end points are Candidate derivations; other end points use the CUSTOM arrival rule, and the same-map field portals of map 9041 (104010, 504001-504003) stay refused. Saved entrance doodad phases are restored only for the character who triggered them. No original-client trial of copies, jumps, end points or saved doodads exists; the scoped Cliffs encounter reconstructs its known changes from saved quest progress.
- Cliffs of Madness (a point of interest) still uses one shared map channel; inviting or transferring party members through its gate is not implemented. General gated interaction routes, point-of-interest channel allocation and boss behavior remain partial.
- The !unstuck cooldown is session-local, no destination is invented when a map and its parent lack known shrines, and the command has not been tried in the original client.
- Glide direction, velocity and uninterrupted original-client flight across loading are not established by static analysis or synthetic traffic.

**Evidence and verification**

Recovered descriptors/opcode names establish message shapes, not behavior. No complete implementation or original-client acceptance evidence was established. NPC MoveNoti emission: synthetic Combat tests, a native-socket test (NativeWorld.NpcPursuitMoveNotificationsReachTheClientSocketInRunningShape) and a private-PostgreSQL run (7/7, port 55467) support the server behavior only; there is no official capture and no original-client observation. A1 adds interaction-driven ChannelMove tasks 71 and 72: each receives InteractUnitRes and MapMoveStart/Complete with map_id 9012 (69 ms and 121 ms to completion). This is same-map handoff evidence, not a new map or proven channel-number/private-instance rule. Fall-system validation (2026-10-26): isolated C++20 Release build succeeded; all 14 focused CTest cases passed (12 unit/schema/handshake checks plus two native TLS tests using MemoryStore). The socket tests cover safe/nonlethal/lethal landings, no duplicate charge, dead-state reconnect and persisted in-place revival in private and shared map sessions. The protobuf zero-coordinate regression also passed. Tests used generated tutorial/catalog/raw data and the documented child-process OPENSSL_ia32cap=0 diagnostic; PostgreSQL and original-client fall acceptance were not tested. No live server deployment is claimed. Player escape (2026-10-26): evidence is the single official P2 escape sequence, the catalog GameVariables and static client recovery (dumps/ida_research/escape-20261026). Synthetic checks: PlayerEscapeTest.* (schema round trip of every reply, cooldown boundary, refusals, tick-matched handshake ownership) and NativeWorld.OverworldEscapeTeleportsToTheCandidateAndSavesTheDestination over the TLS world transport. No original-client escape trial is claimed. Combat/death regression follow-up: 84 Combat cases passed, 13 environment-gated cases skipped, and six NPC movement cases failed identically in a matching-interface baseline with the combat fall additions removed. Both existing native in-place-revival tests passed with a 180-second allowance (the two-cycle fight exceeded the initial 40-second timeout). These baseline NPC failures and concurrent unreviewed source changes prevent a claim that the entire integration is green. Movement-vitals validation (2026-10-26): isolated C++20 Release build and all 32 focused CTest cases passed without skips (16 movement-vitals unit/schema cases, two new native TLS/MemoryStore stamina/drowning cases and all 14 fall checks). The tutorial socket test observes swim SP drain, drowning without movement, continued damage while stopped underwater, surface cancellation and subsequent sprint SP drain. The shared-map timer kills a low-HP player underwater, persists death, reconnects dead and revives without resumed drowning. Combat regressions: 91 passed, 14 environment-gated skipped, 0 failed of 105. Test processes use the documented OPENSSL_ia32cap=0 diagnostic; no new PostgreSQL execution or original-client trial/live deployment is claimed. Catalog/enums establish inputs only, not official semantics. Tutorial-exit timer correction (2026-10-26): the user reported reaching the world after the tutorial and seeing an entry-error dialog. The active server metadata log shows CutSceneEndReq -> MapMoveStartNoti for the hosted overworld, immediately followed by a fatal timed-action failure because no world position was available during map loading. The timer now defers that stale callback and lets MapLoadCompleteReq and StartPlayingReq finish on the existing TLS connection. The native cutscene socket regression forces a queued sprint deadline behind the map-change worker and checks a Pong before load completion, the deferred-timer path, the subsequent map handshake and arrival quest persistence. An isolated C++20 Release build of live revision d4c6513 plus only the timer fix passed all 49 focused CTests without skips, including that real TLS/MemoryStore regression, housing map moves, swimming/sprint deadlines, escape and fall checks. **Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`PC2S_StartX5RootMotionReq`** — Validated against the owned action, stage, time window, start position, target and the authored reach: max(limit, path) x 1.05 + 300 mm, horizontal with a 5 m height bound for ground-following motions (fitted to 1,407 official frames, none refused). Invalid reports answer CommonErrorRes and log the failed check. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:root_motion (x5.pb.X5RootMotion)

- **`PC2S_EscapeReq`** — is_trading=true recovers the trade wagon after TradeWagonRespawnCooldown. is_trading=false is a CANDIDATE player escape: TeleportReq to the client candidate within 5 m of the server position plus the 300 s 50030003 cooldown; refusals send no frames. No server navigation, sight refresh or persisted cooldown; original-client acceptance open. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:is_trading (bool); 2:candidate_pos (x5.pb.WorldPos)

- **`PC2S_LevelTriggerReq`** — Tutorial triggers (map 8000/10117) plus the shared world: channelSession, channel and portal volumes of every world move the character after the map's entrance and exit conditions; LevelTriggerVolume rules play server cutscenes, run map moves and record doodad phases in the map or instance copy (shared with the players there, saved per character, restored on re-entry). Same-map dungeon GoBoss/GoExit portals jump to the recovered boss/exit doodad arrival (Candidate); other same-map portals refuse with a same-map handoff. Instance and dungeon maps use party or solo copies (CUSTOM). This local candidate is not release-ready: party boss credit and cross-session projectile cancellation require fixes. Copy allocation and boss handoff have focused local fixes but need transport and multi-player verification. Phase-zero persistence needs rollback and reconnect validation. Travel accepted for a busy, dead or GM-encounter character is deferred and retried by gameplay ticks instead of leaving the client waiting. Synthetic TLS only; see docs/instances-and-dungeons.md. Corrected local-client wolves and combat effects are visible; kill/loot/EXP and fresh-ID respawn packet flow are observed. Idle walking animation remains under visual acceptance. Followup tutorial fix: successful map completion binds recreated vitals to the destination without attaching shared monsters; foreign-map requests remain refused. Synthetic regression passes; no blanket gameplay acceptance claim. Schema file: `p_c2s.mapmove.proto`. Fields: Empty protobuf body.
- **`PC2S_StartPlayingReq`** — Tutorial bootstrap or bounded generic presence/movement only; no general map/simulation authority. Saved-death reconnect repair: bootstrap and later observer nubs carry the authoritative Demise/Idle state. After the first StartPlayingReq of a loaded map, a saved-dead character receives Demise then DeathNoti once, without replaying damage, durability loss, rewards or a death transaction. Completed death/revival commits refresh later observer life snapshots. See docs/dead-reconnect.md; original-client acceptance is pending. Schema file: `p_c2s.mapmove.proto`. Also updates bounded movement stamina and sticky SW_Dive/SurfaceIdle underwater state on server time; supported shared-map timers continue without further movement. See docs/movement-vitals.md for local policy and authority limits. Mounted movement no longer reloads full persisted progress for the rider death check. Gameplay ticks are coalesced per session to prevent an overdue timer backlog; no movement requests are discarded. Schema file: `p_c2s.mapmove.proto`. ## World population, visibility and NPC AI

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Player/NPC spawn and removal, sectors, aggro, NPC motion and scripted phases.

**Current implementation**

- Map/distance-filtered generic player presence and private tutorial instances exist.
- Tutorial spawns, basic perception, straight-line pursuit, attack and local leash/reset model exist.
- Tutorial monster spawns and retaliation after server-owned damage exist for monsters without an NPC AI profile.
- Tutorial monsters whose spawner profile carries a complete `ai` block are driven by the NpcAi module (perception, acquisition, pursuit and leash/return) through CombatSession::advance_npc_ai, which emits aggro-target (98), unit-state (32) and AI-phase (114) notifications and ordinary Run/Stop MoveNoti; 64/106 are reserved for supported skill lunges. An AI monster's attack waits until its pursuit is over, and pursuit stop and attack gate share one engagement distance, the smaller of NpcTemplate combatSuitableDistMax and the skill's maxDistance. Phase 1230 is assigned to ten ordinary tutorial NPC types from the captured trace; the leash Return state is a local Candidate because no official leash was captured. A profile with no speed fields keeps the legacy path; a half-present speed pair rejects the profile.
- Map-wide civilian population excludes client-owned staticNpcData actors (including Gus) and now exports 261 active server placements on map 9012: all 145 prior ordinary stationary records plus 116 authored forward civilian routes. Paths and Walk/Run model speeds are read from verified catalog/layer data. One shared listener epoch drives current-pose entry snapshots, late joins and reconnects; per-session timers deliver bounded MoveNoti 177 updates and Stop/StartX5MotionNoti 69 for supported authored inline pauses/activities. Registry positions follow the same timeline before interactions. Map transitions discard old delivery state. This is a local bounded runtime policy, not recovered complete official civilian AI.
- Local combat rework selects a range/cooldown-valid offensive repertoire, rotates eligible attacks, stops movement before casting and steers ranged-only NPCs outside their minimum-distance dead zone. This is a local policy, not recovered official AI; see docs/combat-rework-20261026.md.
- NPC locomotion repair (2026-10-26): ordinary pursuit uses Run/Stop MoveNoti 177 with prediction and increasing ns ticks, never orphan skill-only 64/106. GM-created private encounters use complete catalog locomotion on tutorial and open-world maps, face their route, stop before casting and settle position before return/cast interruption. The generator exports 71 locomotion blocks, including passive zero-cone rows. Private GM kills do not count as authored tutorial quest kills; despawn cancels owned effects and releases actor state. Ambient public/shared-world monster authority, navmesh routing and candidate original-client acceptance remain open. See docs/npc-locomotion-fix-20261026.md.
- Map NPC ids now retain the client NPC type nibble2 using deterministic 16-slot allocation. The user-authorized typed replacement is running with the patrol rate initialization. All 49 selected module/socket checks pass; the earlier speed-stat-only live trial remained visually failing. The user subsequently confirmed NPC movement now works on the final typed build; this human-observed acceptance is separate from synthetic validation.
- World monsters (2026-10-26): shared authoritative populations export 2,802 slots on 106 populated maps (196 definitions), including 417 on 9012 and 812 on 9031, with 470 authored patrols and 1,893 actions. Public clients share health, aggro/action ownership, damage, death and respawn. Raid channels use independent populations keyed by actual channel ID. Current-pose sight, bounded visual journals, fresh life IDs, one-time slots, corpse expiry, killer-owned loot, server HuntMonster credit and EXP are wired. GM test NPCs remain private. See docs/world-mobs.md. Catalog Instance maps use per-character monster populations; party-instance admission remains unrecovered.
- Client-owned static NPCs have a separate optional MapStaticNpcs interaction index. The verified exporter admits unambiguous initially active single-point staticNpcData placements on Release or Demo ArcheWorld Field/HousingArea maps (Demo covers the reachable Shining Shore public channels 9011/9012), with unit kind 7 and authored sector/local identity. Native dialogue/shop target resolution falls back to this exact map-scoped index while retaining catalog interaction and range checks. It emits no duplicate UnitAddNoti, creates no ordinary UnitRegistry entry and does not implement static activation or AI. Missing exports leave this optional interaction path disabled.
- Map civilian population is delivered by sight (src/world/features/npc/npc_sight.cpp): every unit stays registered for server authorization, but UnitAddNoti is sent only for units within 130 m horizontally, after map load and on every client packet or timer tick, and one UnitRemoveNoti removes units beyond 150 m. Patrol MoveNoti/StartX5MotionNoti reach only units the client knows. Official captures show arrival adds within 123 m and 328 paired NPC adds/removes; the radii are a local Candidate policy. Previously all 261 map-9012 placements were announced once at entry and distant NPCs (for example market NPC Edmund) were missing. See docs/npc-sight-20261026.md.
- World-mob correction (2026-10-26): typed wire identities now fit 32 bits because client MoveNoti actor lookup clears the high dword. Separate server-only random receipt IDs preserve durable HuntMonster credit. Roaming-enabled pathless NPCs get bounded local idle walks (687 slots, including 163 on map 9012 and all 21 Meadow Wolf slots); authored patrols remain distinct. Combat/return/death/GM pause suspend walks, and fresh lives reset at home. Explicit player skill targets use the live/attackable/private-ownership predicate. See docs/world-mobs.md.
- Map-load packet preservation: the historical adapter fix retained UnitAddNoti already queued by world combat. The current candidate uses guarded sector snapshots; when the grid lacks the map, the native adapter requests a guarded full-map snapshot without claiming the map-load request. The earlier invisible-mob observation is historical; current original-client acceptance remains pending.
- Shared-world sector streaming (2026-10-27): after every shared-map MapLoadCompleteReq the session sends PS2C_SectorUpdateNoti for the 5 x 5 sector block around the player (y then x), clipped per axis to [sector(Map.area.min) - 1, sector(Map.area.max)], then only sectors entering the block as the player moves; re-entered sectors are sent again. Sector indices use OriginMap.area.min and sectorWidth from the catalog. Updates carry the sector's depleted gathering placements and changed gathering doodads. The private tutorial keeps its authored sector list. See docs/sector-streaming.md.
- Static-NPC map scope correction (2026-10-27): maps 9011/9012 are Demo-package maps, so tools/build_map_static_npcs.py now admits Demo as well as Release ArcheWorld Field/HousingArea maps. The regenerated index has 726 targets (250 on 9012, 1 on 9011); all 475 earlier targets are unchanged. tools/export_client_data.py and tools/start_persistent.ps1 now generate the index with the other server data; the hosted data directory had no static-npcs export, so every static NPC dialogue there resolved to Interaction_TargetNotFound.
- World-mob tick cost (2026-10-27): CombatData builds npc_attacks once at load (each NPC template's executable attacks in catalog order with minimum/maximum range and ranged flag). NPC AI steps, attack selection and usable_npc_attack read that table instead of copying npc_skills JSON and re-walking skill/effect/projectile rows for every mob on every poll. Selection order, distance bands, cooldowns, least-recently-used choice and cast-range rules are unchanged.
- Monster disengagement (2026-10-27): an engaged NpcAi monster returns home when the player or the monster itself is farther than Npc.returnStartDist from its spawn point, and, as a local Candidate policy (kNpcGiveUpWithoutContactMs = 10 s), when it has not attacked, been hit or had its target within attack reach for 10 seconds. Return, reset delay and health reset are unchanged. Melee pursuit now stops at the attack's own hit reach (see combat). See docs/mob-combat-fix-20261027.md.
- Interaction repair (2026-10-29): population sight removals carry by_sight=true and preserve authoritative map/instance registry entries and current patrol poses. Actual despawn and map departure still clear targets. The live host had no static-npcs export; the repair requires deploying the existing 726-target index. Startup now reports its target count or warns when absent. See docs/interaction-mount-repair-20261029.md.
- Scheduled static-NPC identity repair (2026-10-29): day/night client-owned actors are included in the authored interaction index instead of being discarded for startGameTime/endGameTime. The regenerated profile has 1428 map-scoped targets and preserves all 726 previous targets. This restores supported Harbor City vendor operations through the existing map/template/range/catalog and atomic item/gold checks without spawning duplicate actors. The client owns scheduled appearance; independent server opening-hour enforcement remains unimplemented. Weather-dependent, disabled, adventure-controlled and ambiguous placements remain excluded.
- ApplyThreatenReactionReq (20056) resolves each low-32 runtime unit id inside the current map and instance, within the authored 5 m threat range, for 612 civilian definitions with a threatened montage, and sends StartX5MotionNoti (69) to the player and observers with one start tick per channel. Patrols pause and resume from the paused pose; the threatening player's own patrol sends the stop and reaction together; late viewers see the same reaction. There is no acknowledgement.
- Static world-layer repair (2026-10-29): ArcheWorld's always-loaded Static data layers (village NPCs such as Romeline 1002232 in Ruins of Gold) are now exported for each supported public map whose authored area contains the placement; test layers are excluded and the identity, activation, single-candidate and single-position rules are unchanged. The regenerated profile has 2459 targets on 9 maps (9021 rose from 5 to 466) and keeps all 1428 previous targets unchanged. **Custom / guessed behavior (not official)**

Our own guesses, because the data to reproduce the official behavior does not exist. They add no capture evidence and do not promote any status.

- Reaction state is bounded at 4096 actors: finished stationary reactions are dropped first, then finished private-instance reactions; shared patrol offsets are kept.

- **`PS2C_UnitAddNoti`** — Tutorial bootstrap or bounded generic presence/movement only; no general map/simulation authority. Companion mounts (npc.summon/mount), mates (npc.mate) and vehicles (operable.vehicle) on shared maps. Map-wide stationary NPC generation excludes client-owned staticNpcData placements; 261 ordinary map-9012 placements remain (145 stationary, 116 authored civilian routes). Static sector actors are not created as duplicate ordinary NPCs; server-controlled static activation remains missing. Authored civilian routes also use current shared-timeline poses; ordinary walking uses opcode 177 with prediction/Stop and supported inline stop activities use opcode 69. Missing motion-point scripts are not synthesized; original-client acceptance remains pending. Local patrol correction requires NpcNub MoveSpeedRate stat 84=1000 to avoid a zero client speed cap; the running older build omitted it. Corrected client animation is unverified. Server NPC identities must retain type nibble2; sequential untyped allocation was corrected. The speed-stat-only local trial remained visually failing; the final typed build awaits visual acceptance. The user subsequently confirms movement now works on the final typed-ID server; specialized routines remain partial. World-mob update: shared map/channel combat, fresh life IDs, killer-owned loot and server hunt/EXP events are wired. Original-client acceptance and full scripted encounters remain pending; see docs/world-mobs.md. Population NPCs are added by sight (130 m enter, 150 m leave, local Candidate radii) instead of all at map entry; see docs/npc-sight-20261026.md. World-mob correction: actor IDs use the typed 32-bit wire range required by the client low-dword movement lookup; durable quest receipts are separate server-only IDs. Pathless roaming uses the explicit local policy. Corrected original-client combat acceptance remains pending. Map-load correction: gathering appends its snapshot without discarding previously queued monster UnitAddNoti; the former replacement caused unannounced attackers. Corrected local-client wolves and combat effects are visible; kill/loot/EXP and fresh-ID respawn packet flow are observed. Idle walking animation remains under visual acceptance. Server-spawned areas of effect use 32-bit skill-object ids (0xD0000000 | sequence << 4 | 3). Initial dungeon, instance and point-of-interest monster nubs now follow StartPlayingRes (candidate repair; synthetic TLS only). Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:unit_id (uint64); 2:nub (x5.UnitNub); 3:by_sight (bool); 4:debug_ghost (bool); 5:spawned_unit (bool)
- **`PS2C_UnitRemoveNoti`** — Tutorial bootstrap or bounded generic presence/movement only; no general map/simulation authority. Corpses with loot are removed by the loot session instead of combat's timer. World-mob update: shared map/channel combat, fresh life IDs, killer-owned loot and server hunt/EXP events are wired. Original-client acceptance and full scripted encounters remain pending; see docs/world-mobs.md. Population NPCs leaving the 150 m sight radius are removed in one UnitRemoveNoti (local Candidate radius; official captures pair 328 NPC adds with 328 removes). World-mob correction: actor IDs use the typed 32-bit wire range required by the client low-dword movement lookup; durable quest receipts are separate server-only IDs. Pathless roaming uses the explicit local policy. Corrected original-client combat acceptance remains pending. Population sight removals now explicitly set by_sight=true and preserve server authorization; actual despawn still erases the registry entry. CUSTOM (guessed, not official): Corpse lifetimes and the emptied-lifetime anchor are guesses (configurable). Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:unit_ids (repeated uint64); 2:by_sight (bool); 3:debug_ghost (bool)
- **`PS2C_NpcGroupNoti`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:group_cms_id (int32); 2:unit_ids (repeated uint64)
- **`PS2C_UnitChangeStateNoti`** — Current server-owned tutorial combat/AI path; exact mechanics, general effects and shared world remain open. The player Demise uses the player wire unit id (nibble 1), which the client needs to apply Demise (static evidence, Candidate); no original-client proof yet. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:unit_id (uint64); 2:tick (sfixed64); 3:state (x5.cms.EX5UnitStateType); 4:reason (x5.cms.EX5ReturnReasonType)

Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:unit_id (uint64); 2:attributes (repeated x5.pb.UnitChangeAttributeNoti.AttributesEntry)

- **`PS2C_ChangeNpcAggroTopTargetNoti`** — Emitted for tutorial monsters with a complete NPC AI profile on acquisition and release; no shared-world or group threat. Original-client acceptance and full scripted encounters remain pending; see docs/world-mobs.md. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:unit_id (uint64); 2:new_target_unit_id (uint64)
- **`PS2C_NpcMotionEndSyncNoti`** — Supported for the authored NPC attack-lunge lifecycle only: forward-only AdaptedChaseTarget blocks with the 190100400 back-off semantics, with a matching active skill instance/stage/layer. ## Combat, skill stages and damage

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Class/weapon skills, combos/cancel windows, costs, damage, deaths and reactions.

**Current implementation**

- Server deadlines own tutorial actions, costs/cooldowns, stage transitions, damage and quest kill credit.
- The seven-capture corpus requests 109 player/item skill IDs. All 35 new Warrior, twelve Wavesword and 22 mage action IDs were already statically indexed; indexing is not complete simulation.
- Client stage-change requests are validated per reason against the matching extracted notify: input_condition windows, action_stage_condition ground-landing/grab entries and the default next stage, with 250 ms window-edge skew. The 13 extracted ground-landing skills, including 2213, now enter their landing stage on a ground_landing report.
- Accepted stage changes are silent to their owner. A refused change of the current action returns the recovered error code and ends that action, so a refused continuation cannot hold the caster in a 99-second landing wait; stale reports only return Skill_NotUsingSkill.
- Accepted stage changes are silent to their owner, replacing the earlier local response/notification pair that the official captures do not show. A refused change of the current action returns the recovered error code and ends that action, so a refused continuation cannot hold the caster in a 99-second landing wait; stale reports only return Skill_NotUsingSkill.
- Catalog autoRegistration SkillOpen/WeaponUsable perks are sent before map completion; captured-shape gauge, attribute and trait notifications follow map completion in the official Magic entry order.
- Tutorial player death and 3%-of-maximum equipped-item durability loss are revision-guarded and persisted together; dead reconnect and duplicate revival are handled with revision-guarded recovery at a catalog/raw-export indexed shrine.
- SP shortage is refused with Skill_Condition_NotEnoughCost, matching the official refusals observed for skill 1418 (SP cost 10); an HP-cost shortage was not captured and keeps its previous code.
- CombatData accepts up to 8,192 NPC stat definitions (expanded for world populations; earlier limits were 128/256), so the 173-entry open-world profile loads.

- Historical profile-absent/GM fallback contract: CANDIDATE durable in-place player revive (PC2S_ReviveReq 20039): a dead player's request first commits dead=false through the existing revision-guarded commit_world_revival (store-owned account, character and world ownership, dead-only) at the last movement position or, if the player died without moving, the persisted entry position, and only after that commit applies the committed progress and sends exactly PS2C_AddStatusEffectNoti 50030002 (49), PS2C_RemoveStatusEffectNoti of that instance (51), PS2C_ChangeStatNoti with source SCS_Revive restoring health and stamina to their maxima (47) and the Idle unit state (32). A living player or a repeated request does nothing. A refused revival (no known position, revision conflict, store error) is logged, sends no frames, applies no HP/SP/status effect, leaves the player dead in memory and in the store and does not tear the session down; the consequence is that after a conflict the session's cached revision is stale, so a later progress save by that session can still fail with the existing revision-conflict handling. Validations: builder focused run 121 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped of 123 including NativeWorld.InPlaceReviveIsDurableRepeatableAndIgnoredForALivingOrRepeatRequest (real 5001084 fight kills the level-1 Wild through the real death path, 49/51/47/32 in order, immediate reconnect alive, second death and second revive, duplicate and live-player requests are no-ops), NativeWorld.InPlaceReviveWithARevisionConflictSendsNoSuccessAndLeavesThePlayerDead (revision bumped behind the session: no frames, still dead, ping answered) and Combat.PlayerDeathRemovesActiveSelfCastStatusOnceAndReviveEmitsNoRemoval; PostgreSQL store proof 7 of 7 *Postgres* tests on a private disposable cluster (port 55462) including Storage.PostgresDeathAndRevivalRollbackAndReconnect; and the independent reviewer's native-wire run against a private PostgreSQL (death, 20039, frames 49/51/47/32, row dead=false revision 2, reconnect alive, second death and revive). Limits: no official teleport or shrine rule, no gold penalty, no 50030001 protection, no shared world or PvP; the revival position is the client-reported movement position (no new authority, no verification); a theoretical split exists if the in-memory step after the store commit ever threw (the store would hold alive while the session stays dead until reconnect); sessions without a persistence handoff (unit fixtures only) revive in memory; a throwing store was not induced (argued from the catch and the conflict test); the NativeWorld revive tests use MemoryStore and PostgreSQL evidence is the store test plus the reviewer's wire run; original-client acceptance is not observed.

- Local combat rework (2026-10-26): authored unique effect IDs survive damage/projectile notifications; event deadlines and default-stage clocks do not drift with late polling. Captures refine matching authored events without deleting uncaptured events. The same-build seven-capture importer corrects 2249 release timing to stage 1 and adds 379 NPC/skill memberships; generated coverage is 1008 actions and 1245 effects, not complete gameplay.
- NPC local selection policy: least recently used eligible offensive Normal action, catalog minimum/maximum distance, per-skill/shared-group cooldown, ranged casting independent of the melee stopping gate, melee suitable-distance gate, and action-duration pacing instead of a universal three-second interval. Approach selects a usable band and ranged-only retreat is leash-bounded. Official selection/retreat rules and original-client acceptance remain unresolved.
- Bounded interval areas support cylinders and oriented boxes, target-relative placement, repeated per-pulse overlap groups, lifetime despawn and later removal. Projectile splash selects around impact; self-directed chained effects retain their caster. Sphere effects use a spherical distance check.
- CANDIDATE fitted damage (docs/item-effects.md): a player hit on an NPC deals 5.7685 x (physicalCoefficient x PhysicalAttackPower + magicCoefficient x MagicAttackPower) + 47.109 - 0.5717 x target armor (physical/magic armor weighted by the attack shares), fitted to 867 official hits with every residual within 1.4 points (882 of 882 within 1 point after rounding, fixed damage included); an NPC hit on the player deals 1.2106 x coefficient x attack x 44.88/(44.88 + armor) per share plus 1.0282 x elemental coefficient x elemental attack mitigated the same way, fitted to 89 official hits (91% exact after rounding). Fixed damage (the dagger's 2120) lands unchanged; armor below zero counts as zero (Stat minimum); Incoming/Outgoing damage stats scale the hit as per mille (Candidate). Attack and armor buffs and debuffs therefore change damage. Stats without attack ratings (53/48) keep the earlier local model, so existing fixtures are unchanged. src/world/features/combat/combat_rules.cpp; CombatRules tests reproduce four official hits.

Ambient public/shared-world monster authority, navmesh routing and candidate original-client acceptance remain open. See docs/npc-locomotion-fix-20261026.md.

GM in-place revival and the profile-absent fallback remain separate paths; full official penalties, protection duration and selection semantics are unresolved.

Roaming-enabled pathless NPCs get bounded local idle walks (687 slots, including 163 on map 9012 and all 21 Meadow Wolf slots); authored patrols remain distinct. Combat/return/death/GM pause suspend walks, and fresh lives reset at home. Explicit player skill targets use the live/attackable/private-ownership predicate. See docs/world-mobs.md.

- Area spawn hits and 32-bit area ids (2026-10-27): an area whose SkillObject row names aoeSpawnSkillEffectId exports it as spawn_effect_id and applies it once at the created tick, right after its UnitAddNoti, to the enemies inside the area (effect maxTargetCount or the area cap), with the area unit as DamageNoti caster. This restores the damage of the mage elemental bursts 2274/2275 (areas 160402/160401, effects 160505/160503) and their combo variants (31 player skills, 2 NPC skills, 24 areas). Area unit ids now use the 32-bit block 0xD0000000 | sequence << 4 | 3 instead of a bit-60 tag, matching the captured 32-bit ids and the client's low-dword unit lookup; ids still held by live areas are skipped on wrap.
- Monster hit fixes (2026-10-27): shapes are tested against the target's game-hit capsule (player_collision for NPC attacks, npc_collision for player attacks) instead of its centre point; shapeCylinder targeting is a real cylinder instead of the skill-range fallback that let 1.5 m melee cylinders of 50 m skills hit distant players. Each executable NPC attack gets a load-time melee reach (furthest straight-ahead distance at which within_shape still touches a standing player, plus a supported lunge's travel) that limits cast range, pursuit stop and first engagement distance; attacks whose reach is shorter than their catalog minimum distance are not used as pursuit bands. Candidate: delayed AdaptedChaseTarget windows (394 NPC attacks) are now simulated, starting their 64/106 lunge when the window opens, sampling and facing the target then, and judging later hits from the moving pose; offset direction -180 equals 180. See docs/mob-combat-fix-20261027.md.

After the first StartPlayingReq of a loaded map, a saved-dead character receives Demise then DeathNoti once, without replaying damage, durability loss, rewards or a death transaction. Completed death/revival commits refresh later observer life snapshots. See docs/dead-reconnect.md; original-client acceptance is pending.

- Weapon switch repair (2026-10-29): captured official switches are StartSkillReq of a SwapWeapon skill (17 catalog skills, e.g. 1102000 HandAxe, 1327 LongBow) whose equip_slot names the destination (absent = Weapon_1), answered by WeaponSlotActivationNoti 172. CombatPlayerSession now asks the inventory owner to commit that slot before the skill is validated against the equipped weapon type, on both the shared-world and private-encounter paths; previously the skill was refused against the old weapon. Ordinary skills never change the slot. The combat profile skill limit rose from 2,048 to 4,096 (kMaxCombatSkills / MAX_COMBAT_SKILLS) because the wider monster export carries 1,941+ skills.
- Skill special mechanics (2026-10-30): (1) Stage immune windows: a hit landing while the target's running stage has an immune notify whose Immune row grants Dodge (235 player and 37 NPC windows; row 1) or Damage is cancelled and answered with PS2C_ImmuneNoti {dodge|damage}; the overlap group is not consumed. A hit whose damage reactionType category (Sway, Knockback, KnockDown, ParryingAttacker) is in the target's immune names still lands, preceded by ImmuneNoti{reaction} naming the category's first level. (2) addShield/dispelShield: the Shield row amount plus per-mille of maximum/current health becomes stat 71 (ChangeStatNoti SCS_StatusEffect, then the effect's status), hits spend stat 71 before health (DamageNoti lists the stat-71 change, damage_type Shield when fully absorbed), the shield's FK_immuneId applies while it lasts, and expiry, dispel and death clear it. (3) changeWeaponSkillSlot sends PS2C_ChangeWeaponSkillSlotNoti with expire_tick = effect tick + SkillEffect.duration (54 catalog effects, 93 player skills). (4) skillCooldownReset frees the cooldown keys of FK_CooldownResetSkillIds and sends PS2C_ResetCooldownNoti (parry counter 1127 -> pursuit 1000526). The generator exports the Immune and Shield tables and the two effect fields.
- Root-motion reach repair (2026-10-30, docs/root-motion-reach-20261030.md): live logs showed 6 of 85 player 20033 reports refused with BadRequest (the client's "Invalid Request" modal), more often in towns. Replaying the old 3D bound max_distance_mm x 1.05 + 50 mm over the 1,407 official 20033 frames refused 54 (3.8%): reports overshoot the authored reach by at most 196 mm regardless of length, Adapted motions travel their whole authored path when maxMoveDistance is shorter (1100518: 24 of 24 refused) and ground-following motions change height by up to 1.5 m on terrain. The reach is now max(max_distance_mm, path_length_mm) x 1.05 + 300 mm, compared horizontally for ground motions with height change bounded by the 5 m position tolerance (3D for the one non-ground motion); the new rule refuses none of the 1,407 official frames. Refusals log their reason and distances without positions or unit ids. The margin and height bound are local policy fitted to captures. Evidence: capture replay and synthetic Combat tests; original-client confirmation in a town is pending.
- Refused player combat requests are logged (Combat refused player request opcode, skill id, instance, error code) so live sessions show which casts, stage changes and projectile reports the server rejects.
- Instance monster announcement timing (candidate): Dungeon, Instance and PointOfInterest populations attach and send their initial NPC nubs after StartPlayingRes instead of during map loading. The official Cliffs capture shows monster additions after StartPlaying. A synthetic dungeon TLS case checks the ordering; ordinary Field map timing is preserved.
- The authored Stun status pauses NPC pursuit and attacks until expiry. A positive DamageNoti targeted to the player cancels a pending gathering interaction; further hit-reaction and PvP interruption behavior remains unverified.
- Early Stun removal releases NPC AI; first-hit engagement is counted before an NPC acquires aggro. Other hit reactions remain partial. The current candidate retains and fences a session with an uncertain death commit until reconciliation and the required cleanup complete before readmission.
- Outstanding-projectile immunity retention (2026-11-02): ending or changing a player action retains its elapsed Dodge, Damage and reaction immunity on already outstanding flights for their own impact deadlines. Cancellation and stage retirement win at the exact cutoff; authored stage duration bounds the lifetime. Immediate chained effects use the retained immunity, but new secondary flights do not inherit it. A newer action cannot grant immunity to an earlier impact, including sub-millisecond differences. No packet schema or opcode changes.
- 2026-11-02 native population scheduling admits requests, every scheduled gameplay deadline, and close through the shared population/copy CombatTimeline. Work executes on the existing session worker at its admitted logical tick; successor registration completes the claim. The wake identity includes population and owner generation. Map departure retires its old schedule after the admitted frame; close retains the actual session through durable recovery and detach. A never-admitted close retries at the current clock, while an accepted close retains its tick. No process-wide combat lock or transient-combat restart reconstruction is introduced.
- Successful map completion binds recreated player vitals to the loaded map, including followup tutorial instances without shared monsters. Failed map-load responses do not initialize combat; foreign-map requests remain rejected.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Criticals, guard and parry (dodge immune windows and shields are now implemented), an exact (not fitted) official damage formula, defense/invulnerability, full effects and shared-world combat remain unfinished.
- Living vitals/cooldowns reset on reconnect; durable encounter recovery and complete official revival semantics remain unfinished.
- Ground contact and grab outcomes are client-reported; the server has no terrain or grab simulation. Move-cancel endings, observer stage notifications, cost/chase/air-drop/teleport transitions and the official client reaction to a refused stage change are not reconstructed.
- Criticals, guard and parry (dodge immune windows and shields are now implemented), an exact (not fitted) official damage formula, defense/invulnerability, full effects and shared-world combat and PvP remain unfinished.
- Shared-world mob combat sessions now run; original-client death/revival acceptance remains pending; nearest same-map shrine is a local Candidate policy and official gold, delay, failure and aggro rules remain unverified.
- Earned skill perks, exact official damage/defense, effect scope, automatic stage notifications and nearby observer delivery remain unfinished; original-client acceptance beyond the HUMAN-confirmed Wild/starter-axe attack baseline f9d5d15b (13:51; other classes and weapons untested) remains open.
- Area/status support is bounded to the implemented effect paths. Moving skill objects, all conditional effects, shields/auras and full collision/visual parity remain open; see docs/combat-rework-20261026.md.
- Original-client acceptance of tutorial monster retaliation and the expanded NPC repertoires remains open. World monster populations now have shared CombatSession authority; full conditional encounters and navigation remain open.
- Cross-session late-poll projectile ordering remains unresolved: an earlier-due stun flight can be processed after a later-due NPC projectile when the target session polls first. The official ordering is not captured. This is distinct from the synthetic test where a stun already committed by another player cancels the same-life NPC projectile.
- Projectile application is not transactional under every exception: an allocation or effect failure after HP or other state mutation may leave partial changes. A synthetic throwing logging-sink test exercises a stronger retry contract than the live close-on-error path; normal logging may swallow sink failures. No complete retry or rollback guarantee is claimed.
- Corpse-removal delay anchor and the 5000 ms catalog conflict are unresolved.
- NPC damage amount now follows a Candidate fit to 89 official NPC hits (armor mitigation 44.88/(44.88 + armor)); the fit is empirical, criticals and reactions are not modelled and original-client acceptance of the new amounts is open.
- The retained in-place fallback lacks an official teleport/shrine rule; the indexed shrine path remains Candidate and lacks gold penalty, the 50030001 post-revival protection (a fixed 1.5 s is refuted: observed 0.375-52.7 s, duration rule unresolved), shared-world and PvP behavior, and original-client acceptance; NPC damage AMOUNT remains too high (Candidate evidence only, not implemented: combat/npc-damage-amount.md and combat/npc-attack-unit.md).
- Original-client acceptance of the player wire id, visible NPC damage and the player death (Demise and HP) is still required: only synthetic tests and private-wire evidence exist, and a character that died in a session stays durably dead until the supported revival path is used.

- NPC priorities, encounter chains, boss phases, reactions, navigation and official retreat/acquisition rules remain unresolved. Least-recently-used selection and retreat are documented local policies. No original-client acceptance of the rework is recorded.
- Quest 10000040 objective 2 is NOT fixed by the update-frame parity change: the reported failure had no second 20019 in the examined server log and its cause is open (client-side gates and server-fed local condition state are not ruled out); no progress or reward is forced.
- NPC attack lunges remain narrow: only forward-only AdaptedChaseTarget blocks with the 190100400 back-off semantics move the NPC, now including delayed windows (Candidate, 2026-10-27); their client start timing is not captured and the 64 for a delayed window has no original-client observation. The target sample is a bounded local policy (not proven official homing); the official final 106 pose/cadence is not reproduced; dashes have no collision or navmesh; attacks whose movement exists only in animation data cannot be simulated; and no original-client acceptance exists.

**Evidence and verification**

Monster hit fix validation (2026-10-27): new Combat tests cover reach-gated melee approach, a shapeCylinder that no longer hits a player 20 m away, capsule-overlap hits and delayed lunge windows; lunge, event-shape and ranged-selection tests whose negative controls asserted swings from out of reach were updated. Generated world profile: 838 monster types simulated, 0 attacking without a hit (152 on unmodified HEAD), 0 never attacking. Isolated full chronicles-tests 868 passed, 72 optional skips; the area-spawn test belonging to concurrent work fails without touching a changed path. Synthetic only. Area spawn-hit validation (2026-10-27): live server logs showed every cast of 2274/2275 applying only the zero-damage interval effect 143514 (damage=0). The official mage capture (9 burst casts) places each area on the StartSkillReq target with created_tick equal to the client effect report, and across the capture corpus 113 area spawns with an authored spawn effect show that effect at the created tick with the area as caster.
