**Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`PC2S_AcceptQuestReq`** — Tutorial instances use their generated profile; every other map uses the all-quest catalog through WorldQuestBook. Company conditions are checked against CompanyService in the client order; unsupported quest rules fail closed. Full coverage 2026-10-30: unit may also name a job board, quest doodad or memo spot object; requireGold/requireItemIds gates; abandoned and repeated jobs start a new attempt. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:quest_cms_id (int32); 2:pos (x5.pb.WorldPos); 3:yaw (float); 4:unit (x5.pb.AcceptQuestReq.Unit); 5:trigger_volume_enter (x5.pb.AcceptQuestReq.TriggerVolume); 6:unexpect_trigger_volume_enter (x5.pb.AcceptQuestReq.UnexpectTriggerVolume); 15:packet_seq (x5.pb.PacketSeq)
- **`PC2S_QuestAbandonReq`** — Accepted incomplete quests with isAbandonable become tombstones with a higher attempt (schema 37); Quest_AbandonFailed otherwise. Never captured. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:quest_cms_id (int32)
- **`PC2S_QuestRewardReq`** — Tutorial instances use their generated profile; every other map uses the all-quest catalog through WorldQuestBook. Unsupported quest rules fail closed. Turn-in consumes the stacks that satisfied GetItem objectives (captured). unit_id names the job board or turn-in doodad for JobBoard and Doodad completions (2026-10-30). Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:quest_cms_id (int32); 2:unit_id (uint64)
- **`PC2S_ProgressQuestReq`** — Tutorial instances use their generated profile; every other map uses the all-quest catalog through WorldQuestBook. Unsupported quest rules fail closed. Shared world 2026-10-30: interact_memo is validated against the placed memo spot objects of the objective; interact_npc confirms the announced NPC. 2026-10-30: time, housing_funishing, company_contribution and level_exp_gain reports ask for a server re-evaluation; adventure_logbook_percentage is accepted for the objective's zone (CUSTOM). Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:quest_cms_id (int32); 2:quest_progress_sequence_id (int32); 3:pos (x5.pb.WorldPos); 4:yaw (float); 5:adventure_logbook_percentage (x5.pb.ProgressQuestReq.AdventureLogbookPercentage); 6:company_contribution (x5.pb.ProgressQuestReq.CompanyContribution); 7:dialogue_selection (x5.pb.ProgressQuestReq.DialogueSelection); 8:equip_item (x5.pb.ProgressQuestReq.EquipItem); 9:housing_funishing (x5.pb.ProgressQuestReq.HousingFunishing); 10:interact_memo (x5.pb.ProgressQuestReq.InteractMemo); 11:interact_npc (x5.pb.ProgressQuestReq.InteractNpc); 12:level_exp_gain (x5.pb.ProgressQuestReq.LevelExpGain); 13:time (x5.pb.ProgressQuestReq.Time); 14:trigger_volume_enter (x5.pb.ProgressQuestReq.TriggerVolume); 15:trigger_volume_leave (x5.pb.ProgressQuestReq.TriggerVolume)
- **`PC2S_QuestJobBoardReq`** — Board doodad placed near the player; renews the daily period (completed jobs become abandoned tombstones announced with QuestAbandonRes force) and, with refresh_using_cost, spends QuestJobBoard.resetCost Gold and draws again. Recovered client sender AAC_QuestJobBoard_SendQuestJobBoardReq; never captured. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:quest_job_board_cms_id (int32); 2:doodad_unit_id (uint64); 3:refresh_using_cost (bool)
- **`PS2C_QuestUpdateNoti`** — Tutorial instances use their generated profile; every other map uses the all-quest catalog through WorldQuestBook. GM acceptance bypasses NPC/range, optionally retains catalog conditions and commits ordinary supplies/progress before publishing these packets. Existing saved quests cannot be restarted. Unsupported quest rules fail closed. World-mob update: shared map/channel combat, fresh life IDs, killer-owned loot and server hunt/EXP events are wired. Original-client acceptance and full scripted encounters remain pending; see docs/world-mobs.md. World-mob correction: actor IDs use the typed 32-bit wire range required by the client low-dword movement lookup; durable quest receipts are separate server-only IDs. Pathless roaming uses the explicit local policy. Corrected original-client combat acceptance remains pending. Crafting-station recipes and gathering doodads credit counter objectives after their commit (2026-10-30). Combat events from requests, timers and successful direct item effects now use a retained source-bound quest transaction before later monster rewards. Lost acknowledgements retry the same planned output; an uncommitted RAM batch is not process-crash recovery. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:quest (x5.pb.Quest); 2:skip_contents_effect (bool)
- **`PS2C_QuestAcceptRes`** — Tutorial instances use their generated profile; every other map uses the all-quest catalog through WorldQuestBook. Unsupported quest rules fail closed. Four captured Cliffs quest follow-ups are also repaired on periodic refresh for previously stranded characters. Three later authored story follow-ups are candidate automatic starts, with prerequisite checks and no reactivation of abandoned quests. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:quest (x5.pb.Quest); 2:npc_pos (x5.pb.WorldPos); 15:packet_seq (x5.pb.PacketSeq)
- **`PS2C_QuestAbandonRes`** — force false answers an abandonment; force true removes a completed job at the board's daily renewal (Candidate). The client handler removes the quest record (AAC_Quest_Candidate_OnQuestAbandonRes). Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:quest_cms_id (int32); 2:force (bool)
- **`PS2C_QuestJobBoardRes`** — jobs map {board id: quest_cms_ids} with three slots (CUSTOM deterministic draw per character, board, period and paid refresh) and condition_not_met_ids for offers whose conditions fail. Never captured. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:jobs (repeated x5.pb.QuestJobBoardRes.JobsEntry); 2:condition_not_met_ids (repeated int32)
- **`PS2C_QuestJobBoardRemoveNoti`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:jobs (repeated x5.pb.QuestJobBoardRemoveNoti.JobsEntry)
- **`PS2C_WorldCharQuestsNoti`** — Tutorial instances use their generated profile; every other map uses the all-quest catalog through WorldQuestBook. Unsupported quest rules fail closed. Schema file: `p_s2c.character.proto`. Fields: 1:quests (repeated x5.pb.Quest)

## Dialogue, adventure objects, doors and cutscenes

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Discovery/activation, NPC dialogue, interaction animations, object phases and cutscenes.

**Current implementation**

- Tutorial floor objects, key door, lever/gate, notes and bounded NPC quest dialogue exist.
- Server animation timing, map/range checks, atomic consumption and reconnect state protect rewards.
- Level triggers (LevelTriggerReq 20084) are generated from LevelTriggerVolume/Task/Condition for each tutorial instance: per-volume rules with PlayCutScene and ChangeDoodadPhase tasks and grouped quest conditions. Rules with unmodeled conditions, tasks or unrecovered cutscene end points are kept but never run.
- Server cutscenes: VisibleChannelNoti (6) plus CutScenePlayNoti; CutSceneEndReq (20055) applies the cutscene's follow-up exactly once: captured end teleport (TeleportReq 181, then TeleportStart/Completion 20088/20089), visible channel 3, CutSceneBind server NPC AI phase (SetNpcAiPhaseNoti 114), or the end-point map move.
- Herald Knight chain: quest 10000044's final volume plays cutscene 1523, its end teleports the player through the sealed door into the arena and sets the boss to phase 2302400; the finishing kill sends BossKilledBannerNoti, activates arena doodad 10100017 and plays cutscene 1521, whose end point moves the player to map 10117. Cutscene 1520 in map 10117 moves the player to the shared world.
- In-session map moves re-arm MapLoadComplete/StartPlaying, remove the previous map's units, persist the new position, and resume a character saved in map 10117 in that instance.
- Tutorial treasure chest 20080008 (interaction 300, animation 100): the generator attaches the Interaction row's animation and the earliest rig execute notify (2851 ms of 2851-2937 ms; all rigs end at 4000 ms) to looting objects, and marks equipment rewards as item instances. Execute sends ActivateAdventureObjectRes, ItemsUpdateNoti (adventure_object_activate, one new necklace 11500101 row) and InteractionAnimRes; the row and the Activated state commit in one storage transaction. A full inventory answers ItemSlotLimit and keeps the chest closed; reopening an activated chest grants nothing.
- Rejected tutorial StartInteractionAnimReq answers StartInteractionAnimRes (ec, sheathed weapon state), the captured rejection shape; CommonErrorRes left the original client locked in its pending animation. Adventure-object StartInteractionAnimNoti echoes the request yaw without target_unit_id, as captured for animations 100 and 305.
- Nuia Tears (TearsOfNui): a build-guarded immutable index exports 137 placements / 119 CMS IDs / 30 map IDs from verified Map layers, spot files and deterministic catalog reward joins; 44 placements belong to map 9012. ActivateAdventureObjectReq (20049) grants item 2000 in quantities 1, 5 or 10, commits its balance and character-owned Activated marker atomically before response 91 and item update 169, prevents duplicate/reconnect/cross-map rewards, and restores saved states through snapshot 127. Discovery 20050 grants nothing. Living-character, server map, 10 m tracked range, 5 m reported-position tolerance, input/overflow/revision bounds and 32 requests/second limit apply; range/tolerance are bounded local policy, not recovered official rules.
- Nui statues and flames: a matching-build immutable export contains 788 map/spot placements (512 statues, 276 flames, 118 catalog map IDs; not hosted maps), including common world layers resolved by world-asset ownership and three-dimensional Map.area bounds. All ten official P1/P2 activation targets join to this index; runtimeDataLayerPath alone omitted nine. Dynamic layer activation is not fully recovered. Discovery persists character-owned Discovered state without rewards. Group-10 animations 10/16 validate target/map/range, living/busy state, reported position and authored execute time (5000/3408 ms with a local 100 ms allowance); activation commits the Activated marker before 91/167, and refill 104 reserves owned utility-stack units without manufacturing or spending inventory. Repeated execution is idempotent, repeated starts retain the original deadline, and cancellation or a 30-second timeout grants nothing. Start rejections use 165; successful starts use 166. See src/world/features/nuia/nui_statue.* and the saved research under dumps/ida_research/nui-statue-20261026/.
- Nui offerings use the statically recovered ItemUseReq 20077 sender rather than an invented blessing request. The bounded runtime requires item 2000, an indexed nearby statue target, a positive owned-stack count, no quick-slot/nonzero instance selector and living/nonbusy state. A revision-guarded transaction spends tears and advances incremental NuiBlessingLevel thresholds; duplicate sequences cannot spend twice. ItemsUpdateNoti 169 and ChangeNuiBlessingLevelNoti 74 follow commit, with SCS_Growth stat refresh when the level changes. Stored level/partial tears appear in WorldCharBaseNoti; CharacterStats applies cumulative catalog MaxHP/MaxSP rewards. The researched catalog grants 20 MaxHP per reached level through level 30; this is not a direct GM blessing-level operation.
- Saved-death reconnect compatibility: automatic tear/statue discovery while dead is a mutation-free no-op within existing request-rate bounds. Explicit collection, activation, offerings and interaction refusals remain enforced. Ignoring this proximity report does not implement discovery or unindexed objects.
- Interaction repair (2026-10-29): NPC dialogue/shop resolution keeps the authoritative target when its client actor leaves sight and later returns. Client-owned NPCs require the separately deployed static-npcs index; catalog interaction, map, instance and range checks remain enforced. Other unsupported shared-world interaction types are still partial.
- Automatic discovery routing repair (2026-10-29): the Nuia Tear handler claims well-formed DiscoverAdventureObjectReq only for its indexed map/target. Other objects fall through without a target-error notification, progress access, reward, fabricated discovery or consumption of the tear request budget. Malformed requests retain bounded BadRequest validation; explicit activation, known-tear distance checks, statue ownership and tutorial routing are preserved. This does not implement unsupported adventure-object types.
- Shared-world chests and records (interaction groups 300/305) on 54 maps and 386 generated placements use the tutorial interaction timing, range and cancellation with one atomic activation, reward and item commit. Rewards are rolled once per session and object and never repeat after reconnect.
- Static world-layer repair (2026-10-29): ArcheWorld's always-loaded Static data layers (village NPCs such as Romeline 1002232 in Ruins of Gold) are now exported for each supported public map whose authored area contains the placement; test layers are excluded and the identity, activation, single-candidate and single-position rules are unchanged. The regenerated profile has 2459 targets on 9 maps (9021 rose from 5 to 466) and keeps all 1428 previous targets unchanged. Before this, village dialogue on map 9021 was refused with Interaction_TargetNotFound, which the client shows as 'Unable to find target'. Sessions placed on main-world map 1 by GM tp_map remain outside the index.
- Static NPC interaction targets now exist on every playable ArcheWorld map type (2,584 targets on 26 maps), including instances and points of interest.
- Static-layer adventure repair (2026-10-30): build_adventure_objects.py and build_nuia_tears.py now read ArcheWorld's always-loaded Static layers inside each public Field/HousingArea map area (tools/world_layers.map_layer_files), like the NPC exporters. The shared adventure profile also takes every adventure object whose interaction is an unconditional Use that activates it (for example the Ruins of Gold looting spot 20029010, group 23 without animation, activated through InteractUnitReq); Nuia Tears and Nui idols keep their own owners. Shared adventure objects grow from 386 on 54 maps to 1,933 on 72 maps (9021: 4 -> 469); Nuia Tears from 137 to 285 (9021: 2 -> 75). Before this the live server answered Interaction_TargetNotFound for Ruins of Gold tears and looting spots. Objects with unresolved loot conditions or unsupported requirements stay explicit unavailable entries (127).
- Quest-gated adventure objects (2026-10-30): build_adventure_objects.py also exports activating Use interactions whose condition rows are all Quest or OwnItem (normalized by build_quest_catalog.quest_conditions on InteractionCondition) as interaction_conditions; 27 placements on 10 maps were added, for example First Hunt's Hunting Knife 20019119 and the Hands to Spare axe 20019120. adventure::Session refuses a start or InteractUnitReq on a not yet activated gated object with Interaction_ConditionsNotMatch unless the quest service confirms the conditions (fail closed without one); activated objects replay without a check or a second reward. The profile loader rejects unknown condition kinds.
- Live hotfix (2026-11-01): equipment rewards from shared adventure objects, such as First Hunt's hunting knife 20019119 and chests that roll Grand or Legendary gear, passed the full enum name (EX5ItemGrade_Normal) to the tutorial instance-reward commit, which adds the prefix itself, so every such take or chest opening threw and the connection was closed. adventure::Catalog::roll_rewards now emits the catalog grade name. A failure inside one adventure request is now logged, closes the open interaction and refuses only that request (adventure::Session::abort) instead of dropping the player; the stock client could not always return after the drop (repeated world TLS handshake failures). Tests: EquipmentRewardAdventure and AdventureProfile.EveryGeneratedObjectRewardUsesACommittableGradeName.
- Automatic discovery range repair (2026-11-01): shared adventure/tutorial objects, Nuia Tears and Nui statues now accept DiscoverAdventureObjectReq through one check, quest_rules::within_discovery_range: horizontal distance from the tracked position up to 100 m plus the 5 m reported-position tolerance, ignoring height. Previously each handler required a 3D distance of at most 100 m, which refused reports for objects on cliffs or at the boundary with TooFar and showed 'Target is too far.' while the player only walked. Discovery still grants nothing; explicit activation, collection and interaction keep their 3D ranges; Tear reported-position, map, target, death and rate checks are unchanged.
- Coilstones with supported play-record conditions and build-point rewards are exported and enforce their authored gates. Air-bubble doodads use their authored stamina-recovery effect and timed respawn.
- Air-bubble execution rechecks recovery capacity before consuming the doodad.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- General dialogue functions and arbitrary shared-world interactions remain outside the indexed tutorial set.
- Boss AI phase transitions after 2302400 (2302401/2302403/2302404) are not emitted.
- Shared-world level triggers, ClientPlayDialogue/MapMove trigger tasks, and cutscene end points other than 10117/9999993 and 9011/10000046 are not recovered.
- The 9011 end point is placed on the single hosted overworld channel; channel 9011 itself is not hosted separately.
- Sitting needs seat-slot ownership, occupied-seat checks, attach/detach, cancellation and disconnect release; no current runtime path was established.
- Counted repeatable world-object contributions (49039) are outside the tutorial object set. The catalog's 20-use phase transition and linked object 49040 were not observed after only five contributions.
- Generic interaction 11150 was used twice; its player-facing purpose remains unresolved.
- Nuia Tear play-record counters, collection achievements/unlocks, missing raw placements, and original-client local acceptance remain unverified or unsupported. The available 30-map static index does not host those maps; unsupported adventure-object types remain missing.
- Nui refill economics, offering reply order, exact shrine eligibility/range and current-HP behavior are bounded local policies without official offering/refill success captures. The recovered offering UI sender exists, but demo UI reachability is unverified. Runtime rejects nonzero item-instance selectors and quick-slot offers. Exported sanctuary combat/NPC-spawn radii are not general sanctuary enforcement; physical navigation/collision and other shared objects remain unfinished. Statue ChannelMove interactions 71/72 require distinct ordinary/PK field channels and remain unsupported; the existing player PvP flag is not substituted for a channel transition. Zone-completion hooks, non-kill play-record counters and the client's separate cached utility-group tier source remain unresolved.
- Eight authored chest placements stay unavailable because their client data is invalid (map 20702 objects 20070100-20070103 name missing ExpertiseReward rows; map 30711 objects 20075000-20075003 contain malformed reward JSON).
- Shared-world LevelTriggerReq scripts (map move, cutscenes without recovered end points, client dialogue tasks) remain unhandled outside the tutorial.
- Adventure objects gated by ConsumeItem (locked chests), PlayRecord (Raven waystones) or channel-event conditions remain unexported and unanswered.

**Evidence and verification**

Post-deployment acceptance (2026-10-29): repair 220807a is live; after reconnecting, the user confirmed both automatic proximity warnings and the Harbor City vendor sale are fixed, including item removal and gold receipt. This is user-observed original-client acceptance of these two cases; the bounded buffered capture covers reconnect but not the final sale. It does not establish all interactions or server NPC schedules. Proximity discovery investigation (2026-10-29): original-client emulator capture correlates 21 Interaction_TargetNotFound responses to automatic discovery: 18 LootingObject targets and one each HersanderCairn, RecordStone and RavenMaumet, all outside the tear index. Error 4207 matches the displayed English text. Session and real-TLS regressions failed before the repair and pass afterward; the focused CTest selection passed all 46 without skips. See docs/proximity-discovery-repair-20261029.md. Nui Statue implementation validation (2026-10-26): Release tests/server/account targets built. Focused CTest 36 passed, two PostgreSQL gates skipped, zero failed; both gated cases subsequently passed in an isolated PostgreSQL run of seven persistence tests plus account/lobby/restart checks. Surrounding CTest selection passed 159 with 26 optional gates skipped and zero failed of 185. Ten Nui export/capture, three tear-collection and eleven reference-generator Python tests passed without skips. Native TLS covers activation/offering/reconnect and flame revival with atomic supply/destination/life commit only after teleport completion. TLS used the documented OPENSSL_ia32cap=0 diagnostic, not proof of normal CPU dispatch or original-client acceptance. The disposable cluster was stopped and the live service was not replaced. See docs/nui-statues.md for remaining sanctuary/PK/zone/economics boundaries. Earlier evidence follows. Recovered descriptors/opcode names establish message shapes. The 2026-10-24 official tutorial capture shows the order LevelTriggerReq -> CutScenePlayNoti(1523) -> CutSceneEndReq -> TeleportReq/VisibleChannelNoti/SetNpcAiPhaseNoti, and boss death -> BossKilledBannerNoti -> doodad phase -> CutScenePlayNoti(1521) -> CutSceneEndReq -> MapMoveStartNoti(10117). The teleport destination and both end-point spawns come from that capture (static coordinates); the client tables do not contain them. On 2026-10-26 LevelTriggers, GeneratedQuests.HeraldKnightDoorCutsceneReachesTheArenaAndTheBossOpensTheNextInstance and the real-socket NativeWorld.TutorialCutsceneFollowUpsTeleportAndMoveMapsOverTheRealFramePath passed. The door/arena path has not yet been observed in the original client against this server. Additional capture A1 (2026-10-26) adds chair-sit and interaction 49039 observations; see protocol/demo-capture-observations.json. Treasure chest: three official captures (2026-10-24 full tutorial, 2026-10-26 mage and warrior tutorials) show StartInteractionAnimReq(100/300) -> StartInteractionAnimNoti -> ExecuteInteractionReq at 2856-2938 ms -> ActivateAdventureObjectRes -> ItemsUpdateNoti (adventure_object_activate, one item row) -> InteractionAnimRes, then EndInteractionAnimReq -> InteractionAnimRes. In a 2026-10-26 local original-client trial the user reported being stuck at the chest; the server log (no payloads) shows a StartInteractionAnimReq answered with CommonErrorRes, no ExecuteInteractionReq, then a relog. Synthetic TutorialInteractionTest cases cover the captured order, the instance row, early execution, full inventory, missing item storage, reconnect and the start-rejection shape; the corrected chest has not yet been observed in the original client. Nuia Tears (2026-10-26): all 19 official P1/P2 activation requests join to authored spots and returned CMS IDs and to item-2000 adventure-object updates; requested positions are approximately 1026-8001 mm from authored points. The verified export has 137 placements, 119 CMS IDs and 30 map IDs (44 placements on 9012); catalog tiers are 1/5/10. Release chronicles-tests and chronicles-server built in out/build-chest. Nine focused CTests passed without skips (eight NuiaTears cases and NativeWorld.NuiaTearsCollectOncePerCharacterAndRestoreOverTls); three Python extraction/capture checks passed, including all 19 official associations. The TLS test verified the dispatcher position-gate fix for sessions without other gameplay services, independent characters, committed item/activation state, duplicate refusal and reconnect snapshot/no duplicate award. These are scoped synthetic results in the shared working tree, not a full-suite pass, deployment or original-client acceptance. Play-record counters/achievements remain outside this contract. Saved static research distinguishes the real 20077 offering sender, incremental thresholds and cumulative rewards from official P1 animation-10 activation (166 then delayed 20070, 91/167, then end/167) and P2 to_nui_flame teleport evidence. No official offering/74 or animation-16 success was observed. 2026-10-26 pre-commit source review inspected Nui statue/shrine, static-NPC and housing-product paths and their test sources. The parent reports an aggregate Python run of 137 cases: 136 passed, one environment-gated skip, across combat/processing/exploration/static-NPC/Nui/world-mob/GM-catalog/reference suites. This documentation pass did not execute C++ or an original-client trial. Native TLS, storage and stat test names below identify available checks, not newly observed passes; fresh aggregate C++ validation remains pending while external builders are active. Available checks include NuiStatue.*, NativeWorld.NuiStatueActivationPersistsAndRestoresWithoutTheTearService, CharacterStats.NuiBlessingAddsCumulativeCatalogRewardsAndExposesStoredBalances and Storage.*ShrineRevivalCommitsSupplyPositionAndLifeAtomically. Saved-death reconnect regression: three new cases fail on the deployed source baseline and 25 focused native world/tear/statue cases pass after the repair, including native TLS death presentation, duplicate StartPlaying suppression, unchanged dead progress before revival, completed shrine revival and a later observer seeing Idle with positive health. These are synthetic checks, not an original-client dead-reconnect trial. See docs/dead-reconnect.md. The final rebased Project Chronicles 0.2.7 Release C++ executable passed 1,036 cases with 94 environment-gated skips and zero failures; native HTTP/WebSocket/TLS smoke passed 39 checks. Independent source review found no remaining blockers. All five critical reconnect/discovery/revival CTest cases also pass on that baseline. Source layout move (phase 1a of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-modular-emulator-architecture-design.md): every src/ file moved into its module folder listed in tools/source_layout.json; only includes, src/CMakeLists.txt source paths and src/ path references changed. No packet, persistence or gameplay behavior changed. Dated verification records stay as written. Test split (phase 1b-2): these suites moved verbatim from the aggregated src/testing/tests.cpp when one test program per module replaced the chronicles-tests executable; suite and case names are unchanged. Checks: Release build and the full CTest run keep the same 1568 registered names with zero failures; tools.module_includes passes. Refactor: the monolithic PostgresStore was split into PostgresAccountRepository, PostgresCharacterRepository and PostgresCharacterStateRepository (src/persistence/postgres_repositories.hpp); method bodies, SQL text, revision guards and the character-row-first locking order moved verbatim, and migrate_postgres keeps advisory lock 7342091001. PostgresStore forwards all 36 repository methods and keeps its 15 feature methods unchanged; Release ctest passes 1572/1572 and both disposable-cluster PostgreSQL tools pass. Checks: full CTest (1573, 0 failures), the mail and market smoke tools, and the disposable-cluster PostgreSQL and reconnect tools. Refactor: Store drops the MarketRepository and RankingRepository bases and the facades drop the seven methods and the three feature tables; create_repositories builds MemoryMarketRepository and MemoryRankingRepository over the store's shared database (PostgreSQL builds the connection-string repositories), so one shared database, the escrow veto on character deletion and identical startup order are preserved. Checks: Release build, full CTest (1576, 0 failures), tools.module_includes, and the disposable-cluster PostgreSQL, reconnect and market smoke tools. Storage split (phase 2): Store now inherits only AccountRepository, CharacterRepository and CharacterStateRepository; MemoryStore and PostgresStore dropped the four mail methods and the last feature table, and MemoryStore registers no deletion hook because the recipient-mail erase moved into MemoryMailRepository's own hook on the shared database. create_repositories builds the mail repository over the shared MemoryDatabase in memory mode and over the shared connection string in postgres mode; MailRest, tutorial-completion delivery, WorldRepositories.mail and AdminServices.mail take the narrow interface. No behavior change. Checks: Release build, full CTest, the mail and market smoke tools, the disposable PostgreSQL and reconnect runs, tools.module_includes. The Store, MemoryStore and PostgresStore facades, character_repositories_of, the Store AuthService constructor and persistence/storage.hpp are deleted; callers use the account, character and character-state repositories over one shared MemoryDatabase or one PostgreSQL connection string, and tests use MemoryRepositories/make_postgres_character_repositories. Method bodies, SQL text, revision guards and locking order unchanged; assertions, suites and test names unchanged. Two comment lines only, equal line count/all other bytes exact; ALL and selected Project Chronicles checks pass. **Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`PC2S_NpcCaptionReq`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:npc_caption (x5.cms.EX5NpcCaption)
- **`PC2S_ActivateAdventureObjectReq`** — Nuia Tear subset: resolves a verified placement on the tracked map, atomically persists character-owned activation and item-2000 reward, then sends Activated response 91 and adventure_object_activate item update 169. Other adventure-object activation types remain unsupported; local original-client acceptance is pending. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:spot_object_id (uint64); 2:pos (x5.pb.WorldPos)
- **`PC2S_DiscoverAdventureObjectReq`** — Indexed tutorial map/object/quest/action scope only; shared-world and general interactions remain missing. Nuia Tears additionally support discovery, character-owned collection and reconnect snapshots through the verified placement index; other unindexed shared-world objects remain unsupported. Indexed Nui statues persist discovery and animation-10 activation without a tear/item reward, and restore saved object states on reconnect; flames remain revival destinations. Test sources were reviewed; no new original-client trial. Saved-death reconnect compatibility: automatic tear/statue discovery while dead is a mutation-free no-op within existing request-rate bounds. Explicit collection, activation, offerings and interaction refusals remain enforced. Ignoring this proximity report does not implement discovery or unindexed objects. Automatic discovery routing repair (2026-10-29): the Nuia Tear handler claims well-formed DiscoverAdventureObjectReq only for its indexed map/target. Other objects fall through without a target-error notification, progress access, reward, fabricated discovery or consumption of the tear request budget. Malformed requests retain bounded BadRequest validation; explicit activation, known-tear distance checks, statue ownership and tutorial routing are preserved. This does not implement unsupported adventure-object types. Automatic discovery range repair (2026-11-01): tutorial/shared adventure objects, Tears and statues accept reports within 100 m horizontally plus the 5 m position tolerance, ignoring height, matching the observed client trigger; farther reports keep TooFar. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:spot_object_id (uint64); 2:pos (x5.pb.WorldPos)
- **`PC2S_CutSceneEndReq`** — Tutorial cutscene follow-ups; in the shared world the end of a travel cutscene restores the visible channel of invisible cutscenes or, when its CutScene row names an end point, moves the character there with MapMoveStartNoti (captured position, else the end point's single placed doodad (Candidate), else the travel arrival rule (CUSTOM); raid end maps are left to the raid service). Cliffs gate scene 1565 completes the pending entrance handoff. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:cut_scene_id (int32)
- **`PC2S_DialogueStartReq`** — Tutorial NPC dialogue, crafting stations, and shared-world quest NPCs announced to the session. The non-tutorial shop-open dialogue exchange is not implemented. Trade-manager NPCs on shared maps open the trade dialogue. Crafting stations placed on a housing lot resolve through the requester's lot and channel (synthetic TLS only, 2026-11-02). Schema file: `p_c2s.interaction.proto`. ## Inventory, equipment, currency and utility bag

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Item snapshots/deltas, equipment swaps, discard, money and quick-slot allocations.

**Current implementation**

- Owned persistent item instances, stackables, gold, equip swaps and validated batch discard exist.
- PARTIAL item skills (docs/item-use.md): the recovered StartSkillReq use_item path now owns tutorial and shared-field consumables, including maps without NPC populations. The mapped Item skill must name its positive owned stack and no item instance. Empty quantity returns 13 with skill/instance identifiers and no 53/14 animation start. The catalog useItem event commits one stack unit and the first matching quick-slot reservation under the current progress revision before notification/effects. Failed commits do not mark an item spent. Recovery, buffs, projectiles, abnormal-gauge cures and area effects retain their existing recovered/Candidate policies. Unsupported item kinds and profiles without item-skill data remain partial; network latency can permit predicted client frames.
- CANDIDATE PC2S_ItemUseReq (20077, never captured; docs/item-effects.md): draw boxes (80 items, Item.FK_drawBoxId) spend one box and grant its DrawBox rows (rows without drawWeight always, one weighted pick among the rest, uniform quantity) as gold, Hersander Tokens, stacks, housing objects or equipment instances in free slots, in one revision-guarded commit; effect consumables (Item.FK_skillEffectList, the four FGT foods) spend the item, then apply their effects through the combat session (private tutorial instance only). Summon registrations stay with the companion session. Reply: ItemsUpdateNoti with the use reason; refusals answer the common error and change nothing. src/world/features/item_use/item_use.cpp; ItemUse tests, no network-path test.
- Utility bag (quick item slots 1-4, docs/inventory-equipment.md): the tutorial session and the shared-world session apply UtilityBagSetReq through one helper (src/world/features/inventory/utility_bag.cpp): at most four entries for slots 0-3, applied in order so a slot named again takes its last entry (the client repeats the target slot when the item or its utilityBagGroup is already in the bag), catalog bag-eligible items (Item.FK_utilityBagFullFillCnt; the shared world reads the client catalog Item table, the tutorial the same rule exported as its profile's utility_items) and reservations bounded by owned stacks. Validation refusals answer CommonErrorRes BadRequest or Interaction_ConditionsNotMatch; shared-world NPC combat also returns UtilityBag_InCombat. Refused requests change nothing. Shared-world requests commit through the progress revision before UtilityBagSetRes 104, and a shared-world entry whose saved bag has any assigned slot sends WorldCharUtilityBagNoti 140 once per connection. Tutorial and shared-field item-skill spends decrement the first slot holding the item; ItemUseReq spends lower reservations that the remaining stack no longer covers.
- Carried weight drives a movement-speed penalty. InventoryCapacity measures the weight (owned items and stackables against the equipped bag safeWeight, otherwise BagDefaultSafeWeight) and EncumbranceRules classifies it: unencumbered up to the safe weight, Heavy (status 50030004, MoveSpeedRate -500) in the lower half of the overweight band, VeryHeavy (status 50030005, MoveSpeedRate -1500, clamped to the catalog minimum 200) from InvWeightMoveSpeedStep2RatioFrom of that band on. The band runs from the safe weight to safe * BagMaxWeightMultiplier percent. The thresholds are Candidate; the statuses, their stat modifiers and the stat limits are catalog values.
- A slot-only ItemEquipReq (item_id absent or 0) vacates the slot through InventoryRules::bare_unequip and answers with the observed item update without an equip slot (169) and equipment update without item_cms_id (168); an empty slot is a silent no-op, a stale revision leaves the state unchanged, and the Bag slot has no verified server rule.
- Carried weight is measured by InventoryRules::compute_weight with checked int64 arithmetic: negative inputs and overflow are rejected and an equipped bag replaces the default safe weight. The world session re-measures after every packet batch that carries an ItemsUpdateNoti (169) and on world entry, so every inventory path (loot, shop, quest, gathering, crafting, equip, discard, GM grants) is covered. A tier change sends ChangeStatNoti (stat 84, SCS_StatusEffect), then RemoveStatusEffectNoti of the old tier and AddStatusEffectNoti of the new one (level 1, stack 1, permanent expire_tick INT64_MAX as observed for catalog-durationless statuses, instance ids from 0x40000000 so they never collide with combat statuses). Equipment, trade and tempering stat refreshes keep the applied tier. No weight-limit refusal code is enforced because none was observed.
- Hersander Token balance is a revision-guarded WorldProgress field persisted by schema version 10; Gold and Hersander Token share the 0 to 9,000,000,000,000,000 catalog Money limit; out-of-range values are rejected before the write.
- Gold rewards are credited through the currency module on a working copy that commits only if every reward succeeds; overflow past the catalog limit is refused with the existing BadRequest code (no money-specific wire code is established). Candidate: the entry money snapshot (126) carries the persisted Hersander Token balance as key 1 only when nonzero; this rests on a single captured snapshot and is not a proven wire rule.
- Schema version 11 adds a database CHECK that emulator_characters.gold stays within the catalog Gold limit (9,000,000,000,000,000), the same bound the currency module and the world-progress validation enforce. Author result: Storage.PostgresGoldColumnRejectsValuesAboveCatalogLimit and the migration applied twice on the disposable cluster; independent reviewer full CTest 253 registered, 0 failed, 11 named skips, PostgreSQL main 8/8, news 4/4, portal 4/4. Deployment must run the read-only production Gold preflight (npc-runtime/v11-gold-preflight.sql) before the migration.
- PARTIAL item tempering (ItemPolishReq 20075, persisted polish_step 0..15). The server rolls the ItemPolish row of the next step itself (success, fail, destruction in parts per 10000): success raises the step, fail keeps it, destruction deletes the unequipped item; every outcome charges the stone, an optional additive and gold in one commit under the character revision (MemoryStore and PostgreSQL), and every refusal happens before any roll or write. The cap is the smaller of the client's ItemPolish maximum for the item's grade and category (AAC_ItemPolish_GetMaxStepForItem), its increase table and storage. Reply: one 169 with the item (destruction: item_id only, which the client removes, AAC_Inventory_ApplyItemUpdate), money_changes, remaining stone/additive stacks and the polish reason; success keeps the observed empty marker, fail/destruction name the ItemRollResult. An equipped success adds 47 (every changed stat plus vitals) and 168; the six captured weapon attack frames still reproduce. Candidate parts: Fail charging the full cost, the refusal codes (ItemIdInvalid, ItemPolish_Invalid, _Damaged for zero durability, _StepIsMax, _InvalidAdditiveMaterial, _RequireUnEquip when destruction is possible on worn gear, ItemCountError, MoneyNotEnough), additive math (AddSuccessPercent adds percentage points taken from fail then destruction; DestructionProhibition turns destruction into fail) and 47 after an equipped armor success. The shipping widget sends item_id only (AAC_ItemPolishWidget_SendItemPolishReq), so additives are server-only; no catalog row has a destruction chance and no item has polishResidueId.
- Inventory slot allocation is shared by corpse loot and item-use reward planning. The existing lowest-free-slot/capacity contract is preserved; this also repairs the missing item-use helper that prevented compilation in the shared checkout.
- Nui statue refill conserves owned stacks while reallocating utility-slot reservations against recovered item/group/equipped-bag capacity tiers. Targeted item-2000 offerings atomically spend stack units and persist blessing state before notifications; generic boxes/effect consumables remain in their existing item-use handler.
- Second weapon repair (2026-10-29): weapon instances accept Weapon_1 or Weapon_2 despite the catalog default slot, preserving ownership/class/level/durability checks and both equipped instances. Moving an equipped weapon clears its old visual slot. WeaponSlotActivationReq 20078 validates an equipped healthy weapon and idle/live state, commits active_weapon_slot under the progress revision, then sends 172 and changed stats without healing spent HP/SP. Duplicate selection is a no-op; failures report the current slot because the recovered client applies it on failure too. Combat validates the selected weapon; skill packets, lobby, inventory/PlayerNub, nearby and late-join equipment snapshots carry its selection. Additive schema 34 persists it with a 0/1 bound in Memory/PostgreSQL.
- InventorySession::select_weapon_for_skill shares the ActivateWeaponReq slot rules (owned, durable weapon in Weapon_1/Weapon_2, alive, revision-guarded commit, stat refresh) but does not refuse while a combat action is open, because the SwapWeapon skill start that follows decides cancelability.
- Shared-world Utility Pouch edits return UtilityBag_InCombat while an NPC is engaged with the player. Re-equipping an already-assigned slot refills up to the requested count from owned items not reserved in other slots. PvP combat-state coverage and original-client acceptance remain unverified.
- Inactive item-use receipt primitives prepare a canonical inventory transition and response without mutating progress. Memory and PostgreSQL reserve a caller-retained expected sequence and nonce, fence the owner epoch, compare the authoritative progress snapshot, atomically commit the spend with its receipt, and permit exact replay or character-scoped lookup. One pending or last receipt and its sequence high-water mark are retained per character; pending receipts prevent character deletion. Existing item consumption shares the same utility-slot decrement logic. These primitives are not connected to native combat.

**Custom / guessed behavior (not official)**

Our own guesses, because the data to reproduce the official behavior does not exist. They add no capture evidence and do not promote any status.

- Shared-world WorldCharUtilityBagNoti 140 is placed after the quest snapshot at the first time sync, following the tutorial snapshot's order, and is omitted for an empty bag (the client's initial state); the official shared-world position and empty-bag behavior of this frame are unobserved.
- After an ItemUseReq spend lowers a utility-slot reservation, the committed bag is announced with UtilityBagSetRes 104, as the Nui statue refill does; no official frame shows how the client learns a lowered count on this path.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- ItemUseReq 20077 has no official capture: draw rules, reply and refusal codes remain Candidate. Food/effect-list consumables require their separately installed combat effect binding; this repair validates mapped StartSkillReq item skills. Unsupported item kinds, disassembly integration, item options/sockets and all delta reasons remain unfinished.
- Weight-limit rejection, complete capacity semantics and secondary/premium currency need evidence and implementation; the movement-speed penalty is implemented.
- Weight-limit refusals and their error codes (ItemWeightLimit 1004, ItemNotEnoughFreeWeight 1024, Npc_LootOverMaxWeight 6006) remain unobserved and are not enforced; InvWeightSpRegenPenaltyRate and WeightPenaltyState (900) are not applied. No capture crosses a weight threshold, so the tier boundaries, the packet order between two tiers and the instance numbering are Candidate, and original-client acceptance of the encumbrance debuff has not been observed.
- No gameplay source grants or spends Hersander Tokens; Blue Salt has no verified mutation rules and other secondary/premium currencies are not implemented.
- Official weapon-switch delay and switching during actions are unrecovered; the bounded local policy acknowledges eligible idle switches immediately. Original-client weapon HUD, both-weapon combat and animation acceptance remain pending. Disassembly, item options/sockets and all delta reasons remain unfinished.
- Tempering: no Fail, Destruction, refusal or additive frame was captured; polish recovery (Reason_PolishRecovery) has no request message and no client text use in this build, polishResidueId grants are not modelled (a destruction that would need one is refused), and the blacksmith dialogue route (OpenPolish) is client-side only.
- Utility bag: official UtilityBag_* group and capacity refusals (17001-17008) and UtilityBagFullFillCnt maximums are not enforced on set requests. Original-client display and empty-item animation timing remain unverified; shared-field consumption and reservation clearing now have native TLS coverage.
- The item-use receipt does not persist the combat target, effects or continuation. Native combat and character admission do not yet own, fence and recover that continuation or prevent later inventory mutations while an operation is pending; the primitive must remain inactive until those lifecycle guarantees are implemented and reviewed. The inactive schema-45 experiment and its test/rollback scripts have been retired from the fresh-install distribution. The baseline remains schema 44; this primitive is not enabled by database installation. No original-client acceptance is claimed.
- The historical raw research artifacts previously linked here are no longer present in this checkout after workspace cleanup. Existing historical findings are retained as recorded evidence, not newly reproduced analysis.

Gameplay repairs 2026-10-29: Release build succeeds; default CTest 1989 registered, 1866 passed, 123 optional skips, zero failures. Disposable PostgreSQL migration/account checks and 11 repository cases pass. Generated-profile native TLS checks pass: last shared-field potion and empty retry; first/second weapon equip/activation/reconnect; authored checkpoint, spatial map-9021 crossing and same-map recovery, all preserving committed state. Four spatial export tests and 14 MapChannels cases pass. The selected-weapon combat regression verifies weapon-specific skill eligibility and slot notifications. Twenty-five client functions were annotated, indexed and saved to the matching IDB. These are server/synthetic checks; original-client animation, UI recovery and audible speech acceptance remain pending. Protocol Page synchronization is blocked by its existing document-size limit; its verified publication fingerprint remains unchanged. See docs/gameplay-repairs-20261029.md. World coverage repair 2026-10-29: synthetic tests MapChannels (16), GmFeatureTest teleport routing, NpcFeature map populations, WeaponSwapOwner (3), WorldQuests reward relaxation, exporter tests (static NPC 11, world mobs 9, combat data); real-catalog CTest with the regenerated data loads 200 monster maps, 2,584 static targets and 52 population maps. Original-client weapon switching, regional populations and teleports are not yet observed. November 2026 gameplay repair: focused synthetic tests exercise the changed paths; no original-client acceptance or live deployment is claimed. Current candidate synthetic inventory and utility-bag tests cover NPC-combat refusal and same-slot refill from unreserved stock; this is not original-client acceptance. Inactive item-use receipt checkpoint (2026-11-02): the fresh memory receipt test passed, including same-revision incorrect stack, utility-slot and scalar snapshots; a changed stack between reserve and commit; sequence replay, older/skipped sequences, concurrent calls, owner takeover and deletion. Four inventory skill-item cases passed, including multi-slot and response parity, absent/empty stacks and revision exhaustion; one tutorial plan test passed. In a disposable PostgreSQL cluster, the equivalent receipt test passed, and two proxy cases dropped the actual reservation and commit COMMIT acknowledgements and verified exact replay. Separate test processes recovered pending receipts after a PostgreSQL stop/start and after a v45 backup and restore. A separate quiescent v44 backup was upgraded to v45; the rollback guard refused an in-place downgrade, and restoration to another disposable database confirmed v45 and a post-backup sentinel were absent. This tests the isolated restore procedure, not a production migration or recovery of combat effects; no original-client trial was performed.

**Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`PC2S_ItemDiscardReq`** — Owned persistent equip/discard or tutorial inventory subset; mixed-use packet has unimplemented reasons and item modifiers. Schema file: `p_c2s.item.proto`. Fields: 1:identity_list (repeated x5.pb.ItemIdentity)
- **`PC2S_ItemEquipReq`** — Owned persistent equip/discard and slot-only bare unequip (item_id absent or 0) for the bounded subset; mixed-use packet has unimplemented reasons and item modifiers. Weapons accept both Weapon_1 and Weapon_2; moving slots clears the old visual slot. Owned/class/level/durability checks and atomic equip persistence remain enforced. Schema file: `p_c2s.item.proto`. Fields: 1:slot (x5.cms.EX5EquipSlotType); 2:item_id (sfixed64); 15:packet_seq (x5.pb.PacketSeq)
- **`PC2S_ItemUseReq`** — Never captured. Summon-registration consumables are handled by the companion session; draw boxes and effect consumables (Candidate) by the item-use session (docs/item-effects.md). Other skill-less items are refused. Targeted item-2000 shrine offerings are routed first to NuiStatueSession: owned stacks, bounded counts, exact nearby authored target and revisioned tear/blessing update; nonzero item-instance selectors and quick-slot use are refused. The real sender is recovered statically, but offering success/ordering/UI acceptance are unobserved. Recipe items spend one owned item and record the learned craft once (schema 35). A registration item is refused while its registration animation is pending. Items only a quest objective uses (CounterUseItem, UseItemInTriggerVolume) are spent and reported to quests (2026-10-30). Schema file: `p_c2s.item.proto`. Fields: 1:item_cms_id (int32); 2:item_id (sfixed64); 3:count (int32); 4:target_unit_id (uint64); 5:use_quick_slot (bool); 15:packet_seq (x5.pb.PacketSeq)
- **`PC2S_WeaponSlotActivationReq`** — Eligible idle selection of an equipped healthy weapon persists active slot 0/1 before 172 and stat refresh, without healing. Duplicate requests are no-ops; failure reports current selection. Nearby/late-join snapshots and reconnect retain selection. Official delay/action-switch policy and original-client acceptance remain unverified; docs/gameplay-repairs-20261029.md. Schema file: `p_c2s.item.proto`. Fields: 1:slot (x5.cms.EX5EquipSlotType)
- **`PC2S_UtilityBagSetReq`** — Tutorial and shared-world sessions validate and persist the four quick item slots through src/world/features/inventory/utility_bag.cpp: catalog bag-eligible items, at most four entries for slots 0-3 applied in order (a repeated slot takes its last entry, as the client sends when re-assigning an item already in the bag), non-negative counts and reservations bounded by owned stacks; refusals use the local codes BadRequest and Interaction_ConditionsNotMatch. UtilityBag_InCombat is returned while an NPC is engaged; group and capacity limits remain unenforced. Existing-slot refills clamp to available owned items. PvP combat-state coverage remains unverified. Original-client shared-world acceptance unverified. Schema file: `p_c2s.item.proto`. Fields: 1:slots (repeated x5.pb.UtilityBagSlot)
- **`PS2C_UtilityBagSetRes`** — Answers accepted tutorial and shared-world set requests with the committed bag. Also carries committed statue-refill and authored shrine-revival utility reservations; quantities are bounded by owned stacks and recovered bag capacity tiers, with no invented inventory refill. Candidate: sent after an ItemUseReq spend lowers an unbacked reservation. Original-client acceptance unverified. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode); 2:bag (x5.pb.UtilityBag)
- **`PS2C_WorldCharMoneyNoti`** — Owned persistent equip/discard or tutorial inventory subset; mixed-use packet has unimplemented reasons and item modifiers. Schema file: `p_s2c.character.proto`. Fields: 1:update (bool); 2:money (x5.pb.DbCharacterMoney); 3:blue_salt (int64)
- **`PS2C_WorldCharItemsNoti`** — Owned persistent equip/discard or tutorial inventory subset; mixed-use packet has unimplemented reasons and item modifiers. Schema file: `p_s2c.character.proto`. Fields: 1:weapon_slot (x5.cms.EX5EquipSlotType); 2:items (repeated x5.pb.Item); 3:stackables (repeated x5.pb.ItemStackable); 4:update (bool); 5:has_more (bool)
- **`PS2C_WorldCharUtilityBagNoti`** — Carries the saved bag in the tutorial time-sync snapshot and, for a shared-world entry whose saved bag has any assigned slot, once per connection after the quest snapshot (local order; an empty bag is not announced). Original-client display after a shared-world rejoin unverified. Schema file: `p_s2c.character.proto`. Fields: 1:bag (x5.pb.UtilityBag)
- **`PS2C_EquipmentsUpdateNoti`** — Owned persistent equip/discard or tutorial inventory subset including the observed equipment update without item_cms_id after bare unequip; mixed-use packet has unimplemented reasons and item modifiers. Schema file: `p_s2c.item.proto`. Fields: 1:packet_seq (x5.pb.PacketSeq); 2:unit_id (uint64); 3:equipments (repeated x5.pb.Equipment); 4:equip_slot_types (uint32)
- **`PS2C_ItemsUpdateNoti`** — Owned persistent equip/discard or tutorial inventory subset including the observed item update without equip slot after bare unequip; mixed-use packet has unimplemented reasons and item modifiers. NPC merchant trades use reason shop for buy, sell and repair (observed), housing_items counts and money_type for Hersander Token (Candidate), and a discard update removes a sold voucher (Candidate pairing). The looting reason is emitted for corpse loot (items, stackables, money). The polish reason is emitted for tempering: an empty marker on success (as captured) and result Fail or Destruction otherwise, with an item_id-only entry for a destroyed item. Item use emits the stack update with the utility_bag reason at the useItem event, as observed after official item uses. Reasons use (summon registration), trade_loading, trade_sell and trade_voucher for trade runs. The adventure_object_activate reason carries new item instances for tutorial equipment rewards (the treasure chest's necklace), filled with the committed row ids. Housing charges, storage installs and refunds use the Housing reason with housing_items rows (Candidate; synthetic only). Mail claims use system.account_mail_id or system.char_mail_id with committed instances and resulting balances/quantities. Nuia Tears use adventure_object_activate with the committed resulting stackable item-2000 quantity (official captured shape). Gathering emits system (placements, ExpertiseReward doodads) or looting naming the doodad (LootingPack doodads) with new stack totals, plus the worn tool row for tool gathers. The Cliffs prison key is an item instance, consumed by the door after an atomic item trade. CUSTOM (guessed, not official): The looting reason also carries guessed kill gold, polished equipment and full moon stone drops. Schema file: `p_s2c.item.proto`. ## Corpse loot and reward ownership

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Loot eligibility, corpse requests/results and item/money grants.

**Current implementation**

- Tutorial-instance monsters roll corpse loot once at death from Npc.FK_lootPackId (LootPack, LootCondition, LootItem). The killer's corpse announces has_chance_to_loot ahead of the Demise state and death, as in the captures, even when the roll is empty.
- PC2S_LootItemReq is answered with exactly one PS2C_LootItemRes. A take needs an unexpired corpse owned by the character, within GameVariable.LootingRange (plus the custom tolerance below), that has not been taken. Gold, stacks and item instances then commit atomically under the character's progress revision (the tutorial session adopts it) and are reported as ItemsUpdateNoti.looting with resulting stack totals, followed by cleared loot flags.
- Refusals (ownership, range, empty or repeated take, stack/gold/slot overflow, optional weight policy, storage conflict or failure) write nothing and leave the corpse lootable; a successful take cannot repeat.
- A corpse with loot is removed from the client after NpcCorpseLootingDestroyMillis, or NpcCorpseNoneDestroyMillis after a take; combat's default removal covers other monsters and is not duplicated for these.
- tools/build_loot_data.py (format 2) emits 513 loot packs, 8 handling packs and 310 items for 3,215 monster NPCs, tags every group that depends on a custom rule with that rule's name, and lists the 25 groups no rule covers instead of dropping them wrongly.
- World monsters (2026-10-26): shared authoritative populations export 2,802 slots on 106 populated maps (196 definitions), including 417 on 9012 and 812 on 9031, with 470 authored patrols and 1,893 actions. Public clients share health, aggro/action ownership, damage, death and respawn. Raid channels use independent populations keyed by actual channel ID. Current-pose sight, bounded visual journals, fresh life IDs, one-time slots, corpse expiry, killer-owned loot, server HuntMonster credit and EXP are wired. GM test NPCs remain private. See docs/world-mobs.md. Catalog Instance maps use per-character monster populations; party-instance admission remains unrecovered.
- World-mob correction (2026-10-26): typed wire identities now fit 32 bits because client MoveNoti actor lookup clears the high dword. Separate server-only random receipt IDs preserve durable HuntMonster credit. Roaming-enabled pathless NPCs get bounded local idle walks (687 slots, including 163 on map 9012 and all 21 Meadow Wolf slots); authored patrols remain distinct. Combat/return/death/GM pause suspend walks, and fresh lives reset at home. Explicit player skill targets use the live/attackable/private-ownership predicate. See docs/world-mobs.md.
- Corpse butchering (2026-10-30, captured wavesword-mob-combat-20261026): a monster whose Npc.FK_expertiseRewardId authors a loot pack is a handling-loot candidate. Its world-mob nub carries npc.is_handling_loot_candidate, the killer's death announcement carries possible_handling_loot, and the corpse stays NpcCorpseLootingDestroyMillis (90 s) until butchered, also after an ordinary take; a butchered corpse expires NpcCorpseNoneDestroyMillis (10 s) later, matching the captured 10.1-10.8 s removals. LootSession owns these corpse rights; GatheringSession runs the knife interaction (animation 1000) and its reward.
- Full-wallet loot (2026-11-01): CUSTOM: kill gold above the wallet limit stays behind and the corpse's items are still taken; the reported money change is the amount credited. Before, a graduated character with the full test-kit wallet could not loot any corpse that carried kill gold, including quest drops. Tests: LootSessionTest.OverflowingCountsAreRefusedAndGoldStopsAtTheWalletLimit and KillGoldStopsAtTheWalletLimitWithoutRefusingTheTake.
- The Cliffs prison-key quest item 120109 is exported as an individual item with durability 1, matching the official P2 adventure-object reward; the prison-door interaction consumes the owned instance transactionally. Synthetic tests cover item generation and consumption.
- Ordinary durable loot claims (2026-11-02): a world repository with an acquired or adopted owner epoch validates that epoch before claim insertion or replay. PostgreSQL holds the existing owner-row share lock through the claim transaction, so takeover waits for the old transaction and rejects later stale-owner claims; the memory backend checks under its database mutex. The production server acquires an epoch before opening listeners.

**Custom / guessed behavior (not official)**

Our own guesses, because the data to reproduce the official behavior does not exist. They add no capture evidence and do not promote any status.

- Every item below is our own guess; none has capture or client evidence. Each rule has a switch (--loot-custom-rules off, or --loot-rules-file {"custom_rules": {...}}; all on by default), the server logs the active rules once at startup, and docs/monster-loot.md lists each guess with its evidence.
- kill_gold: every monster pays gold with its corpse, fitted per NPC template grade as round(base + per_level * level) to 23 captured samples (exact for Weak/Normal/Strong, within 1 for Elite and 6 for Boss; Boss_A/C/S reuse Boss_B). The official server pays it at the kill; the emulator pays it with the corpse take.
- first_kill_rewards: groups filtered by lootingClass or FK_PlayRecord_End drop only on a character's first looted kill of that NPC, persisted in WorldProgress.loot_first_kills (table emulator_character_loot_first_kills, schema version 22).
- quest_gated_rows: Item.questLooting and QuestItem rows drop only while a listed quest is active; quest IDs missing from the client's Quest table fall back to no gate.
- full_moon_stones: FullMoonStone rows drop as ordinary stackable items.
- polish_step_rows: LootItem.polishStep is the polish step of the dropped equipment instance.
- handling_loot: Npc.FK_handlingLootPackId is a second pack rolled at Npc.handlingRate, taken with the ordinary loot request, announced with possible_handling_loot.
- party_shared_loot: connected party members in the killer's instance within 30 m share a corpse; the first eligible member to take it receives everything, and the others are told with a cleared flag. Dormant in production: monsters exist only in private tutorial instances, so the audience is empty.
- Guessed details, each a named constant or key: 2 m range tolerance; Npc_HasNoLoot for a repeated take; ItemSlotLimit, ItemCountError and Npc_LootOverMaxWeight for capacity refusals; a successful reply when nothing dropped; corpse lifetimes of 90 s from the death and 10 s from the take (or the death, by configuration).

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Official behavior behind the custom rules is unknown: the real kill-gold formula and its timing, first-kill and PlayRecord triggers, quest-gate semantics, the role of Npc.FK_handlingLootPackId (now only joined to the ordinary take), party loot policy, range rule, capacity errors and corpse timer anchors are not captured. Party members cannot butcher a shared kill.
- Groups using contributionType, FK_PlayRecord_Start, WayPoint, Memo or CraftRecipe rows (25 groups) never drop. There is no contribution or public loot model.
- World monsters now produce killer-owned corpse loot. Shared-world party distribution and contribution remain unfinished.
- No evidenced weight rule exists, so Npc_LootOverMaxWeight has a tested policy hook that production leaves unset. Item rows have no affixes or sockets.
- The original client has not been observed looting against this emulator. The new disposable PostgreSQL checks cover ordinary loot receipts and owner fencing, not original-client gameplay or the first-kill path; the command-line options have no unit test.
- A zero-epoch direct repository remains available for trusted offline and legacy callers. It is not a fence against an arbitrary unleased writer while a world server is active; world startup must acquire its positive owner epoch.
- World-mob fidelity is partial: 154 source layers are absent; inactive/time/quest/event spawners, navigation/collision, full threat/group linkage, phase conditions/chains, boss scripts, party contribution rewards and transient encounter crash recovery remain unfinished. Weighted slots, maximum populations, maximum respawn delay and faction behavior are local policies. 765 types use custom fallback stats; one placed type lacks complete locomotion. The tested mob artifact replaced the loopback service on 2026-10-26; both listeners and all 196 loaded map definitions were verified, with PostgreSQL staying online. Missing character columns required the backed-up additive migration 29; storage-backed admin checks then passed. Original-client acceptance remains pending; full-world completeness is not claimed.

**Evidence and verification**

**Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`PC2S_LootItemReq`** — Handled for monster corpses in the private tutorial instance only, with ownership, range, expiry, capacity and double-take checks. Synthetic tests only; the original client has not been observed using it against this emulator. World-mob update: shared map/channel combat, fresh life IDs, killer-owned loot and server hunt/EXP events are wired. Original-client acceptance and full scripted encounters remain pending; see docs/world-mobs.md. CUSTOM (guessed, not official): The range tolerance and the first-come party take of a shared corpse are guesses, switchable through the loot rules file. Schema file: `p_c2s.item.proto`. Fields: 1:unit_id (uint64); 15:packet_seq (x5.pb.PacketSeq)
- **`PS2C_LootItemRes`** — Sent once per request: success carries no ec; Action_InvalidLootingRange is captured. Tutorial instance only. World-mob update: shared map/channel combat, fresh life IDs, killer-owned loot and server hunt/EXP events are wired. Original-client acceptance and full scripted encounters remain pending; see docs/world-mobs.md. CUSTOM (guessed, not official): Npc_InvalidId, Npc_ImpossibleLoot, Npc_HasNoLoot, Npc_FailLootTransaction, ItemSlotLimit, ItemCountError and Npc_LootOverMaxWeight (weight rule not wired) are unobserved choices; the repeated-take, capacity and nothing-dropped replies are configurable. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode); 2:unit_id (uint64); 15:packet_seq (x5.pb.PacketSeq)
- **`PS2C_UnitLootItemInfoNoti`** — has_chance_to_loot is sent at the kill for the killer's corpse with loot facts, and a both-flags-clear update after a take, as captured. World-mob update: shared map/channel combat, fresh life IDs, killer-owned loot and server hunt/EXP events are wired. Original-client acceptance and full scripted encounters remain pending; see docs/world-mobs.md. possible_handling_loot (captured) marks a corpse its killer may butcher; it stays set after an ordinary take and clears after butchering. CUSTOM (guessed, not official): has_chance_to_loot is also sent for NPCs that only pay guessed kill gold and for the guessed Npc.FK_handlingLootPackId pack, and party members near a kill receive has_chance_to_loot. Schema file: `p_s2c.item.proto`. Fields: 1:unit_id (uint64); 2:possible_handling_loot (bool); 3:has_chance_to_loot (bool)

## NPC shops, sales and repairs

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

NPC merchants: shop open, buy and sell in Gold or Hersander Token, durability repair, housing objects, trade-voucher purchase and sale, purchase limits and condition checks.

**Current implementation**

- One catalog-backed service (src/world/features/shop/npc_shop.*, src/data/shop_catalog.*, src/data/shop_conditions.*) handles PC2S_InteractUnitReq param.shop (open, buy_list, sell_list), param.repair and param.voucher_group. The target resolves through this session's announced UnitRegistry actors or its exact optional authored map-scoped static-NPC index, the NPC template's interaction group must contain the interaction (Npc.interactionGroupId -> Interaction.groupId), the request kind must match the interaction kind, and the server-tracked position must be within 7 m. Rejections use PS2C_CommonErrorRes with distinct codes (Interaction_TargetNotFound, GroupIdNotMatch, InvalidParamType, ConditionsNotMatch, TooFar, MoneyNotEnough, ItemCountError, ItemSlotLimit, PurchaseLimitExceeded, ItemWeightLimit, ItemNonSellable, ItemEquipped, ItemLocked, ItemNotNpcRepairable, ItemNotRepairable). The former always-refusing gate is removed.
- Observed (official captures: 5 opens, 4 buys, 3 sales): open answers InteractUnitRes then ShopItemLimitNoti; trades answer ItemsUpdateNoti (reason shop) then InteractUnitRes. Prices reproduce exactly: Item.priceValue x Shop.priceMultiplierPerMille / 1000 x count and refunds Item.refundValue x count; an opt-in test replays every captured amount from the hash-checked export.
- Repair (observed: 5 requests; per-item rounding up reproduces the captured totals of 5 and 207 gold): ceil(ItemRepairCost.costValue x missing durability / Item.maxDurability) per item; undamaged items in a repair-all list are skipped; durability is restored under an expected-value guard in the same transaction as the gold. The tool-class proportion (max 2000) is unobserved.
- Conditions are evaluated, not rejected: Interaction.FK_conditionId (condition 704, the only one on shop interactions, is PioneerPermit false OR true and holds for everyone), Shop.fk_shopItemCondition (ShopItemCondition 13/14/15: BlueSalt company level) and VoucherCondition. Sessions supply the character's company standing and pioneer permit; goods whose condition fails answer Interaction_ConditionsNotMatch, and an unknown condition kind answers Interaction_InvalidData.
- Hersander Token prices and refunds use the currency module (separate balance, Money.limitUserMax cap, overflow-checked); one request may charge both currencies. The wire uses MoneyChange.money_type for tokens (shape observed once for an adventure object; no token shop spend was captured).
- Housing objects (428 Gold and 2 token goods) are stored as housing item counts (WorldProgress::housing_items, shared with the housing service) and reported through ItemsUpdateNoti.housing_items. Candidate: no housing purchase frame was captured.
- Trade vouchers (Candidate, no capture): VoucherGroup interactions issue vouchers under the trade-run rules when the trade catalog is loaded (production fee and materials, validPeriod minutes, own limit; docs/vehicles-and-trade.md) and a basicValue/validPeriod-hours fallback otherwise; sold vouchers refund basicValue x TradeRefundBasisPoints / 10000. Client list handling is grounded in IDA (ApplyVoucherDelta: good_cms_id != 0 appends, == 0 removes by id; reasons trade_voucher and discard).
- Purchases are bounded by a Candidate weight ceiling (safe weight x BagMaxWeightMultiplier / 100, ItemWeightLimit 1004; the encumbrance feature uses the same reading) and bought equipment carries created_epochtime, durability and grade like the captured purchase (created time persisted in schema v15).
- Gold, Hersander Token, stack/housing counts, purchase-limit counters, vouchers, item rows and repairs commit in one revisioned transaction (Store::commit_item_trade, memory and PostgreSQL, schema v12 and v15); stale revisions, stale wear, equipped removals and slot collisions roll everything back and a retried request cannot pay twice. Each session accepts eight authorized shop requests per second.
- Prerequisite modules (not merchant features by themselves): UnitRegistry (src/world/core/unit_registry.*), NpcInteractionIndex and NpcPopulation. The map-9012 placement file holds 23 shop, 10 repair and 3 voucher NPCs; a character whose persisted position is on map 9012 receives them.
- Client-owned static NPCs have a separate optional MapStaticNpcs interaction index. The verified exporter admits unambiguous initially active single-point staticNpcData placements on Release or Demo ArcheWorld Field/HousingArea maps (Demo covers the reachable Shining Shore public channels 9011/9012), with unit kind 7 and authored sector/local identity. Native dialogue/shop target resolution falls back to this exact map-scoped index while retaining catalog interaction and range checks. It emits no duplicate UnitAddNoti, creates no ordinary UnitRegistry entry and does not implement static activation or AI. Missing exports leave this optional interaction path disabled.
- HousingBuildingDrawing purchases use stackable inventory instead of housing-item/installed storage. Catalog conditions, currency/capacity checks and the existing atomic trade commit remain mandatory; new goods are not unconditionally unlocked.
- Scheduled static-NPC identity repair (2026-10-29): day/night client-owned actors are included in the authored interaction index instead of being discarded for startGameTime/endGameTime. The regenerated profile has 1428 map-scoped targets and preserves all 726 previous targets. This restores supported Harbor City vendor operations through the existing map/template/range/catalog and atomic item/gold checks without spawning duplicate actors. The client owns scheduled appearance; independent server opening-hour enforcement remains unimplemented. Weather-dependent, disabled, adventure-controlled and ambiguous placements remain excluded.
- Static world-layer repair (2026-10-29): ArcheWorld's always-loaded Static data layers (village NPCs such as Romeline 1002232 in Ruins of Gold) are now exported for each supported public map whose authored area contains the placement; test layers are excluded and the identity, activation, single-candidate and single-position rules are unchanged. The regenerated profile has 2459 targets on 9 maps (9021 rose from 5 to 466) and keeps all 1428 previous targets unchanged. Before this, village dialogue on map 9021 was refused with Interaction_TargetNotFound, which the client shows as 'Unable to find target'. Sessions placed on main-world map 1 by GM tp_map remain outside the index.
- Company-aware merchant conditions (2026-10-30): shop sessions now evaluate interaction, ShopItemCondition and voucher conditions against the character's CompanyService standing (current company and position level, pioneer permit validity). Company rows follow the client's check order: same company, valid permit unless ignorePermit, minimum level; omitted fields use protobuf defaults and EX5CompanyType_None means no company. Live evidence: a Blue Salt level 3 character was refused housing blueprints (condition 13, 'Conditions not met') because sessions passed an empty context.
- Full-wallet sales (2026-11-01): CUSTOM: NPC sale proceeds above the wallet limit fill the wallet to the limit instead of refusing the sale with ItemError, so graduated characters can sell items (including quest steps that ask for a sale). A sale with a full wallet sends no money change.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- The reported Harbor City sale has user-observed original-client acceptance; broader vendor service and schedule coverage remains partial.
- Buyback is absent from this client build (no Buyback/Repurchase string in the image, no recovered message or GameVariable for a sold-item list), so none is implemented.
- Unsupported goods still include CraftRecipe and QuestItem. HousingBuildingDrawing goods now use stack storage while retaining catalog conditions, prices and existing shop ownership/range limits; original-client drawing purchase acceptance is unverified. The ItemRepairCostDeclineRate unit trait is not modelled.
- Candidate rules without a capture: rejection codes, the weight ceiling formula and its error code, voucher price/expiry/refund, housing_items and token money wire details, per-shop refund multipliers and UTC limit-reset windows. Repair does not emit the ChangeStatNoti and EquipmentsUpdateNoti that follow the captured repair reply.

**Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`PS2C_ShopItemLimitNoti`** — Sent after a validated shop open with the current window's purchased counts; the count meaning is inferred from an empty official list, the immediate timing is Candidate (the capture shows it about 400 ms after the request) and reset boundaries are Candidate.
