## Gathering, cooking, crafting and item improvement

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Expertise/tool animations, recipe results, polishing, disassembly and item expertise.

**Current implementation**

- Server-authoritative gathering for demo ArcheWorld map sessions on two captured request shapes: placements (param.gathering, 15,322 gathering.json nodes) and doodads (param.interaction 20001-20003 on spot units sector<<32|local<<12|6: Roseberry Bush 74, Dark Vein 90, Wild Bush 58000; 289 placements). Range/map/tool/busy/death checks, montage-derived execute deadlines, ExpertiseReward loot rolls and shared per-map node state.
- Captured reply shapes: StartInteractionAnimNoti names the wire unit and echoes the request param/pos/yaw/tick with an empty packet_seq; an SP StatSyncNoti (SCS_InteractionFlow, rate -cost/execute s, regen range to duration+SPStatRegenDelayMilli) precedes it and the cost is deducted once at execution; nearby players receive 166 and both 167 results.
- Gathering submits rewards, tool wear (ToolDurabiliyDecreaseValue 100) and the next revision as one item-trade plan. Since 2026-10-30 the shared item-trade validator accepts any non-negative durability update on a distinct row (repairs and tool wear), so equipped-tool gathering and butchering commit through the real repository (GatheringFeature.RealRepositoryCommitsToolWearBeforePostCommitEffects); the authored path emits 169 with the tool row, then 47 (SCS_Equip vitals) and 168. Doodad results and timed phase/respawn behavior retain their existing policy.
- All 26 gathering IDs have rewards: 13 authored, 4 capture-confirmed (102, 300, 301, 302) and 9 catalog-name Candidate joins to the mirrored 1306xxxx ExpertiseReward family.
- SectorUpdateNoti carries depleted placements and changed doodads; without the sector grid each map load receives incremental 196/194 notifications. Unconsumed shared-world interaction starts are logged with static metadata only.
- Catalog-backed non-tutorial world sessions route gathering requests and initial depleted-node snapshots through the native adapter; tutorial routing remains separate.
- Current ProcessingSession validates station dialogue, craft/animation identity, server deadlines, range, materials, gold and count, then atomically commits product and resource changes. The generated profile contains 9 map areas, 12 station definitions, 39 placements and 111 supported recipes, with 127 explicitly unsupported recipes. Processing opts into the shipped housing map while the shared gathering helper keeps its default map scope unchanged. Original-client station/recipe acceptance remains unverified.
- HousingBuilding and HousingObject recipe outputs use WorldProgress.housing_items; HousingBuildingDrawing ingredients use the existing stack store. The ordinary revisioned craft transaction consumes blueprint/material/gold costs once, increments housing quantity without changing installed_count and emits ItemsUpdateNoti.housing_items plus the craft result. Learned recipes, unsupported costs and equipment-instance ingredients remain refused.
- Map-load packet preservation: the historical adapter fix retained UnitAddNoti already queued by world combat. The current candidate uses guarded sector snapshots; when the grid lacks the map, the native adapter requests a guarded full-map snapshot without claiming the map-load request. The earlier invisible-mob observation is historical; current original-client acceptance remains pending.
- Player unit identity (2026-10-27): the native adapter constructs GatheringSession and ProcessingSession with the player's wire unit ID ((character_id << 4) | 1, player_wire_unit_id), matching official own DialogueEndNoti.player_unit_id and InteractionAnimRes.unit_id. Both sessions previously received the raw character ID; in a local original-client trial the station DialogueEndNoti and the gathering StartInteractionAnimNoti named the character ID and the character stayed locked until relog. Persistence keys keep the raw character ID.
- Crafting entry snapshots (2026-10-27): every world entry now sends WorldCharExpertiseSkillsNoti (all sixteen EX5ExpertiseType values at Lv1) before WorldCharItemsNoti and an empty non-update WorldCharItemCraftsNoti after it, matching the order and content of every official entry. In the local trial the original client sent DialogueEndReq 17 ms after DialogueStartRes on the map-9012 Brewing Furnace (doodad 20251, Craft interaction 10220, expertise Jewealry). Static analysis of the matching client build (AAC_Interaction_Craft_OpenUiRequiresExpertise) shows the craft window opens only when FX5CraftManager reports a non-zero level for the interaction's expertise type; without the snapshot it raises Craft_SkillNotLearn (1104) and ends the dialogue.
- Map-scope repair (2026-10-29): gathering and processing explicitly include Release ArcheWorld Field maps reached by live travel, including 9031. Gathering regenerates 27 maps/119474 points/466 supported doodad points; processing 28 maps/111 placements. Existing reward and recipe support, range, timing, ownership and atomic commits are preserved; arbitrary chest/action interactions are not added.
- Recipe items (category CraftRecipe) used through ItemUseReq spend one owned item and record the learned craft in one commit (schema 35), then send ItemsUpdateNoti and a merged WorldCharItemCraftsNoti (update=true). Entry restores the saved list. Processing previews and execution require a learned recipe when the craft needs learning; automatic crafts cannot spend an extra item.
- Corpse butchering: StartInteractionAnimReq{interaction_anim_id 1000, param.handling_loot, target_unit_id = corpse} needs the killer's unbutchered corpse, an equipped knife, SP and the 7 m range; it is accepted on every map, not only gathering areas. ExecuteInteractionReq after the montage execute event (2,930 ms) rolls the monster's ExpertiseReward pack (build_gathering_data.py: 101 monsters, 2 explicit unsupported), wears the knife by 100 and answers ItemsUpdateNoti (system reason), the corpse's UnitLootItemInfoNoti and InteractionAnimRes, as captured. Bone Chips for Gathering Bone Fragments come from coastal reptiles this way.
- Cliffs of Madness quest doodads: the prison door checks the Rescue Plan state and consumes its key, and the cannon checks Alight the Cliffs, changes its own and the barrier phase, and starts captured cutscene 301006. Direct InteractUnitReq parameters are supported. Synthetic tests cover the interactions and item-commit failure.
- Cliffs encounter candidate: server-owned elite defeat opens the authored barricade and activates its nearby object; captain defeat enables the Dimensional Rift. Saved quest progress reconstructs these and the cannon barricade after restart, without resetting already changed shared phases. Rift interaction requires the character’s captain objective and uses the existing authored travel and quest event.
- Cliffs elite object: eligible interaction with doodad 777 in either authored phase selects the synthetic server-played cutscene 1550 and emits the existing doodad quest event; the quest service enforces the authored hidden-quest and Alight the Cliffs conditions; the travel exporter includes its server-played scene metadata.
- A positive DamageNoti targeted to the player abandons an active gathering action without granting rewards; PvP interruption remains unverified. Monster butchering retains its authored 2.93-second execute deadline; the reported client hold-to-gather and fast-animation behavior remains unresolved and needs original-client tracing.
- Cliffs shared boss-source snapshots preserve durable phase-1 activation for the specifically identified elite object and rift, whose authored placements start deactivated even though phase 1 is usable. Late visitors and restart-hydrated state receive those activations.
- Authored deactivation metadata (2026-11-02): the profile exports the flag per supported doodad placement. A recorded shared activation at the initial phase is included in late sector and map snapshots when that placement started deactivated; older profiles retain the two evidenced Cliffs exceptions. This is snapshot behavior, not generic activation or interaction enforcement.
- Runtime station placements (2026-11-02): ProcessingSession accepts an optional ProcessingStationLocator. A target that is not an exported map placement is resolved through it and served only when its doodad is a profiled station; each placement carries its own reach (map stations keep 7 m). The world session supplies housing lot stations with the lot centre and a reach of the lot's corner distance plus 7 m. The exporter keeps craft stations a housing lot can hold (HousingObject/HousingBuilding Item.FK_doodadId, HousingPresetDoodad, HousingModelPartAddOn) without a map placement: the regenerated profile has 21 stations (85001-85005 added), 111 placements and 233 recipes; lot-only stations whose recipes contradict their interaction's expertise (169990, 170000) are omitted and listed under unsupported_stations, while map stations still fail the build.

**Custom / guessed behavior (not official)**

Our own guesses, because the data to reproduce the official behavior does not exist. They add no capture evidence and do not promote any status.

- Recipe acquisition packet order (consumed item before the merged recipe list) is a Candidate; the client's merge behavior is established statically only.
- The Cliffs rift is enabled directly after captain defeat, instead of reproducing the captured post-boss object interaction.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Gathering: expertise progression (ItemLvUpExpertiseReq, ExpertiseReqItemCount) and level benefits (SPDecrease, RewardIncrease, GatheringCountIncrease) are not implemented; no capture shows a level-up. Doodad tool requirements are not enforced (no captured doodad wear). The not-enough-SP code and cancellation StatSyncNoti are Candidates; InteractionCancelMinimumTime and weight limits are not enforced; nine reward joins are catalog-name Candidates. The corrected flow has not yet been tried with the original client.
- Shared-world observer animation delivery and sector-state payloads exist in the source and synthetic adapter checks; original-client acceptance of the corrected gathering flow remains unverified.
- Disassembly has no runtime handler or full item-state model; item tempering (ItemPolishReq, including chance steps and additives) is covered under inventory.
- Processing still lacks original-client craft acceptance, expertise experience/level-up persistence and level enforcement (every character reports Lv1 in all sixteen types), learned recipes, unsupported costs/company-position requirements and equipment-instance material recipes, movement cancellation and observer synchronization. A count above one remains a local scaling inference: every captured craft uses count one.
- After the 2026-10-27 expertise-snapshot fix, an original-client trial must still confirm that the station window opens and that a craft completes end to end. Shared-world SectorUpdateNoti streaming is now sent (docs/sector-streaming.md); static analysis shows its absence was not what closed the station window.
- Cliffs encounter phases are shared by map rather than party. The captured post-captain object sequence is not implemented; the rift is enabled directly as a local workaround. The new progression flow has not been confirmed in the original client.
- Original-client reproduction is needed for the reported hold-to-butcher and fast-animation behavior.
- The exporter retains authored per-placement deactivation, but generic activation scripts and interaction gating remain unimplemented or unverified. The shared volume path can still omit an activation that sets an initially deactivated placement to its initial phase; safely resolving its storage, publication and character-trigger ordering remains open. Original-client visibility is unverified.

**Dependencies:** Authenticated ownership, authoritative state and bounded execution.

**Packet inventory** — counts follow capture keys T / P1 / P2 / A1 / M1 / W1 / R1. Zero means absent from these world logs, not impossible or unsupported by the game.

| Packet / payload schema | ID or route | Runtime | T / P1 / P2 / A1 / M1 / W1 / R1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `PC2S_ItemDisassembleReq`<br>`x5.pb.ItemDisassembleReq` | 20073 | missing | 0 / 0 / 1 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `PC2S_ItemPolishReq`<br>`x5.pb.ItemPolishReq` | 20075 | partial | 0 / 2 / 5 / 2 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `PC2S_ItemLvUpExpertiseReq`<br>`x5.pb.ItemLvUpExpertiseReq` | 20076 | missing | 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `PS2C_WorldCharItemCraftsNoti`<br>`x5.pb.WorldCharItemCraftsNoti` | 132 | partial | 1 / 0 / 1 / 1 / 2 / 0 / 0 |
| `PS2C_OnDemandDynamicCharItemCraftResultNoti`<br>`x5.pb.OnDemandDynamicCharItemCraftResultNoti` | 147 | partial | 0 / 2 / 7 / 5 / 4 / 0 / 0 |
| `PS2C_ChangeGatheringStateNoti`<br>`x5.pb.ChangeGatheringStateNoti` | 196 | partial | 2 / 332 / 43 / 104 / 69 / 3 / 7 |

**Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`PC2S_ItemDisassembleReq`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_c2s.item.proto`. Fields: 1:item_ids (repeated sfixed64)
- **`PC2S_ItemPolishReq`** — Server-rolled tempering of owned weapons and armor: success, fail and (unequipped-only) destruction each charge stone, optional additive and gold atomically and answer with one ItemsUpdateNoti.polish. Seven always-succeed official exchanges are reproduced; fail/destruction/refusal/additive behavior is synthetic-test and static-client evidence only, and no original-client trial was run. Schema file: `p_c2s.item.proto`. Fields: 1:item_id (sfixed64); 2:add_material_item_cms_id (int32)
- **`PC2S_ItemLvUpExpertiseReq`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_c2s.item.proto`. Fields: 1:expertise_type (x5.cms.EX5ExpertiseType); 2:item_cms_id (int32)
- **`PS2C_WorldCharItemCraftsNoti`** — Entry sends the saved learned-recipe list (non-update); learning a recipe sends a merged update. Original-client recipe use is unobserved. Schema file: `p_s2c.character.proto`. Fields: 1:update (bool); 2:craft_ids (repeated int32)
- **`PS2C_OnDemandDynamicCharItemCraftResultNoti`** — Current ProcessingSession emits a result after an atomic recipe transaction; station reachability and original-client acceptance remain open. Supported building/object outputs now commit to housing-item quantity storage while preserving installed counts; blueprint ingredients are consumed as stacks. General learned/equipment-instance material recipes remain unsupported. Stations placed on a housing lot (85001-85005) now produce results (synthetic TLS only, 2026-11-02). Schema file: `p_s2c.character.proto`. Fields: 1:item_craft_id (int32); 2:items (repeated x5.pb.ItemInfo)
- **`PS2C_ChangeGatheringStateNoti`** — Gathering depletion and respawn on demo ArcheWorld maps, delivered to every session on the map. Initial state rides SectorUpdateNoti (as captured) when the sector grid is loaded; otherwise each map load receives incremental notifications (local choice). Schema file: `p_s2c.sector.proto`. Fields: 1:sector_id (uint32); 2:activated_indices (repeated uint32); 3:deactivated_indices (repeated uint32)

## World/local/group chat and whispers

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Front chat/DM and world Party chat, authenticated audience routing and unsolicited pushes.

**Current implementation**

- Initial in-process front World chat and online whispers route by selected realm/character with bounded queues.
- Identity/UTF-8/length/rate checks, sender echo, name/ID whisper lookup and recipient push paths exist.
- World-transport Party chat: PC2S_SendChatReq type Party is validated and rate-limited by WorldChatService and delivered as PS2C_SendChatNoti to the sender's connected party, including the sender.
- Operator notices: the console sends a World-type WSF2C_ChatNoti with an operator sender label (default [Server]) to every front chat connection on the realm through the same bounded per-connection queues, without the player rate limit.
- Guild chat uses the authenticated selected character and addresses only connected members from the shared guild registry; the client cannot supply its audience.
- Operator chat view: the front chat service keeps the latest 1,000 delivered World messages (player and operator) in memory only, never logged or persisted; the console reads them through GET /admin/v1/chat with a sequence cursor.
- A configurable monotonic scheduler rotates enabled server World chat messages at the operator interval. Welcome lines are private notices once per successful StartPlaying connection; selection, duplicate starts and map moves do not repeat them.
- Player !help and !pvp on|off|status commands are intercepted privately before front/Party audience routing, use a separate bounded allowlist and per-character rate limit, and never become public chat or GM commands. Help lists player commands in seven short lines. Forwarded /help and /pvp aliases share the parser, but matching-build static client routing and its 236 exported aliases establish that unknown slash commands are discarded locally; use ! with the stock client.
- Player !mount and !dismount (2026-10-29) share the same allowlist, rate limit and private routing. They take no argument and are queued on the character's live world session (see the companions feature); a queued request adds no immediate line and the world session sends the outcome as a private [Server] line.
- Front Local chat (the stock client's default channel, type 1) reaches the speaker's echo plus every in-world character whose client currently sees the speaker in the world listener's shared presence registry (same map, presence sight distance). The world service resolves the audience per message; private tutorial and hidden-GM speakers reach only themselves, and a speaker without an in-world connection receives CommonErrorRes BadRequest. Front chat refusals log only the channel number and reason.
- Front chat registrations are bounded at 1024 concurrent connections (previously 128), so in-world players beyond 128 can use Local/World/Guild chat. Not load tested at that size.
- The authenticated private player-command parser exposes !unstuck, validates its arguments and queues the request to the owning world session. The player receives the actual queued outcome; the help command includes it.
- Chat departure records entered, exiting, completed and uncertain outcomes. Close retains admission while departure is pending or its external outcome is uncertain, and does not replay an uncertain external exit.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Company audience remains unimplemented; ordinary world-transport Local/World chat has no audience. The Local radius is the emulator presence sight distance, not a recovered official range.
- Offline messages, durable chat history/moderation, blocking and cross-realm delivery remain separate work.
- Original-client rendering of server labels, welcome text and the ! command exchange has not been observed. Slash aliases require a client that forwards them.
- Original-client chat invocation and successful !unstuck relocation have not been observed.
- An uncertain external chat departure remains fenced; no operator recovery or safe replay is implemented. The native entry wrapper can suppress a partially applied friend-presence entry error, and concurrent entry safety depends on the worker-strand caller.

**Evidence and verification**

**Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`PC2S_SendChatReq`** — Party type only: validated, rate-limited and delivered to the sender's connected party; other types get no world-transport audience. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:type (x5.cms.EX5ChatMessageType); 2:message (string)
- **`PS2C_SendChatNoti`** — Party chat delivery with sender_name and sender_unit_id from the session; display_secs unset; synthetic tests only. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:type (x5.cms.EX5ChatMessageType); 2:message (string); 3:sender_name (string); 4:sender_unit_id (uint64); 5:display_secs (float)
- **`WSC2F_ChatReq`** — Front World, Local (speaker plus characters that currently see the speaker), Guild and online-whisper paths exist; Company, official limits/radius and original-client acceptance remain open. Schema file: `p_c2f.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:type (x5.cms.EX5ChatMessageType); 2:message (string)
- **`WSC2F_DirectMessageReq`** — Initial front World/online-whisper path exists; other audiences, official limits and original-client acceptance remain open. Schema file: `p_c2f.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:char_id (sfixed64); 2:char_name (string); 3:message (string)
- **`WSF2C_ChatNoti`** — Front World, Local, Guild and online-whisper paths exist; Company, official limits and original-client acceptance remain open. The operator console also sends World-type notices with an operator sender label. Private player-command replies, welcome-once notices and enabled rotating server chat use the same bounded front queues. Schema file: `p_f2c.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:type (x5.cms.EX5ChatMessageType); 2:message (string); 3:sender_name (string)
- **`WSF2C_DirectMessageRes`** — Initial front World/online-whisper path exists; other audiences, official limits and original-client acceptance remain open. Schema file: `p_f2c.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode); 2:char_name (string); 3:char_id (sfixed64); 4:message (string)
- **`WSF2C_DirectMessageNoti`** — Initial front World/online-whisper path exists; other audiences, official limits and original-client acceptance remain open. Schema file: `p_f2c.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:char_id (sfixed64); 2:char_name (string); 3:message (string)

## Parties, leadership and group channels

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Invite/accept/reject, roster, leader, kick/leave and channel coordination.

**Current implementation**

- Server-authoritative membership in the world listener: invite popup with a temporary invite-carrier party, accept, reject, leave, kick and leader change; refusals return the recovered Party_* EErrorCode in CommonErrorRes.
- Catalog GameVariable limits: 4 members, 20 s invite expiry, 10 s member world-state sync and the PartyUnlockQuestId 90100011 gate (Party_UnlockPartyContentRequired) for inviter, invitee and accepter.
- Disconnects keep seats as EX5PartyMemberConnStateType_Retain for 5 minutes (operator policy); reconnect resends PartyJoinNoti, and leadership passes to the lowest connected member.
- Party benefits: PartyMemberWorldStateNoti HP/max HP/death/position/same-channel sync, ChangePartyUnitNoti plus PlayerNub.party_id for the member and its observers, and world-transport Party chat.
- Party and guild unit labels use typed player wire IDs; directory and persistence keys remain raw character IDs.
- Instance and dungeon copies (2026-11-01, CUSTOM; docs/instances-and-dungeons.md): members of an established party enter the party's copy of an Instance or Dungeon map (chosen when the map move starts), so they share its monsters, nodes and doodads and see each other; party kill credit and loot sharing use the copy's channel key. Characters without a party get their own copy.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Party channel invites and travel (PartyChannelInvite*, PartyChannelMove* and PartyMoveToLeaderChannelReq), WSF2C front-WebSocket party notifications, WorldCharEntry party hints and persistence across server restarts are not implemented.
- Quest kill-credit sharing (QuestProgress isPartyShare and QuestPartyShareCredit* ranges) and shared loot need shared-world combat; combat and quests run only in private tutorial instances.
- The live route enters every character into a private map 8000 instance, so players see each other's units only on shared maps; invite targets must come from client contexts carrying a character ID, such as whisper senders.
- Accept/leave/kick/leader transitions, the world-transport choice for roster notifications and the seat retention time are Candidate. No original-client party trial was performed.
- Three popup invites, one channel invite and membership notifications/snapshots do not establish the complete lifecycle.

## Friends, lookup and presence

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Friend search/add/remove/modify/list, recommended friends and presence notifications.

**Current implementation**

- Account-scoped FriendService with memory/PostgreSQL persistence (schema version 31): one-directional immediate adds, the added account's recommended list, dismissal, removal, nicknames and last-login records. Actors come from the authenticated selected character.
- Front adapter answers FriendSearchReq (character name, character ID or account; req_seq echoed), FriendAddReq, FriendRemoveReq (FriendRemoveNoti), FriendModifyReq (FriendUpdateNoti) and FriendListReq (friends or recommended, recommend preserved). Refusals use the client's mapped codes: InvalidChar, InvalidState (MaxFriendNum 60) and DuplicateRequest.
- FriendInfo uses the recovered status oneof: char while the friend's account is in the world, otherwise last_login_epochtime in 100 ns Unix ticks. World entry and the paired connection close push FriendUpdateNoti to in-world owners; a second connection keeps the account online until both close.
- Adding an in-world player who does not list the requester pushes WSF2C_SystemMessageNoti SM_FRIEND_ADD_ALARM (335).
- Before character selection FriendListReq keeps the previous empty-list reply, so lobby requests never close the socket.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Blocking, Steam friend codes (searches report InvalidChar) and pk_kill_count (always 0) are not implemented.
- Level and guild changes while both players stay online are not pushed; the next FriendListReq returns stored values. Recommended-list changes are not pushed.
- The one-directional recommendation model, default alias (character name), alias bound (16 code points) and FriendModifyReq reply mapping are Candidate. Original-client acceptance is unobserved.

**Evidence and verification**

Client friend-manager handlers, error mapping and presence encoding were recovered statically (dumps/ida_research/friends-20261027). **Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`WSC2F_FriendSearchReq`** — Searches by character name, character ID or account on the realm and echoes req_seq. Steam friend codes are not modeled and report InvalidChar. Schema file: `p_c2f.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:req_seq (uint32); 2:char_id (sfixed64); 3:account_id (sfixed64); 4:char_name (string); 5:steam_friend_code (string)
- **`WSC2F_FriendAddReq`** — Adds the account immediately (one-directional, Candidate) with MaxFriendNum, duplicate, self and unknown-target checks; the target's recommended list gains the requester. Schema file: `p_c2f.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:account_id (sfixed64)
- **`WSC2F_FriendRemoveReq`** — Removes a listed friend, or dismisses a recommendation when recommend is true. Idempotent. Schema file: `p_c2f.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:account_id (sfixed64); 2:recommend (bool)
- **`WSC2F_FriendModifyReq`** — Stores a validated alias (16 code points, Candidate bound); an empty alias restores the character name. No modify response exists, so the reply is FriendUpdateNoti (Candidate); invalid targets receive CommonErrorRes. Schema file: `p_c2f.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:account_id (sfixed64); 2:alias (string)
- **`WSC2F_FriendListReq`** — Returns the stored friends or recommended list for the selected character's account, preserving recommend presence; before selection the empty lobby reply is kept. Schema file: `p_c2f.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:recommend (bool)
- **`WSF2C_FriendSearchRes`** — Returns the matched character in FriendInfo.char and last_login_epochtime when its account is offline; InvalidChar when nothing matches. Steam friend codes are not modeled. Schema file: `p_f2c.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode); 2:req_seq (uint32); 3:friend (x5.pb.FriendInfo); 4:last_login_epochtime (sfixed64)
- **`WSF2C_FriendAddRes`** — Success carries the new FriendInfo; refusals use InvalidChar, InvalidState, DuplicateRequest or BadRequest (self). Schema file: `p_f2c.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode); 2:friend (x5.pb.FriendInfo)
- **`WSF2C_FriendListRes`** — FriendInfo entries use char while online and last_login_epochtime while offline. Schema file: `p_f2c.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:recommend (bool); 2:friends (repeated x5.pb.FriendInfo)
- **`WSF2C_FriendRemoveNoti`** — Always answers FriendRemoveReq with the account and recommend flag; the client confirms only when its local entry existed. Schema file: `p_f2c.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:account_id (sfixed64); 2:recommend (bool)
- **`WSF2C_FriendUpdateNoti`** — Sent for alias changes and for presence changes at world entry and exit. Level and guild changes during play are not pushed. Schema file: `p_f2c.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:friend (x5.pb.FriendInfo)

## Guilds, companies and membership

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Guild discovery/create/join/manage/leave/disband and company membership.

**Current implementation**

- Authoritative guild registry with atomic memory/PostgreSQL persistence: create, search, joinable lists, details, settings, automatic join, leave, grade changes, master transfer and disband. Actors come from authenticated selected characters. Schema version 17 preserves memberships and cooldown anchors across reconstruction.
- Front WebSocket request/response adapters and committed member notifications share the registry with world invitations, expiry, accept/reject replies, player guild labels and bounded guild chat audiences. Notification mapping and unobserved policy remain Candidate.
- Operator character deletion requires leaving or disbanding its guild first so the live registry cannot retain a deleted member.
- Own-entry labels address only the entering client; observer decorations and membership-change labels use the current typed player wire IDs.
- Leave, kick and disband release guild housing after the guild change commits; a failed, timed-out or interrupted housing cleanup is retried by reconciliation instead of being dropped, and cleanup exceptions no longer terminate the server.
- Pioneer permit desks that name no company (Devicas, dialogue 10500, NPC 1001175) register or extend the permit of the character's own company; a join or change selection still needs a named company and is refused with Company_InvalidCmsId otherwise. On shared-world maps, which have no tutorial instance, the permit charge commits from stored progress (CompanyContext::company_current_progress) and the speaker comes from the quest book's open DialogueStartReq NPC (2026-11-02).

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Company membership, company-position admission requirements and guild EXP awards are not implemented.
- Original-client guild UI, official notification timing and complete guild/housing behavior remain unverified. Master-transfer demotion and guild disband cooldown interpretation are emulator policies.

Refactor: Store drops the MarketRepository and RankingRepository bases and the facades drop the seven methods and the three feature tables; create_repositories builds MemoryMarketRepository and MemoryRankingRepository over the store's shared database (PostgreSQL builds the connection-string repositories), so one shared database, the escrow veto on character deletion and identical startup order are preserved. Checks: Release build, full CTest (1576, 0 failures), tools.module_includes, and the disposable-cluster PostgreSQL, reconnect and market smoke tools. Storage split (phase 2): Store now inherits only AccountRepository, CharacterRepository and CharacterStateRepository; MemoryStore and PostgresStore dropped the four mail methods and the last feature table, and MemoryStore registers no deletion hook because the recipient-mail erase moved into MemoryMailRepository's own hook on the shared database. create_repositories builds the mail repository over the shared MemoryDatabase in memory mode and over the shared connection string in postgres mode; MailRest, tutorial-completion delivery, WorldRepositories.mail and AdminServices.mail take the narrow interface. No behavior change. Checks: Release build, full CTest, the mail and market smoke tools, the disposable PostgreSQL and reconnect runs, tools.module_includes. Tests build repositories instead of the Store facades: MemoryRepositories over a shared MemoryDatabase (accounts member replaceable by the fault-injecting repository) and make_postgres_character_repositories(url); assertions, suites and test names unchanged (ctest 1577/1577). The Store, MemoryStore and PostgresStore facades, character_repositories_of, the Store AuthService constructor and persistence/storage.hpp are deleted; callers use the account, character and character-state repositories over one shared MemoryDatabase or one PostgreSQL connection string, and tests use MemoryRepositories/make_postgres_character_repositories. Method bodies, SQL text, revision guards and locking order unchanged; assertions, suites and test names unchanged. Checks: Release build, full CTest, mail/market/fog smoke tools, disposable-cluster PostgreSQL, reconnect and Discord runs, tools.module_includes. Phase 2 final-review cleanup: comment and brace fixes in native_world_tests.cpp; test names and assertions unchanged. Checks: Release build, affected NativeWorld and ranking tests pass. GM ownership refactor: the existing GM command adapter moved to GmSession with unchanged authorization, refusal, commit and effect order; see the Phase 4 GM evidence in docs/modular-migration-phase-4.md. Feature status is unchanged. Phase 4 Guild extraction: GuildFeature owns the existing directory, weak shared-service subscription and delivery policy; GuildSession owns authenticated actor enrichment, atomic attachment, entry snapshot and Guild EXP delivery. Front and world retain the same GuildService/CompanyService instances and absent-service guards. Late-close detach, codec/fanout scopes and cursor-before-Guild-EXP-before-Company-contribution order are preserved. The exact native invitation test moves with all 17 assertions (91 native definitions become 90 retained plus one moved). Actual affected Release targets/server built; 1760 unique names retain all 1754 prior names plus six cases. Focused checks: 202 passed, three existing Company/Guild PostgreSQL opt-ins skipped, zero failed across 205 cases. Owning Guild TLS, full Company/GM/front, Chat/Party TLS and selected route/admission/bus checks pass. Actual disposable-server world smoke 39, Guild smoke eight and social smoke nine pass. Bus/factory/shared fixture unchanged. No packet/status/gameplay or original-client acceptance change. See docs/modular-migration-phase-4.md. Phase 4 Company extraction: CompanyFeature owns the existing shared CompanyService and optional dialogue index; CompanySession owns dialogue/permit orchestration and the single tutorial activity EXP cursor. The cursor advances before synchronous Guild EXP publication, then Company contribution, Company packet and optional membership refresh. Authenticated identity/refusal queries, atomic paid-permit save, tutorial adoption and inventory-before-permit-response order are preserved. All 90 retained native definitions/file bytes are unchanged; no native test move is claimed. Actual affected Release targets/server built; 1768 unique names retain all 1760 prior names plus eight cases. Focused checks: 210 passed, three existing Company/Guild PostgreSQL opt-ins skipped, zero failed across 213 cases. Full Guild/GM/front, Chat/Party/Guild TLS and selected route/admission/bus checks pass. Actual disposable-server world smoke 39, Guild smoke eight and social smoke nine pass. Bus/factory/shared fixture unchanged. No packet/status/gameplay or original-client acceptance change. See docs/modular-migration-phase-4.md. Phase 4 membership replication and notice closure: existing PartyFeature/GuildFeature own the actual recipient-expansion loops through three narrow synchronous queue/observer capabilities. Addressed packets precede membership changes, each subject precedes current observers, duplicates/order survive, and Guild resolves each online character at the original interleaved position. Native keeps the original codec/local-frame/weak-lookup/per-encode-catch/immutable-byte-buffer/strong-recipient/post-unlock delivery scopes; the stack adapter adds no callback conversion or retained owner. Chat owns the opcode 3 text/type/style builder and public enum reexport; JSON construction remains before locking and the same audience/encoding/send body remains in composition. Original-client display of free-text notices remains unobserved. Actual ALL Release passes, all 1937 prior names remain plus six (1943 unique), with 155 existing test source files byte-exact and no losses/duplicates/owner transfers. Focused 320: 317 passed, zero failed, three original Company/Guild PostgreSQL skips in 24.29s. All six new and selected social/GM/notice/history/presence/current-model TLS, 36 routes/19 admission and rebuilt-server world39/market7 pass. All 17 applied outputs match frozen review; Bootstrap/bus/factory/base fixture remain unchanged. No gameplay, packet/status, schema or new original-client acceptance change. See docs/modular-migration-phase-4.md. Phase 5 neutral event composition: the single immutable synchronous bus is composed through named application observers, without the transitional GM event-subscriber context. Thirteen subscribers retain their explicit order: five named effects are required and eight preserve their existing optional behavior. Five generic GM sink requirements are removed; their actual Native effects remain unchanged after parameter substitution. Handshake is declared/constructed before the bus, followed by 25 player-owner fields and pipeline; inverse destruction keeps dependencies alive. Observer creation captures this without accessing later unconstructed owners; delivery resolves current state. Borrowed payloads remain synchronous and original owning bootstrap stat/build copies remain. Allocation and required-slot validation now occur earlier, a disclosed construction-error precedence change; no inspected feature destructor publishes. Actual ALL Release passes at eight jobs. All 1943 previous names remain plus four (1947 unique), no losses/duplicates/owner moves; original native/graduation and GM definitions remain exact. Focused 377: 374 passed, zero failed, three original PostgreSQL skips in 36.32s. All 51 GM/pipeline/bus/neutral regressions, 36 routes, 19 admission checks and selected real native/current-model/social/lifecycle cases pass; rebuilt-server World/Market smoke checks (39/7) pass. All ten source outputs and untouched surrounding source match review; module/whitespace/scoped formatting checks pass. No gameplay, packet/status, schema or new original-client acceptance change. See docs/modular-migration-phase-5.md. Follow-up hardening preserves every gameplay, packet, persistence and ordering contract: the world request IDs shared by the frame pipeline, native world and owning features are defined once in world/core/world_request_opcodes.hpp with unchanged values, frame-pipeline route sets for loot, revival, housing, chat, companion/trade, item use, company, equipment, progression, merchant, processing, gathering, utility bag and private combat are asserted across the whole 16-bit opcode range, the full pipeline step order is pinned by literal traces, native world statically ties its credential slice sizes to the transport constants, and party, gathering and guild report once (spdlog error) when a non-empty update is dropped because no delivery is installed. Checked by the default Release suite (0 failures) and the native world smoke; no feature status or packet override changes. Review follow-up preserves every gameplay, packet, persistence and ordering contract: the frame pipeline now exposes its step names so tests pin every composed step in order and dispatch traces for each handler group, the GM and item-use request IDs join the shared request-ID header (private copies alias it), the log-capture test helper drops its logger on destruction, and party, gathering and guild document where their dropped-delivery methods may be called. Checked by the default Release suite (0 failures) and the native world smoke; no feature status or packet override changes. Devicas permit desk (2026-11-02): a live Blue Salt member with an expired permit chose "I'd like to get a Pioneer's Permit" (dialogue 10500, selection 1/2) on map 9012 and the client showed nothing. Three server refusals caused it: shared-world sessions have no tutorial instance, so the company dialogue guard refused with Dialouge_InvalidSelectionData; the speaker came only from the tutorial; and Devicas names no company (Company_InvalidCmsId). The real-socket test NativeWorld.DevicasRegistersAPioneerPermitThroughTheSharedWorldDialogueOverTls (verified catalog, static NPC placement, map 9012) reproduced the Dialouge_InvalidSelectionData refusal before the progress fix and now receives RegisterPioneerPermitRes 94, persists the permit and charges the Trainee fee of 10 Gold. CompanyDialogueIndexTest and CompanySession tests cover company-less permit desks without a tutorial; the full company, world-session and quests test binaries pass. Synthetic evidence only; original-client acceptance after deployment is not yet observed.

## Mounts, mates and summoned NPCs

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Summoned-mount registration, summon, server seating, ridden movement and dismount; trade-wagon boarding, driving, repair and damage; house-mate registration, spawn, invite, despawn and intimacy; companion snapshots and persistence.

**Current implementation**

- Registration consumables (Item.FK_skillEffectList -> SkillEffect registerSummonNpc) consume one item and answer ItemsUpdateNoti(use) then RegisterSummonNpcRes once per summon; WorldCharSummonNpcsNoti and WorldCharMatesNoti are sent when the client starts playing.
- SpawnSummonNpcReq validates catalog, ownership, life and riding state (Summon_InvalidSummonNpcCmsId/NotRegistered/PlayerDead/AlreadyRiding) and sends SpawnSummonNpcRes, the horse UnitAddNoti (NPC nibble 2, raw owner_char_id, summon, mount.passengers) and MountUnitNoti slot 0 to the owner and every viewer.
- Shared CompanionWorld: companion unit ids fit in the client lookup's low 32 bits (reserved block 0xE0000000..0xEFFFFFFF, NPC type nibble 2, vehicle nibble 4). The former bit-62 tag prevented MountUnitNoti/MoveNoti actor resolution. Per map/channel visibility uses the 100 m/120 m presence radii; late viewers receive riders through passengers; a rider's MoveReq moves the ridden unit and is relayed as MoveNoti for that unit (the rider's own presence move is suppressed). Summoned mounts announce neutral MoveSpeedRate stat 84 = 1000 per mille.
- GetOffUnitReq answers MountUnitNoti without slot (reason User, dismount point) and removes a horse; vehicles stay where the driver gets off. RideUnitReq boards an owned vehicle seat with RideUnitRes and the Riding_* error codes.
- Vehicle 200 announced as operable.vehicle (nibble 4) with health stats; RepairWagon (Interaction 62) consumes item 140 and adds 1500 health with ChangeStatNoti; damage breaks a wagon at zero health (MountBroken).
- House mates: SpawnMateNpcReq with SM_HOUSEMATE_* system messages, ChangedMateStateRes Spawned/Invited/BeAway, DespawnMateNpcReq, intimacy capped by MateIntimateLevel; spawned mates are recorded away at exit or next entry.
- Schema 19 persists registered summons, mates and the trade run in the revisioned world-progress transaction (memory and PostgreSQL stores).
- GM register/spawn/despawn summon, register/spawn/invite/despawn mate, add intimacy, spawn operable and damage vehicle commands for game-master accounts.
- The summon key works through quick slots: the front REST routes GET /api/front/CharHotKeyLoadReq/<char_id>/<n> and PUT /api/front/CharHotKeySaveReq/<char_id>/<n> (Bearer session token, binary CharHotKeys/CharHotKey) persist slots in schema 21.
- /gm car (2026-10-28): any player, not only a game master, may spawn the catalog's one vehicle (Vehicle 200, a TradeWagon) through the companion GM path, at most one every five seconds per session. The command takes no argument and every other companion command stays game-master only. Synthetic verification only; original-client behavior is not observed.
- Attachment/lifecycle repair (2026-10-29): the first horse and auto-seated wagon nub includes the committed rider, allowing the client mount readiness callback to recover attachment from passengers. MountUnitNoti retains optional slot zero. Death unseats once with RiderKilled after life persistence on frame/timer paths, removes the horse and settles wagon state; dead boarding is refused. Disconnect unbinds before removal. Dismount uses a finite nearby point or the current mount position (Candidate seven-metre bound). Unit ID text uses the existing checked parser. Synthetic and TLS verified; original-client attachment remains pending.
- Mounted session latency repair (2026-10-29): rider death checks use the entry life snapshot and committed death/revival events instead of loading complete world progress on every frame and timer tick. Failed persistence cannot cause a speculative dismount. Reentry refreshes the stored snapshot; packet formats and dismount reasons are unchanged.
- Mount registration through interaction animation 1013 starts with StartInteractionAnimNoti (166); at 3408 ms on the server clock one registration item is consumed and the summon registered in one commit; InteractionAnimRes (167) finishes at 4400 ms. Movement over 1 m, map change, death or a competing action cancels without spending the item, client execute reports cannot advance the deadline and a direct ItemUseReq for the item is refused while it is pending.
- Player !mount / !dismount (2026-10-29, emulator policy): any character may summon and seat a horse or get off a horse or wagon from chat. The matching client has no horse dismount key (its only key-mapped get-off action is Tradewagon_GetOff in the wagon input layer; re-pressing the summon quick slot is the only horse input). The chat parser queues the action on the character's world session strand (NativeWorldListener::player_mount). !mount uses the lowest registered rideable summon, else lends the catalog's lowest rideable SummonNpc without registering it, and emits the summon UnitAddNoti and MountUnitNoti slot 0 without a SpawnSummonNpcRes. !dismount is the GetOffUnitReq server path without a landing point (reason User, horse removed, wagon stays) followed by the trade-run wagon update. Dead riders, the tutorial instance and housing visits are refused; replies are private [Server] lines. Synthetic and TLS verified; original-client acceptance of a server-initiated summon from chat is pending.
- Natural region handoffs retain a ridden companion or wagon and reannounce the existing unit and seating on arrival. The current candidate binds queued companion updates to source relationships and recipient map/copy views, and retains ordered detach pages for supervised close/retry. Ordinary source mutation ordering and original-client continuity remain under review.

**Custom / guessed behavior (not official)**

Our own guesses, because the data to reproduce the official behavior does not exist. They add no capture evidence and do not promote any status.

- The 1 m movement tolerance that cancels a pending registration animation is a local policy.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- CreateOperableReq, ChangeSummonStateReq and DespawnSummonNpcReq have no client sender in this build and are not handled; SummonStateNoti and UnitChangeOwnerNoti are not emitted (the client ignores the former).
- Mates are called outside houses only (housing_lot_number 0); no item or effect grants a mate in this build, and invite/dismiss have no shipped interaction (GM only).
- Server-side mount speed validation, water dismount and full world combat damage to wagons remain missing. Recovered MountSprintRequireSP=1, MountSprintConsumeTick=500ms and MountSprintConsumeSPPerTick=0 do not justify inventing a positive sprint cost.
- Horse removal timing, rider MoveNoti suppression, server seating and the one-seat wagon are Candidate. A pre-correction local-client trial showed a wagon but failed seating despite successful server replies; post-correction original-client driving, braking and dismount acceptance remain pending.
- !mount is server-initiated, so the client's own summon prechecks (riding-zone restriction 15004, falling, swimming, blocked forward sweep) do not run and no server-side zone, water or fall check replaces them. The housing-visit refusal is a Candidate emulator policy.
- Multi-passenger regional handoff and uninterrupted original-client riding remain unverified.
- Pre-existing presence leave commits before legacy fanout; an exceptional partial fanout can leave an observer stale. This is unresolved and is not identified as a regression introduced by the candidate.

**Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`PC2S_ChangeSummonStateReq`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:state (x5.cms.EX5SummonStateType); 2:summon_npc_unit_id (uint64)
- **`PC2S_CreateOperableReq`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:vehicle_cms_id (int32)
- **`PC2S_DespawnSummonNpcReq`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:summon_npc_unit_id (uint64)
- **`PC2S_SpawnMateNpcReq`** — Spawns a registered mate outside houses; SM_HOUSEMATE_* system messages report refusals. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:mate_npc_cms_id (int32); 2:housing_lot_number (int32)
- **`PC2S_DespawnMateNpcReq`** — Despawns an owned mate unit; ChangedMateStateRes BeAway. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:mate_npc_unit_id (uint64)
- **`PC2S_InviteMateNpcReq`** — Marks an owned spawned mate Invited; Housing_AlreadyInvitedMate when repeated. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:mate_npc_unit_id (uint64)
- **`PC2S_SpawnSummonNpcReq`** — Summons an owned SummonNpc mount and seats its owner; Summon_* refusals in SpawnSummonNpcRes. Mount ids fit the client's low-32-bit dispatch and its nub includes neutral MoveSpeedRate 1000. Synthetic TLS tested; original-client summon acceptance is pending. The initial horse nub now includes its rider in mount.passengers for actor-readiness retries. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:summon_npc_cms_id (int32)
- **`PC2S_RideUnitReq`** — Boards an owned vehicle seat (slot = passenger index); Riding_* refusals. Companion ids now fit the client's low-32-bit actor lookup. GM-wagon boarding, driving, dismount and reboard pass synthetic TLS checks; original-client acceptance after correction is pending. Dead players receive InvalidState and do not acquire a seat. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:mount_unit_id (uint64); 2:slot (uint32)
- **`PC2S_GetOffUnitReq`** — Dismounts at the requested point; no typed reply exists. Horses are removed after dismount (Candidate). Landing positions must be finite and within the seven-metre boarding radius; otherwise the current mount point is used (Candidate local policy). Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:dismount_point (x5.pb.SpawnPoint)
- **`PS2C_SummonStateNoti`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:summoner_unit_id (uint64); 2:summon_npc_unit_id (uint64); 3:state (x5.cms.EX5SummonStateType)
- **`PS2C_MountUnitNoti`** — Seats (slot) and unseats (no slot, dismount_reason User/MountRemoved/MountBroken/ClearTrade) riders for the owner and viewers. Mount/vehicle ids must have zero high dword: the client truncates the lookup key before handler dispatch. Synthetic tests pass; post-correction live acceptance is pending. Also emits RiderKilled on committed death and RiderRemoved before disconnect removal; a present slot zero is preserved. The initial nub carries the same seat state. RiderKilled now consumes cached committed life events instead of polling storage on every frame and timer; durable ordering is preserved. The player !mount and !dismount chat commands emit the same seat and User unseat notifications server-initiated (synthetic and TLS checked; original-client acceptance pending). Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:unit_id (uint64); 2:passenger_unit_id (uint64); 3:slot (uint32); 4:dismount_reason (x5.cms.EX5DismountReason); 5:dismount_point (x5.pb.SpawnPoint); 6:skip_anim (bool); 7:tick (sfixed64)
- **`PS2C_RegisterSummonNpcRes`** — Sent once per newly registered summon (registration consumable or GM). Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:summon_npc_cms_id (uint32)
- **`PS2C_RegisterMateNpcRes`** — Sent when a mate is registered (GM register_mate_npc; no catalog grant exists). Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:mate_npc_cms_id (uint32)
- **`PS2C_ChangedMateIntimateRes`** — Resulting intimacy after a change, capped by MateIntimateLevel. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:mate_npc_cms_id (uint32); 2:result_intimate (int32)
- **`PS2C_ChangedMateStateRes`** — Mate unit and state after spawn, invite and despawn. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:mate_npc_cms_id (uint32); 2:mate_npc_unit_id (uint64); 3:state_type (int32)
- **`PS2C_SpawnSummonNpcRes`** — Empty on success, ec on refusal; sent before the mount UnitAddNoti. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode)
- **`PS2C_RideUnitRes`** — Answers every RideUnitReq; seating itself arrives as MountUnitNoti. Successful replies were observed during the pre-correction local-client seating failure and are not proof of visual mounting. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode)
- **`PS2C_WorldCharMatesNoti`** — Registered mates when the client starts playing; out mates are reported away. Schema file: `p_s2c.character.proto`. Fields: 1:mate_infos (repeated x5.pb.MateInfo)
- **`PS2C_WorldCharSummonNpcsNoti`** — Owned summon ids when the client starts playing (non-tutorial sessions). Schema file: `p_s2c.character.proto`. Fields: 1:summon_npc_ids (repeated int32)

## Housing, land contracts and placed objects

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Personal/guild land, contracts, edit mode, placed housing, moving packages and visits.

**Current implementation**

- Catalog-backed housing domain and version-checked memory/PostgreSQL persistence for personal/guild contracts, placed contents, permissions, storage and move packages. Schema version 18 shares character progress payments with housing mutations.
- Front WebSocket adapter (NativeHousingFront) serves site contract, unlock info, area board, channel list/search/visit, move package list and the five guild housing requests; charging operations run on the character's world session strand.
- World adapter (HousingHub) serves edit mode, UpdateHousingReq placement/removal/upgrade against catalog bounds, object/farm limits and housing storage, contract extension, move package unpack/recover, housing item discard, GoHome, door/window toggles via StartInteractionAnimReq.change_house_part_state and nine GM housing commands.
- GM text command housing_contract <small|medium|large> [monthly|periodic] (emulator-defined; no GmCmd field exists for a personal contract) rents through the same HousingService::contract path as WSC2F_HousingSiteContractReq in the first rentable zone and publishes CharHousingSiteUpdateNoti, ItemsUpdateNoti and channel HousingAddNoti, without WSF2C_HousingSiteContractRes. Every housing GM command now also returns private [GM] chat lines (applied, rented lot/channel, or the refusal code with a next step) beside the unchanged common error response.
- Visits and GoHome move the character into the HousingArea map (20101) on its own connection with MapMoveStart/Complete, announce the channel's lots with HousingAddNoti, isolate presence per channel and return to the recorded origin on ZoneChannelMoveReq; without one (after a restart or a login inside the area) the character steps out onto the parent map 9012 at its current position, by the travel profile's arrival rule.
- A one-minute sweep renews periodic contracts from permits or packs expired sites and guild areas; guild member departure and guild disbanding pack guild housing.
- Supported building drawings are bought as stacks and consumed by existing station crafting into housing-item quantity storage; installed counts are preserved. Client-owned housing architects can resolve through the optional static-NPC index without duplicate visual spawns. Neither change grants land ownership or bypasses ordinary housing permissions.
- Character selection restores the owned HousingSite and saved housing entry channel/version/visit metadata without consuming pending travel. Resident-board requests with an omitted/zero channel use only a known live housing location; explicit invalid channels remain errors. Board diagnostics contain only channel, result count and error code.
- Processing explicitly includes shipped Release HousingArea bounds while gathering retains its default Demo-only map scope. The housing Construction Workshop (doodad 81020, recipe pack 14001) now resolves on map 20101 and exports 17 supported building recipes.
- Guild housing cleanup is idempotent and self-repairing: HousingHub reconciles guild sites and areas against the guild registry at startup and in every one-minute housing sweep, releasing departed members' sites and disbanded guilds' areas. It never releases a current member's site or a live guild's area, and a directory that cannot confirm a guild releases nothing.
- Ordinary NPC entry (2026-10-29): Nivhen's HousingSiteAuthorize selection runs locally in the client and opens the rent window, which sends 20017, 20012 with channel 0 and, on confirmation, 20011. Channel-0 board requests now resolve to the live housing channel or primary channel 1 instead of failing with Housing_ChannelNotFound.
- Personal contracts from players enforce GeneralHousingSite{S,M,L}positionLv against the character's CompanyService position (Housing_InsufficientCompanyPosition, Candidate server rule) before charging. The production guild directory now reports roster company positions, so guild lot assignments are no longer always refused.
- Furniture saves (2026-10-30): the stock client leaves edit mode before saving. It sends HousingEditModeReq{end}, waits for HousingEditModeNoti{end} and only then sends UpdateHousingReq (AAC_PS2C_HousingEditModeNoti_Handle -> AAC_Housing_ExitBuildMode_SaveOrDiscard, dumps/ida_research/housing-furniture-20261030). The server used to drop the edit session on end and refused every save with Housing_InvalidDoodadUpdateReq, so placed furniture was never stored. An ended session now accepts exactly one trailing save to the same site within 30 s (emulator policy); that save closes the session whatever its outcome. Build, customize and upgrade saves use the same path.
- Housing save diagnostics (2026-10-30): every HousingEditModeReq and UpdateHousingReq logs the character ID, counts and result code; a refused save also logs object IDs, catalog IDs and site-local positions (bounded to 24 entries per list).
- Furniture poses (2026-10-30, Candidate wire shape): StartInteractionAnimReq aimed at a placed housing doodad is served when the doodad stands on an occupied lot of the requester's channel and its Doodad.interactionGroupId offers the animation as an unconditional Use whose InteractionAnim costs nothing and has noExecuteNotify (chairs and beds: interaction 70/animation 70 sit, 73/71 stand). Success answers StartInteractionAnimNoti (echoing param/pos/yaw/tick, target_unit_id = the furniture) to the requester and everyone in the channel; refusals answer StartInteractionAnimRes. The matching EndInteractionAnimReq answers InteractionAnimRes{unit_id, end_interaction_anim} to the same audience. Requests for other targets fall through to the statue, processing and gathering handlers.
- Gardens and interactive decorations (2026-10-30, Candidate wire shape): tools/build_housing_data.py exports the DoodadPhaseFlow graphs of garden plots 160066, 160068, 160069, decoration 161124 and farm object 180005 (data/generated/housing/doodads.json; ConsumeItem/OwnItem conditions, ExpertiseReward/LootingPack loot, weighted next phases, earliest-rig montage timing). The lot owner starts an interaction like doodad gathering: StartInteractionAnimReq answers the gathering SP flow and StartInteractionAnimNoti; ExecuteInteractionReq from the execute event spends seeds, rolls the reward, picks the next phase and commits lot and progress together, answering ItemsUpdateNoti, ChangeDoodadPhaseNoti (194) on the housing doodad unit ID and InteractionAnimRes; EndInteractionAnimReq ends or cancels. AAC_PS2C_ChangeDoodadPhaseNoti_Handle (0x1461D3910) applies 194 to placed housing doodads. Timed phases advance in the one-minute housing sweep and before each interaction, chaining elapsed phases from their exact due times; phase starts are stored as Unix ticks and sent on the client's monotonic wire clock.
- Seated-pose replay (2026-10-30): a furniture pose whose animation holds after its end (attachPolicy HoldAfterEnd) is replayed as StartInteractionAnimNoti right after the seated player's UnitAddNoti to a later viewer, through the same presence hook as the selfie pose. Standing up, another interaction, a channel change or moving more than 1.5 m from the seat (emulator threshold) ends it.
- Main-building moves (2026-10-31): UpdateHousingReq reads an absent HouseNub.attach_index as -1 (not attached). AAC_Housing_BuildEditor_FillHouseNub (0x1460C8830) sets that optional field only for attached buildings, so the stock client's main-building move arrived as 0 and was refused with Housing_InvalidAttachIndex (live log 2026-10-31). A move keeps the building's parts state, preset ownership and contents.
- Crafting-station placement (2026-10-31): the five function-facility building items (Kitchen, Spagyric Table, Atelier, Refinery, Smelting Furnace; Item.category HousingBuilding with both FK_housingId and FK_doodadId) are placed by the stock client as UpdateHousingReq.doodads entries of their FK_doodadId (85001-85005), attached to the lot's main building (live log 2026-10-31: house 1, doodad 11, cms 85002). The catalog mapped doodads only for HousingObject items, so every station save was refused with Housing_InvalidCmsId and nothing was stored. Building items now also resolve their doodad; the save installs one stored copy and removal, move packages and contract release return it. Placing the facility as a house (HousingModelPartAddOn station) is unchanged.
- Storage counts on the wire (2026-11-01): HousingItemCount.quantity now carries the copies still in housing storage (owned minus installed) instead of every owned copy. Static analysis (dumps/ida_research/housing-storage-20261101): AAC_Housing_ApplyHousingItemCount stores quantity per Housing id or doodad id, AAC_Housing_CanPlaceSelectedItem allows a placement while it is above zero and the decor list shows it unchanged. With the owned total the client kept offering objects whose every copy was placed; the save was refused with ItemError and the other new objects in that all-or-nothing save were lost (live log 2026-11-01: two garden plots, a decoration and four furniture pieces). All housing-item serializers (saves, WorldCharHousingItemsNoti, shop, item use, crafting, mail, trade) use world/core housing_item_count_json; persistence keeps the owned total.
- Crafting at placed stations (2026-11-02): live log 2026-11-02 showed the Kitchen (doodad 85002) placed on a lot answering DialogueStartReq 20065 with Interaction_TargetNotFound ('Unable to find target'), because processing resolved stations only from exported map placements. HousingHub::placed_doodad resolves a housing doodad unit ID on a lot of the character's current channel and HousingArea map; the world session hands it to ProcessingSession as a runtime station placement. A StartInteractionAnimReq carrying param.interaction.execute_craft is no longer claimed by the furniture-pose handler, which refused it with Interaction_Invalid. tools/build_processing_data.py now exports the five lot stations 85001-85005 (Smelting, Milling/Kitchen, Carpentry, Trimming, Alchemy) with their own interaction groups and packs.
- Walking into the housing area's zone cells from map 9012 (ZoneChannelMoveReq) enters the character's own channel there, else channel 1, where it stands and without a return point; walking out steps onto map 9012 at the request's reported point (2026-11-02).

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Full original-client acceptance of ordinary contracts, channel visits, edit mode, placement, doors and guild housing remains unverified; GM rental, home teleport and housing scene presentation were observed locally on 2026-10-26. No official housing traffic beyond empty entry snapshots exists in the capture corpus.
- The stock resident-list widget needs pending visit context prepared by normal Residence Entry List navigation. Static client analysis shows that missing context can refuse locally before any front request; complete UI recovery after a scene-only GM teleport and the new reconnect metadata still need original-client acceptance testing.
- Ordinary rental through Nivhen requires the client's dialogue conditions (no house, Blue Salt company level 3, quest 160000 acceptable). Post-repair original-client rental, payment and window state remain unverified; the GM command stays an operator test path.
- PC2S_ReleaseHousingReq and WSC2F_ReleaseHousingReq exist only as schema classes: static analysis found no constructor call, sender or numeric-ID wrapper in this build, and front opcode 20016 is VAcceptQuestReq. Players end a contract with Close (lapse at expiry); operators can use the GM release. The pull-out confirmation is an object interaction, not a release, and is not traced.
- Company membership (Blue Salt) is enforced only by the client's dialogue; the server enforces company position levels. Mate NPC lot spawning is not tied to housing ownership.
- Only Zone_01_Housing_001 has a loadable HousingArea map in this build; leaving a housing area for a recorded map 8000 origin recreates only the tutorial instance. The unknown-origin parent-map exit has no original-client observation.
- Reconciliation assumes one server process owns a world's guild and housing rows. A lost COMMIT acknowledgement during any housing commit leaves the in-memory housing cache stale until restart (later writes on those rows are refused, never overwritten).
- Garden limits: ExecSkillEffect tasks (withering 12000008) are not applied, expertise experience is recorded but not granted, harvest tools (Sickle) are not required (captured doodad gathering never checked tools), only the lot owner may garden, timers advance up to a minute late between interactions, and phase 52's pest removal (no next phase) is unsupported. The summon-mate furniture interaction (OpenSummonMateUI) is client-local and not tied to the lot.
- No distance check applies to poses or garden interactions beyond standing in the lot's channel. No official furniture, garden or late-viewer pose capture exists; the shapes mirror captured gathering and the selfie replay.
- Crafting stations placed on a lot (2026-11-02) are reachable within the lot's corner distance plus the 7 m station allowance around the lot centre (emulator policy): the exact world position of a lot-local object attached to a building is not reproduced. Anyone standing in the lot's channel may use a placed station (Candidate, as with furniture). Building add-on stations 169990 (Crafting Workbench) and 170000 pair a craft interaction with recipes of another expertise and stay refused (listed under the processing profile's unsupported_stations). Original-client acceptance of the repaired station dialogue and crafting at a placed Kitchen remains unverified.
- A refused housing save leaves the client's local placements and storage counts as the player arranged them until the next accepted update or re-entry; the server sends only the error. Original-client acceptance of the stored-count repair (decor list counts after placing and removing objects) is pending.

Follow-up hardening preserves every gameplay, packet, persistence and ordering contract: the world request IDs shared by the frame pipeline, native world and owning features are defined once in world/core/world_request_opcodes.hpp with unchanged values, frame-pipeline route sets for loot, revival, housing, chat, companion/trade, item use, company, equipment, progression, merchant, processing, gathering, utility bag and private combat are asserted across the whole 16-bit opcode range, the full pipeline step order is pinned by literal traces, native world statically ties its credential slice sizes to the transport constants, and party, gathering and guild report once (spdlog error) when a non-empty update is dropped because no delivery is installed. Checked by the default Release suite (0 failures) and the native world smoke; no feature status or packet override changes. Review follow-up preserves every gameplay, packet, persistence and ordering contract: the frame pipeline now exposes its step names so tests pin every composed step in order and dispatch traces for each handler group, the GM and item-use request IDs join the shared request-ID header (private copies alias it), the log-capture test helper drops its logger on destruction, and party, gathering and guild document where their dropped-delivery methods may be called. Checked by the default Release suite (0 failures) and the native world smoke; no feature status or packet override changes. Ordinary-flow follow-up (2026-10-29): live server logs recorded the public-world empty 20012 and its 2041 refusal, plus an earlier ordinary 20013 -> 20015 visit, map 20101 entry and return. Static client research in dumps/ida_research/housing-ordinary-20261029 (14 functions annotated, IDA saved in place with stored-section verification) established the local HousingSiteAuthorize path, channel-0 main-world labelling, row-sourced visit channels and the absence of any release sender. Synthetic checks: chronicles-housing-tests 86 passed with the exported catalog (2 PostgreSQL-gated skips), adding board, contract company-position and guild-directory regressions; the isolated PostgreSQL run passed both housing storage tests; the full Release suite passed 2006 registered tests with 124 prerequisite-gated skips. Revision 6a10874 was deployed to the live server with a verified backup, rollback copies, graceful restart and preserved schema 34 and row counts. Post-deployment original-client rental and board acceptance remain pending. Furniture follow-up (2026-10-30): the live server logged HousingEditModeReq{end} followed about 160 ms later by UpdateHousingReq (331-byte save) and stored nothing (site edit_save_cooldown_start_ticks 0, all 27 storage objects uninstalled). Static analysis confirmed the client's end-then-save order. New synthetic checks replay that order (HousingWorldTest.StockClientSaveOrderPlacesFurnitureThatReentryShows), cover the single trailing save, its 30 s window and refusal closure, customization after customize mode, a restart reload of placed furniture, the exported chair poses and furniture pose start/end fan-out and refusals. The full Release suite passed 2118 registered tests with the exported catalog. Original-client placement, reload and seating on the updated server remain pending. Garden follow-up (2026-10-30): synthetic profile tests, service tests for planting, growth, harvest, missing seeds, stale phases, chained timers and restart persistence, hub tests for the start/execute/end packet order, SP flow, channel fan-out and seated-pose replay, and exporter tests pass; the exported profile loads with 5 doodads, 16 animations and 1 unsupported transition. The default and real-catalog Release suites passed 2151 registered tests. Original-client gardening and late-viewer seating remain unverified. Main-building move follow-up (2026-10-31): the live server refused two stock-client main-building moves with Housing_InvalidAttachIndex because the nub omitted attach_index; static analysis in dumps/ida_research/housing-style-20261031 (12 functions annotated, IDA saved in place) shows the client sets it only for attached buildings and that the world house and build-mode preview both read the same six customization bytes. New synthetic checks HousingPayloads.UpdateRequestTreatsMissingAttachIndexAsMainBuilding and HousingServiceTest.MovingThePresetMainBuildingKeepsIt pass with every housing test; the only Release-suite failures are a combat lightning-storm profile and a quest-catalog count read from shared generated data regenerated after this branch. Original-client acceptance of the move on the updated server remains pending. Crafting-station follow-up (2026-10-31): the live server refused two stock-client station saves (doodads 85002 and 85003 on house 1) with Housing_InvalidCmsId, and the database still held all five station items uninstalled. New synthetic checks HousingServiceTest.CraftingStationsPlacedAsDoodadsInstallTheirBuildingItem (place, second-copy refusal, removal) and the catalog assertions, including the five real station doodads under CHRONICLES_CLIENT_CATALOG, pass with every housing test; the full Release suite passed 2161 of 2162 tests, the one failure being Market.ExportedCatalogAndEveryResponseRoundTrips, which needs data/generated/catalog inside the checkout. Original-client placement and reload of a station on the updated server remain pending. Seedling follow-up (2026-10-31): a player reported that only Barley Seedling could be planted. The live server log showed the stock client sending planting starts and executes only for Barley (interaction 160009), all accepted; the other three seedlings shown in the picker were each held below the authored cost of 5, and no request for them reached the server, so the client withheld them locally (observed local-client behavior; the client-side gate itself was not statically analysed). The authored export gives plot 160066 ten seedlings (5 each), plots 160068 and 160069 seven each (5 and 10), with no server-side seed restriction. New synthetic check HousingServiceTest.EveryExportedSeedlingPlantsEveryGardenPlot runs all 24 exported planting transitions through the service with the real profile: each is refused one seed short and planted with exactly its cost into its authored sown phase; all 107 runnable housing tests pass with CHRONICLES_CLIENT_CATALOG (2 PostgreSQL tests skipped). Original-client planting of the other seedlings with enough seeds remains unobserved. Storage-count follow-up (2026-11-01): the live server refused five stock-client saves with ItemError for objects whose every copy was placed (the database showed installed counts equal to owned counts), while saves of objects with stored copies succeeded. The updated serializer tests (HousingPayloads.ProgressUpdateListsOnlyChangedRows, HousingWorldTest.StockClientSaveOrderPlacesFurnitureThatReentryShows, HousingSessionTest.TutorialStorageSnapshotUsesTheLiveBorrowedProgress, ProcessingTest.HousingConstructionConsumesBlueprintsAndPreservesInstalledCount) pass; the default Release suite passed 2211 of 2212 tests (only Market.ExportedCatalogAndEveryResponseRoundTrips, which needs data/generated in the checkout); with the exported catalog 240 of 242 housing, shop, mail, item-use, processing and trade tests passed, the two failures coming from an adventure profile regenerated by uncommitted exporter work in the main checkout. Original-client acceptance of the decor list counts remains pending. Housing station crafting (2026-11-02): new TLS test NativeWorld.CraftingStationPlacedOnAHousingLotOpensAndCraftsOverTls rents a lot, enters map 20101, saves a Kitchen on the preset main building, opens it with DialogueStartReq and completes a craft (materials 5 -> 3, product 1). With the locator disabled the same test fails because the dialogue request is ignored. HousingWorldTest.PlacedObjectsResolveToTheirLotForOtherServices covers lot, channel, map and object resolution and the craft hand-off from the pose handler. chronicles-housing-tests 106 passed with 5 data/PostgreSQL skips; with CHRONICLES_CLIENT_CATALOG the exported catalog, garden profile and HousingServiceTest.EveryExportedSeedlingPlantsEveryGardenPlot pass. Seedling report (same day): the live log had no StartInteractionAnimReq for the reported Potato planting, so the client refused it locally; every planting consumes 5 seedlings (InteractionCondition ConsumeItem count 5, shown as 'Cost Per Run: 5') and the character held 3. Server-side Barley plantings were accepted on 2026-10-31 and 2026-11-02. No garden behavior changed. Original-client acceptance of station crafting is pending deployment. Unknown-origin exit (2026-11-02, docs/live-issues-20261102.md): a live character that logged in inside map 20101 after a restart was sent to the tutorial start when it walked out. HousingSessionTest.LeavingWithoutARecordedOriginStepsOutOntoTheParentMapInPlace and MapTravel parent-arrival tests (including the generated profile) cover the parent return; synthetic only. Housing walk-in (2026-11-02): HousingSessionTest.WalkingInEntersInPlaceAndWalkingOutReturnsToTheReportedSpot; synthetic only.

- **`PC2S_HousingEditModeReq`** — Owner on its own lot in the current channel. Ending edit mode keeps the session open for the client's trailing UpdateHousingReq (30 s policy). Synthetic tests only; original-client acceptance unverified. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:mode (x5.cms.EX5HousingEditMode); 2:end (bool)
- **`PC2S_UpdateHousingSiteContractExtensionReq`** — Prepay inside the imminent window or Close (Candidate rule); synthetic tests only; original-client acceptance unverified. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:contract_type (x5.cms.EX5HousingContractType)

- **`PC2S_HousingMovePackageRecoverToStorageReq`** — Selected or all owned packages into housing storage; synthetic tests only; original-client acceptance unverified. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:package_ids (repeated sfixed64); 2:all (bool)
- **`PC2S_UpdateHousingReq`** — Placement, move, removal and upgrade validated against catalog bounds, limits, upgrade materials and housing storage. An absent HouseNub.attach_index means a main building (-1); the stock client omits it for main buildings (static analysis 2026-10-31). Accepted during edit mode and once after HousingEditModeReq{end}, which is when the stock client saves (static analysis 2026-10-30); refusals are logged. Synthetic tests only; original-client acceptance unverified. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`.
