## Trading posts, wagons, vouchers and trade runs

**Feature status: IMPLEMENTED.**

Trade-manager dialogue, trade vouchers, goods loading, wagon departure, parking, stowing, selling rewards, cancel, wagon escape, market prices and run persistence.

**Current implementation**

- TradeManager DialogueStartReq/DialogueFunctionReq select the nearest placed trading post and end the dialogue (DialogueEndNoti) so the client opens the trade UI; trade requests require standing within 30 m of that post.
- Voucher crafting charges MakeTradeGood fee and materials, expires after validPeriod minutes and enforces TradeVoucherOwnMaxLimit; WorldCharTradeVoucherNoti lists live vouchers at entry; GM trade_voucher_add grants vouchers.
- TradeGoodLoadingReq consumes vouchers or buys TradingPostGoods goods up to the wagon's 7 slots (ItemsUpdateNoti trade_loading); start=true charges the 100 Gold rental, sends SpawnTradeWagonRes, the wagon UnitAddNoti and MountUnitNoti, then TradeStartNoti.
- TradingPostWagonParkingReq checks the wagon inside the post's async sphere (TradingPostWagonParkingRes); TradingPostWagonRemoveReq stows the wagon and keeps the goods.
- TradeGoodSellReq matches carried units and pays TradingPostPurchase route rewards (items per unit or Gold scaled by the market ratio), the refund rate at the origin or off-route, quality factors and TradeBonusReward rolls in ItemsUpdateNoti trade_sell; a sold-out run ends with TradeEndNoti.
- TradeMarketPriceReq answers TradeMarketPriceRes with deterministic hourly quotes inside the TradeBasicMarket/TradeClampingMarket bands and TradePatternDesc events.
- TradeCancelReq ends the run without refund (ClearTrade dismount, TradeEndNoti); EscapeReq{is_trading} respawns the wagon beside its owner after TradeWagonRespawnCooldown.
- The run (goods with origin and production time, wagon transform and health, last spawn) persists in schema 19; reconnection restores the wagon and TradeWagonPosNoti; TradeStartNoti follows at entry only for an owner already driving (region re-entry), otherwise when the owner next boards the wagon (RideUnitReq) or trade escape seats it, after MountUnitNoti.
- Full-wallet deliveries (2026-11-01): CUSTOM: trade-run delivery and bonus credits above the wallet limit fill the wallet to the limit instead of failing the delivery.
- Driven trade wagons checkpoint the character position and wagon progress in one revision-guarded commit before a region handoff; reentry reuses the existing wagon and its goods.
- One world-server process serializes character admission and close settlement; entry advances the revision before reading. Failed wagon and position settlements are retained in memory and reconciled before the next bootstrap.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Reward numbers, purchase prices, market model, event ratios, escape placement and the dialogue-end UI trigger are Candidate: the client only displays server values and no official trade capture exists.
- TradeEventResultNoti, RemoteTradeVehicleRes and OnDemandDynamicCharTradeCompletionsNoti are not emitted (this client ignores the first two); random encounter events and daily trade permits have no client tables.
- Voucher company-level conditions now use the character's company standing and require a valid pioneer permit (ignorePermit false); original-client voucher acceptance is unverified. Only posts 1000 and 1100 lie on the one map the live server places characters on (9012).
- Original-client trade runs remain unverified. One original-client observation (2026-11-01): an owner reconnecting on foot with the wagon out saw the world turn black about 3 s after entry while play continued; static analysis traced it to TradeStartNoti (fixed by deferring it). Acceptance of the deferred announcement, and whether a stowed run's sale needs a non-idle client trade state, are unverified.
- Recovery from an unknown database acknowledgement closes the session and relies on reconnecting to durable state; original-client driving and multi-passenger handoffs remain unverified.
- Pending close recovery is process-local and is lost if the server stops during an outage. A close exception before recovery can be captured retains the character admission and has no automated operator recovery. External writers and multiple server processes are not fenced.

**Evidence and verification**

Static client analysis (70 annotated functions) and the tradingpost.json layers define the contract. Synthetic tests cover loading limits, departure order, parking, stowing, route and refund rewards, cancel, escape cooldown, reconnection, GM vouchers and wagon destruction; an end-to-end TLS test runs a full 1100 -> 1000 run on map 9012 with the exported catalog. No official capture or original-client acceptance exists. **Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`PC2S_TradeCancelReq`** — Ends the run without refund, removes the wagon and sends TradeEndNoti. Schema file: `p_c2s.trade.proto`. Fields: Empty protobuf body.
- **`PC2S_TradeMarketPriceReq`** — Answered with the current market window for every placed post. Schema file: `p_c2s.trade.proto`. Fields: Empty protobuf body.
- **`PC2S_TradeGoodLoadingReq`** — Loads vouchers or post goods (start=false) and departs with the wagon (start=true). Schema file: `p_c2s.trade.proto`. Fields: 1:add_goods (repeated x5.pb.TradeGoodIdentity); 2:wagon_cms_id (int32); 3:start (bool)
- **`PC2S_TradeGoodSellReq`** — Sells carried units at the parked post or origin; route, refund, quality and bonus rewards (Candidate numbers). Schema file: `p_c2s.trade.proto`. Fields: 1:goods (repeated x5.pb.TradeGoods)
- **`PC2S_TradingPostWagonParkingReq`** — Parks the owner's wagon inside the post's async sphere. Schema file: `p_c2s.trade.proto`. Fields: 1:trading_post_cms_id (int32)
- **`PC2S_TradingPostWagonRemoveReq`** — Stows the parked wagon (no typed reply); the goods remain for selling. Schema file: `p_c2s.trade.proto`. Fields: Empty protobuf body.
- **`PS2C_RemoteTradeVehicleRes`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode)
- **`PS2C_SpawnTradeWagonRes`** — Empty after a departure or escape spawn; Trade_WagonSpawnFailed/NotInProgress otherwise. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode)
- **`PS2C_OnDemandDynamicCharTradeCompletionsNoti`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_s2c.character.proto`. Fields: 1:trading_post_conn_data (repeated int64)
- **`PS2C_WorldCharTradeVoucherNoti`** — Live vouchers in the non-tutorial entry snapshot. Schema file: `p_s2c.character.proto`. Fields: 1:vouchers (repeated x5.pb.TradeVoucher)
- **`PS2C_TradeStartNoti`** — Carried goods after the wagon UnitAddNoti/MountUnitNoti at departure, region re-entry while driving, and the first boarding or trade escape after a reconnection on foot. The client switches the screen to opaque black on this packet and its 0.5 s trade tick restores it only while the local character rides a vehicle, so it is never sent to an owner on foot. Schema file: `p_s2c.trade.proto`. Fields: 1:trade_goods (repeated x5.pb.TradeGoods)
- **`PS2C_TradeEndNoti`** — After a sold-out run, a cancel or a destroyed wagon. Schema file: `p_s2c.trade.proto`. Fields: Empty protobuf body.
- **`PS2C_TradeWagonPosNoti`** — Wagon position after the owner gets off and at every entry with the wagon out. Schema file: `p_s2c.trade.proto`. Fields: 1:pos (x5.pb.WorldPos)
- **`PS2C_TradeEventResultNoti`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_s2c.trade.proto`. Fields: 1:result (x5.cms.EX5TradeEventResult); 2:dead_count (int32)
- **`PS2C_TradeMarketPriceRes`** — next_update_tick at the window end; group_patterns map EX5TradeGoodGroup to TradePatternDesc ids (Candidate model). Schema file: `p_s2c.trade.proto`. Fields: 1:next_update_tick (sfixed64); 2:trading_posts (repeated x5.pb.TradeMarketPriceRes.TradingPost)
- **`PS2C_TradingPostWagonParkingRes`** — Echoes the post; ec Trade_InvalidPost/NotInProgress/PostTooFar on refusal. Schema file: `p_s2c.trade.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode); 2:trading_post_cms_id (int32)

## Player marketplace (auction listings)

**Feature status: IMPLEMENTED.**

Realm-scoped fixed-price auction listing registration, query, purchase, revoke, separate item/proceeds claims, details and participant history for catalog-allowlisted equipment/materials.

**Current implementation**

- All seven native world request/reply pairs execute on the authenticated character worker. The hash-verified allowlist (177 items in this export), item storage rules and main/subcategory definitions gate registration; equipped, polished, statically bound and unsupported items are refused.
- MemoryStore and PostgreSQL schema 24 atomically escrow items, debit buyer Gold, reserve the buyer and persist independent seller/buyer claim receipts under the character revision and listing snapshot. Competing purchases, stale revisions and repeated claims cannot duplicate or partially transfer assets.
- Revocation and exclusive wall-clock expiry preserve escrow until the seller settles it. The listing-details primary action of the client sends MarketRevokeReq for every listing on the registered tab, including Retrieve on an expired listing; the seller's revoke of a closed, unsold (expired or cancelled) listing therefore returns its escrow atomically through the same durable seller receipt as MarketClaimReq, while a sold listing still refuses with Market_NotSellRegisterCancel. Buyer claims return equipment attributes or material quantities; seller claims return sale proceeds. Settlement works while the other participant is offline and survives PostgreSQL store/server reconstruction.
- Queries implement public, registered-by-me (listings whose seller assets are still unsettled, so a retrieved listing does not reappear after the client re-queries) and unclaimed lists; optional category filters; stable latest and ascending/descending price ordering; bounded pagination and totals. Details and buy/sell history enforce participant visibility for closed listings.
- Committed inventory updates report resulting stacks, Gold and granted instance IDs before market replies. Tutorial caches adopt the committed revision; character deletion refuses outstanding marketplace assets. Registration keys use a random connection scope plus native sequence and contain no authentication material.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- No official market workflow exists in the reviewed captures, and no original-client marketplace UI/ordering/time-unit acceptance trial has completed. Schema/catalog evidence and synthetic service/storage/TLS verification remain distinct.
- Explicit emulator policies: total listing price in Gold; zero listing fee/tax; no extra level gate or relisting cooldown; at most 100 outstanding seller listings; pages/history capped at 100; one-day, three-day and 60-second RapidTest periods; whole-listing purchases with separate claims. Official fees, price bands, priceCustomOverride and cooldown semantics are unresolved.
- Only existing inventory equipment/material representations are supported. Runtime socket/binding/expiration flags are not represented; unsupported future states must gain eligibility checks before they can trade. Purchase/claim retries name durable listing IDs; a registration with a new sequence or connection is a new operation because this schema has no stable client idempotency key.
- Implementation and validation do not migrate the running database, restart/deploy the service or establish original-client compatibility.
- Retrieve semantics are static client recovery plus synthetic verification: the client shows system message 441 (instead of the cancel message 440) for a successful revoke of a listing flagged at details offset +257, but that flag's writer and the localized texts were not recovered, and the fixed server has not yet been tried with the original client. Whether official servers also return a cancelled listing's item immediately is unknown; this emulator keeps cancel as escrow-until-settled.

**Evidence and verification**

2026-10-26 Release: nine marketplace C++ cases pass; the PostgreSQL case passes in a stopped disposable cluster, including durable receipts/store recreation, concurrent purchase/claim races and stale-revision rollback. The two-player HTTP/TLS smoke passes all seven requests and tutorial revision adoption. Six existing memory/native auth/chat/guild/world/mail integrations, the isolated PostgreSQL runner, 11 reference-generator tests and Python compilation pass. TLS uses the existing child-process OPENSSL_ia32cap=0 diagnostic. No full emulator-suite run, official market capture, original-client trial, production migration or deployment. ## Mail, storage boxes and delivery history

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Front REST mailbox/confirm/delete, storage boxes, purchase history and dynamic storage.

**Current implementation**

- Operator-to-player account or character mail persists in MemoryStore/PostgreSQL schema 23 with stable delivery keys, bounded inboxes, read receipts, exclusive expiry and safe all-or-nothing deletion.
- Matching-build IDA establishes PUT front MailboxGetReq, MailboxConfirmReq and MailboxDeleteReq routes and POST MailboxTakeAttachmentReq/{mail_id}; the native bearer/protobuf adapters implement listing, confirmation, deletion and asynchronous claims.
- Claims execute on the active character worker and atomically commit inventory, Gold/HersanderToken, stackable/housing rewards and the durable claim receipt under the gameplay revision. Retries or competing characters cannot grant twice; tutorial caches adopt the committed revision.
- Online delivery sends PS2C_MailInDeliveryNewRes to the addressed account/character only. Claims send PS2C_ItemsUpdateNoti.system with the matching account_mail_id/char_mail_id, committed item IDs and resulting quantities/balances.
- Authenticated operator POST /admin/v1/mail and the desktop Mail form deliver text, catalog-backed equipment/material/housing items and supported currencies with retry-stable delivery keys.
- Emulator policy: the first character of an account that finishes the tutorial (the cutscene map move into the overworld, not a GM teleport) causes one account-addressed welcome mail with 20 health potions and 10 stamina potions to be delivered under the stable key tutorial-completion-supplies-v1. The key makes it once per account and realm across characters and retries; it is announced with PS2C_MailInDeliveryNewRes (account_mail) only when newly created, and a delivery failure is logged without blocking the map move.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Paid-shop storage boxes, purchase history and dynamic item-storage transfers are separate unimplemented services; operator mail does not implement purchases.
- No official mail capture or original-client mailbox rendering/claim acceptance trial has completed. Routes/fields are static recovery; expiry, limits, online-only claims and receipt policies are emulator choices.
- A claim requires a live world session and the required item catalog. It refuses missing items, unsupported rewards, capacity/currency limits, expired attachments and stale revisions without consuming rewards.

## Rankings, raids and channel events

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Leaderboard queries and operator-timed records, bounded raid matchmaking/lifecycle/travel, map status and tribute offerings.

**Current implementation**

- RankingListReq returns catalog-backed bounded lists, own rank and reset/refresh metadata. MemoryStore and PostgreSQL schema 28 keep one best elapsed-time record per holder and period with atomic conditional upserts; PostgreSQL lists and own ranks share a repeatable-read snapshot and byte-wise holder-key ordering. GM-authorized ranking_start/finish/cancel commands exercise server-timed records; accepted finishes are consumed even on ambiguous storage failures.
- RaidUI-backed registration/cancel/matched roster/leave/detach/timeout destruction span world connections. FIFO full groups or 30-second partial groups form under a lock; one active group per map prevents simultaneous unrelated groups sharing the map-only transport. A departing group reserves its map until each session has left shared presence or disconnected. Cancellation/leaving and eviction acknowledgements check the owning connection.
- A matched RaidChannelMoveReq uses server-tracked coordinates from the raid's parent map and the normal in-connection map handshake. Leave/timeout returns to the saved entry point; raid positions are checkpointed at that parent-map point rather than persisting an ephemeral instance. Housing travel preserves the public origin; recovered housing origins pointing to raids resolve to the public parent. Generic server/GM travel cannot bypass raid admission and the saved return-point requirement.
- Verified extraction produces 111 map-event bindings and five map/altar placements. Tribute queries and item contributions validate map, target, range, item, count, living state and ownership. Serialized item commits prevent failed or pending charges completing the offering count; committed costs report ItemsUpdateNoti.tribute and resulting count.
- The in-memory board supports status notification and local target-10 tribute completion. GM status/reset commands and the existing channel_event_info debug panel reflect this state. ChannelTriggerEntryReq reuses authored ungated MapChannels boundaries and checks the requested destination against the resolved map.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Full official gameplay remains incomplete: authored channel-event objectives/tasks, raid boss encounters, automatic score qualification, reward settlement/mail, persistent event recovery and complete CheckChannelEventStatus condition integration are not implemented. GM completion sets a status only; it does not execute an objective or grant rewards.
- Raid queues/channels and tribute/status state are process-local. Tribute inventory costs are durable, but counts/status are not crash-atomic with them. Only one active group per raid map; no independent multiple-instance simulation or recovered schedule. Entry keeps parent-map coordinates; authored spawn/portal policy is unresolved.
- Matching wait/minimum, the 32-query-per-second connection budget, tribute target/range/audience, daily/weekly reset anchors, holder policy and party participants chosen at finish are local choices. Server/World ranking types read the same local board; no cross-server aggregation. Gated channel destinations and unresolved spawn rules fail closed.
- Official evidence remains 16 empty ranking-list exchanges and one unrelated Success status notification, with no score-record or raid/tribute capture. No original-client acceptance or live deployment has completed.

**Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`PC2S_RankingListReq`** — Catalog-backed bounded local board query with own rank and reset/refresh metadata; Server/World types share one local board. A local per-connection bound allows 32 queries per second before storage; excess requests receive sequenced BadRequest. Synthetic tests; original-client acceptance unverified. Schema file: `p_c2s.session.proto`. Fields: 1:ranking_cms_id (int32); 2:ranking_record_type (x5.pb.ERankingRecordType)
- **`PC2S_ChannelEventTributeCountReq`** — Reports the nearest verified altar's process-local offering count within a local 10 m range; target 10 is a local choice, not recovered event scripting. Synthetic only. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: Empty protobuf body.
- **`PC2S_ChannelEventItemTributeReq`** — Validates placement/map/range/item/count/living state/owned stack, serializes the durable inventory commit with in-memory count/status publication and emits tribute inventory updates. Counts are not crash-durable; target/rewards/scripts unresolved. Synthetic only. Schema file: `p_c2s.item.proto`. Fields: 1:item_cms_id (int32); 2:count (int32); 3:target_unit_id (uint64); 15:packet_seq (x5.pb.PacketSeq)
- **`PC2S_ChannelTriggerEntryReq`** — Map travel planner: map_id 0 leaves an instance for its parent; a child map is entered from its entry volume or authored area after MapCondition checks. Without the travel profile the ungated MapChannels boundary route remains. Synthetic TLS only. Schema file: `p_c2s.mapmove.proto`. Fields: 1:map_id (int32); 2:pos (x5.pb.WorldPos); 3:body_yaw (float)
- **`PC2S_RaidChannelMoveReq`** — Matched-map travel from its parent after the countdown and before expiry, with connection ownership, tracked coordinates, range/context/busy/dead checks and normal map handshake; entry-point persistence and leave return. Raid-specific spawn policy and encounter simulation are unresolved; synthetic only. Schema file: `p_c2s.mapmove.proto`. Fields: 1:map_id (int32); 2:pos (x5.pb.WorldPos); 3:body_yaw (float)
- **`PC2S_RaidChannelRegisterReq`** — Authenticated catalog-backed FIFO application with duplicate/context validation, full-group or local 30-second partial matching. One active group per map; process-local and synthetic only. Schema file: `p_c2s.raid_channel.proto`. Fields: 1:map_id (int32)
- **`PC2S_RaidChannelCancelReq`** — Removes only the requester's queued map application on its owning connection and acknowledges cancellation. Synthetic only. Schema file: `p_c2s.raid_channel.proto`. Fields: 1:map_id (int32)
- **`PC2S_RaidChannelLeaveReq`** — Removes an owned matched seat, notifies its roster and schedules return from the raid map. Stale connections cannot remove a seat. Synthetic only; encounter semantics unverified. Schema file: `p_c2s.raid_channel.proto`. Fields: 1:map_id (int32)
- **`PS2C_RankingRecordStartRes`** — GM-authorized ranking_start begins a server-timed attempt; no automatic authored encounter start or official record capture. Synthetic only. Schema file: `p_s2c.session.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode); 2:ranking_cms_id (int32); 3:start_tick (sfixed64)
- **`PS2C_RankingRecordRes`** — GM-authorized ranking_finish stores a server-clock elapsed time and returns the best standing. No automatic boss qualification, immutable start roster or ranking reward settlement. Synthetic only. Schema file: `p_s2c.session.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode); 2:ranking_cms_id (int32); 3:time_record_milli (sfixed64); 4:party_ranking (x5.pb.RankingInfo)
- **`PS2C_RankingListRes`** — Reports stored best times, bounded top list, own entry/rank and reset/refresh metadata. PostgreSQL list and own rank share one snapshot during concurrent finishes. Monthly 10:00 UTC reset matches captured empty-board metadata; nonempty ranking policy is local and synthetically verified. Schema file: `p_s2c.session.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode); 2:rankings (repeated x5.pb.RankingInfo); 3:next_timestamp (sfixed64); 4:reset_counter (int64); 5:ranking_cms_id (int32); 6:ranking_record_type (x5.pb.ERankingRecordType); 7:my_ranking (x5.pb.RankingInfo); 8:is_settling (bool); 9:next_reset_epochtime (sfixed64)
- **`PS2C_ChangeChannelEventStatusNoti`** — Local tribute-threshold Success and GM status/reset notifications; no general event objective/task interpreter, complete condition integration or scripted encounter outcomes. Synthetic only. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:status_type (x5.cms.EX5ChannelEventStatusType)
- **`PS2C_ChannelEventTributeCountNoti`** — Returns or broadcasts committed count and local target 10; failed item commits cannot complete a count. Process-local state; official target/audience and event recovery unverified. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:count (int32); 2:target_count (int32)
- **`PS2C_RaidChannelRegisterNoti`** — Acknowledges the accepted catalog-backed application to its owning connection. Synthetic only. Schema file: `p_s2c.raid_channel.proto`. Fields: 1:map_id (int32)
- **`PS2C_RaidChannelCancelNoti`** — Acknowledges removal of the owned queued application. Synthetic only. Schema file: `p_s2c.raid_channel.proto`. Fields: 1:map_id (int32)
- **`PS2C_RaidChannelMatchedNoti`** — Fan-out of the authenticated matched roster under a bounded local FIFO policy; one active group per map, no independently simulated raid instances. Synthetic only, original-client countdown/entry unobserved. Schema file: `p_s2c.raid_channel.proto`. Fields: 1:map_id (int32); 2:members (repeated x5.pb.raidchannel.RaidChannelMember)
- **`PS2C_RaidChannelLeaveNoti`** — Reports the leaving/disconnected character to the matched roster, removes its seat and schedules return for an online leaver. Synthetic only. Schema file: `p_s2c.raid_channel.proto`. Fields: 1:map_id (int32); 2:char_id (sfixed64)
- **`PS2C_RaidChannelDestroyNoti`** — Timeout destroys the process-local matched channel, notifies members and requests parent-map return. The map stays reserved until every evicted session leaves shared presence or disconnects. No authored encounter completion flow. Synthetic only. Schema file: `p_s2c.raid_channel.proto`. Fields: 1:map_id (int32)

## Paid shop, Steam purchases and preorder rewards

**Feature status: MISSING.**

Paid purchases, premium currency charge/delivery and preorder state/claims.

**Current implementation**

- No behavior-producing runtime service established.
- Authenticated PreorderBonusStateReq answers PreorderBonusStateRes and PreorderBonusClaimReq answers PreorderBonusClaimRes, both with NotEligible. No entitlement or reward is invented.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- No payment/ticket verification, entitlement ledger, premium balance or exactly-once delivery exists.
- Captured preorder-state polls do not prove claiming or a paid transaction.

## Diagnostics, GM commands and anti-cheat messaging

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

GM/debug packets, runtime diagnostic overlays and front Xigncode challenge messages.

**Current implementation**

- A game-master handoff sets WorldCharBaseNoti.gm=true in the bootstrap notification; static research shows the client then enables its Tilde GM console. Chat lines starting with `/gm ` reach the same GmCmdTextReq path.
- PC2S_GmCmdTextReq and PC2S_GmCmdReq run only for game-master handoffs, at most four requests per second, through bounded parsers in a fixed order: diagnostics (src/world/features/gm/gm_diagnostics.cpp), combat/quest/mail commands (src/world/features/gm/gm_world_commands.cpp), session commands (src/world/features/gm/gm_tools.cpp), housing, companion/trade and inventory/progression (src/world/features/gm/gm_commands.cpp). Replies are private `[GM]` chat lines because the client discards PS2C_DebugText; command and reply text are never logged.
- Inventory and progression commands commit under the character revision and report ItemsUpdateNoti with the command reason: item_add (NPC-shop storage rules), add_money (gold, 0..Money.limitUserMax), set_weapon_durability (equipped Weapon_1/Weapon_2 instances, capped at Item.maxDurability, committed as durability updates guarded by the previous value), exp_up, set_level, add/set_char_build_point, reset_stat_bonus and force_reset_perk (src/world/features/character/progression.cpp).
- Session commands (tp and up/down/fwd typed inside a housing area use the field it overlays, map 20101 -> 9012, so they leave the area instead of loading an empty copy of it): pos, tp, tp_map, up/down/fwd, goto, summon, players, god (GmCmd.invincible), invisible, stamina, fly (GmCmd.fly_mode), heal (GmCmd.regen), revive (GmCmd.revive from the GM resurrection button), spawn_npc/despawn_npcs (GmCmd.spawn_npc, despawn_npc_all), complete_quests/complete_quest (GmCmd.completable_quest_all, completable_quest, complete_quest_progress, reward_quest), reveal_map/unlock_map (text-only, persisted catalog fog union for the issuing character; reselect to reload), suicide (GmCmd.suicide: lethal environmental damage that ignores GM protection and is persisted by the normal death commit), kick (GmCmd.test_kick, 0-60 s, own connection only, normal close path) and announce (GmCmd.announce: one World chat notice per realm character through the operator notice path, sender `[GM]`, 1-200 bytes).
- Companion, trade and housing GM commands keep their own parsers: spawn_operable, damage_vehicle, register/spawn/despawn_summon_npc, register/spawn/despawn/invite_mate_npc, add_mate_intimate, trade_voucher_add and housing GmCmd fields 56, 74, 96, 103, 104, 115, 116, 123 and 126, plus the emulator-defined text command housing_contract. Housing GM commands answer with private [GM] chat lines (applied, rented lot, or refusal code and next step).
- World clock override: `game_time [stop] <hour 0-24> [day_seconds]` or GmCmd.game_time sends PS2C_WorldGameTimeNoti (158) to the issuing client only: started_timestamp = now (Unix s), one_day_secs 60-604800 (default 3600, an emulator choice), daily_ratio = hour/24 and stopped. Static evidence: the client handler reaches the world time manager (running clock shifted back by the ratio, or a clock frozen at ratio x day). Not persisted or broadcast.
- Debug watch: GmCmd.debug_watch (sent by the client's own debug UI with add true/false) and `watch <unit_id|me|spawned> [position|path|ai|all]` / `unwatch [unit_id]` keep up to 8 overlays per session for the GM's own unit, server-simulated combat monsters and other units announced on the current map. The server sends an immediate snapshot, then refreshes every 500 ms while the session has gameplay timers: DebugPositionNoti (152), DebugPathNoti (151: current point and the running route end) and DebugAINoti (150: one node named after the emulator AI state; phase numbering is emulator-defined). AbnormalStatus and SkillCollision watches are refused; watches clear on GM map changes and drop units that leave the session.
- `regen_stat` or GmCmd.debug_player_regen_stat sends DebugPlayerRegenStatNoti (155) with HPRegen, SPRegen, SatietyRegen, Health/MaxHealth and Stamina/MaxStamina from the authoritative combat stats.
- `channel_event_info` or GmCmd.channel_event_info sends DebugChannelEventInfoNoti (159) from the channel-event board: current map, recovered event binding and local Success state, with no fabricated objective/save data. `debug_npc_field` remains a private refusal. GM ranking_start/finish/cancel exercise server-timed leaderboard records; raid_channel_enter forms a bounded match; complete_channel_event_objective and reset_channel_event_save_data set/reset local status without executing authored objectives or rewards.
- Emulator-owned operator console: optional bearer-authenticated /admin/v1 routes provide realm settings, account roles and bans, session revocation, offline character edits, notices, rates/events, log viewing and graceful shutdown. The Windows desktop console keeps credentials in native memory and uses the existing WebView2 host. This is an emulator administration interface, not an official client protocol. In-game reactions and desktop operation remain separate acceptance checks.
- Operator diagnostics: the console tails a bounded in-memory ring of the latest 5,000 server log records (sequence cursor, level filter, eviction/restart gap report) and changes the spdlog level at runtime. Log text keeps the server's existing redaction.
- GM spawn_npc: complete catalog-backed private test monsters can pursue/fight on tutorial and open-world maps. They are visible only to the issuing GM, not public shared-world population; incomplete profiles stay visual-only. See docs/gm-commands.md and docs/npc-locomotion-fix-20261026.md.
- Additional bounded GM world commands (src/world/features/gm/gm_world_commands.cpp): private monster kill/damage (percent of current HP, normal defeat observer once; the extracted ordinary defeat helper preserves its state/death notification order and corpse ownership contract), timed status add/remove and abnormal gauges, cancel_skill, server cooldown clearing, AI pause/resume, private NPC placement/self teleport, temporary nonnegative combat stats and clear, and prevalidated self-effect chains of at most eight supported healing/status/recovery/gauge operations. Unit edits are restricted to the issuing character or its private combat-enabled GM spawns; no shared population or other player is edited. Cooldown display reset and original-client acceptance are unverified.
- GM quest acceptance on shared maps bypasses NPC/range and optionally retains catalog conditions, grants ordinary supported supplies and commits revision-guarded progress before packets; saved quests cannot be restarted. GM mail uses the existing validated delivery store, authenticated online/self recipients with account ownership checks, a random key per command, one attachment kind and a 30-day lifetime; uncertain delivery outcomes explicitly warn against blind retries. No new storage schema is introduced.
- GM itembag_clear preserves equipment and utility-slot stack reservations under the existing atomic item-trade contract. add/set_stat_bonus grants bounded bonuses without spending points; learn_all_perks retains prerequisites/exclusive choices. Movement aliases debug_ghost, map_move, set_pos_and_yaw and follow_user map to bounded server protection, explicit map/coordinate travel and one-time goto respectively; unsupported structured selector/follower variants fail closed. See docs/gm-command-catalog.md for every recovered field and its limits.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Unserved GmCmd operations are explicitly listed in docs/gm-command-catalog.md (all 126 recovered fields, not an all-implemented claim): class changes; quest abandonment/removal and job boards; forced NPC skills, reaction/faction/root-motion/spawner control; class gauges; guild/companies; achievements/expertise/world level and direct GM Nui blessing-level assignment (ordinary shrine offerings are separate); content unlock/reset counters; channel incidents and channel-number changes; party channels; premium currency, purchases and preorder rewards; standalone projectile/skill/destructible spawns; doodad/adventure-object GM overrides; mesh/navigation diagnostics. combat_formula_log and stat_sync_warning report their limitation but do not implement toggles. Official GMCommand.csv grammar, continuous follow, offline GM mail recipients, status stacks above one and arbitrary effect execution remain unsupported.
- debug_npc_field, DebugNpcFieldNoti (157), DebugDrawMeshNoti (156) and DebugCollisionShapeNoti (153) are not produced: the server keeps no NPC navigation field, navigation mesh or collision geometry. raycast and togglegraze are client-local console commands.
- Original-client acceptance of the new GM/diagnostic paths remains unverified here. Whether the shipping client instantiates its X5 debug subsystem (overlay visibility) is unresolved; the world clock path is static evidence only; the official default day length, watch cadence and AI phase numbering are unknown.
- No in-client reply packet for refusals exists: no GM response packet was recovered and this client binds PS2C_DebugText (149) to a no-op handler, so replies use private chat. Whether SystemMessageNoti.text renders is unresolved.
- No Xigncode query/response service is implemented; anti-cheat messaging was out of scope for this change.
- Keep diagnostic logging separate from enabling privileged protocol operations; never expose unauthenticated GM execution.
- The historical raw research artifacts previously linked here are no longer present in this checkout after workspace cleanup. Existing historical findings are retained as recorded evidence, not newly reproduced analysis.

**Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`PC2S_GmCmdReq`** — Game-master handoffs only. Bounded served oneofs include debug/watch/time, session protection/movement (map/position only, one-time follow_user), private monster kill/damage/status/gauge/AI/cancel/move, temporary stats, supported self-effect chains, server cooldown clearing, quest acceptance/completion, online/self durable mail, item/money/durability/bag clearing, stat/perk/build grants, companion/trade, local event/raid administration and housing. docs/gm-command-catalog.md enumerates all 126 fields and remaining unavailable operations. Unsupported selectors, extra followers, status stacks above one, arbitrary effect targets, premium and other absent systems are refused rather than promoted. Client cooldown reset and original-client compatibility are unverified; synthetic evidence only. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:cmds (repeated x5.pb.GmCmd)
- **`PC2S_GmCmdTextReq`** — Game-master handoffs only (four per second). Emulator text grammar for the diagnostics, combat/quest/mail, session, inventory/progression, companion and housing commands listed in docs/gm-commands.md and all 126 fields in docs/gm-command-catalog.md, including reveal_map/unlock_map: durable catalog-wide fog union for the issuing character, with character re-selection required for the recovered load path. Missing/invalid catalogs fail closed; no live fog-refresh opcode or zone-access change is claimed. Unknown commands, non-GM senders and rate-limited requests get a private refusal. Synthetic tests only. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:text (string)
- **`PS2C_DebugText`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_s2c.debug.proto`. Fields: 1:text (string)
- **`PS2C_DebugAINoti`** — Debug watch AI overlay for NpcAi monsters: phase and one Running node named Idle, Engaged or Returning (emulator numbering; the official behavior-tree nodes are unknown). Schema file: `p_s2c.debug.proto`. Fields: 1:unit_id (uint64); 2:phase (int32); 3:nodes (repeated x5.pb.debug.BtNode); 4:attacker_slot_idx (int32)
- **`PS2C_DebugPathNoti`** — Debug watch Path overlay: the current point and the running route end of a server-simulated monster. Overlay rendering depends on the client debug subsystem (Candidate). Schema file: `p_s2c.debug.proto`. Fields: 1:unit_id (uint64); 2:paths (repeated x5.pb.DebugPathNoti.Point)
- **`PS2C_DebugPositionNoti`** — Debug watch Position overlay for the GM's own unit, combat monsters and announced units; snapshot plus 500 ms refresh. Overlay rendering depends on the client debug subsystem (Candidate). Schema file: `p_s2c.debug.proto`. Fields: 1:unit_id (uint64); 2:pos (x5.pb.WorldPos); 3:yaw (float)

## Conversational AI agent-engine REST services

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Client AI chat with house mates (agent list/load, knowledge search, converse, suggested player replies, summaries and agent memories) on the client's hard-coded agent-engine URL, plus the recovered status/location/action/schedule/plan DTOs that no client code uses in this build.

**Current implementation**

- Static contract (dumps/ida_research/ai-rest-20261026, 37 annotated functions): the front REST client sends protobuf JSON with proto field names, without Authorization, to a hard-coded private client base endpoint (hostname omitted from this reference) and reads only HTTP 200-206 bodies with a strict parser.
- Agent engine service (src/services/agent_engine/agent_engine*.cpp, --agent-engine-port, loopback peers unless --agent-engine-allow-remote true) serves all eight client routes: GET base, GET /agents/list, POST /agent/{id}/load, /converse, /summarize-conversation, /add-memory, /generate-player-response and /search/knowledge-hybrid, with bounded validation and exact response field sets.
- Agents come from AIChatNpcAgent (NPC 35 Seren -> agent 2) and AIChatPlayerAgent (Fight/Nuian/Male -> agent 0) plus config/agent-engine/agents.json personas; knowledge from config/agent-engine/knowledge.json and personas, returned as "text, Distance:d".
- Conversations keyed by (speaker, partner) end at max_conversation_turn (default 10, at most 50), on a goodbye or when forced, with a summary; memories are rated 1-10 and persisted per agent (PostgreSQL schema 26 or the memory store) and recalled in replies.
- Dialogue model: deterministic ScriptedDialogueModel by default; optional OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint (--agent-engine-model-url/--agent-engine-model, plain HTTP, 20 s deadline) with scripted fallback; conversation text is not logged.
- Launcher: starts the server with --agent-engine-port (setting agent_engine_port, default 38011) and rewrites heap FStrings holding the official base URL to http://<server host>:<port> in place with original-byte backups and restore (agent_engine_redirect); the executable image is not changed.

**Custom / guessed behavior (not official)**

Our own guesses, because the data to reproduce the official behavior does not exist. They add no capture evidence and do not promote any status.

- Our own design, not official: emulator-defined routes /time-and-status, /select-location, /select-action, /breakdown-schedule and /agent/{id}/make-plan with a keyword-matching planner; the scripted dialogue model; IDF keyword coverage plus trigram knowledge scoring; and the emulator-authored personas and knowledge in config/agent-engine (docs/agent-engine.md).

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- No original-client session has reached the emulator's agent engine; in-game display of replies, options and memory lines and the live redirect are unverified.
- The official language model, prompts, knowledge base and ranking are unknown; replies come from the scripted model or an operator-supplied model.
- This client build only has a Fight/Nuian/Male player agent row, so other class/race/gender combinations cannot start AI chat without client data changes.
- Status, location, action, schedule and plan DTOs have no client caller; their routes and planner are emulator-defined (custom).
- The service has no client credential: memories are per agent, shared by every player of a server, and remote access is opt-in on trusted networks only.
- The GeneratePlayerResponseReq agent_id/player_id order is not fully resolved (both orders are accepted).

**Evidence and verification**

Static analysis of the matching client build (IDA, saved in place; dumps/ida_research/ai-rest-20261026/FINDINGS.md) establishes the routes, JSON transport, base URL, agent tables and knowledge filter. Synthetic checks (2026-10-26): 19 chronicles-agent-engine-tests cases (JSON contract and field sets, conversation endings, memory recall/retention, knowledge format, planning routes, model fallback); integration.agent_engine replays the client's route order over HTTP against chronicles-server; 6 AgentEngineRedirect launcher cases and the 9 existing AuthRedirect cases pass after the shared FString patch refactor. A read-only usermode scan of a running client found one writable UTF-16 copy of the base URL; its owning FString header was not confirmed before access was refused. Observed original-client AI chat: none. Source layout move (phase 1a of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-27-modular-emulator-architecture-design.md): every src/ file moved into its module folder listed in tools/source_layout.json; only includes, src/CMakeLists.txt source paths and src/ path references changed. No packet, persistence or gameplay behavior changed. Checks: Release build, the full CTest run with the same test names and results as before the move (including the registered Python smoke tests), and tools/test_move_sources.py. Phase 1b-1 review fixes: comment and documentation paths corrected after the persistence split, include blocks re-sorted, and progress_packets.hpp includes nlohmann/json directly. No behavior change. Checks: Release build, full CTest (1568 tests, 0 failures), tools.module_includes. Portal storage module (phase 1b-2): portal_store and its tests moved from services/portal to services/portal_storage so the launcher's portal content module needs no PostgreSQL. The chronicles-portal-storage library, the chronicles-portal-tests program and its CTest names are unchanged; only include paths, src/CMakeLists.txt source paths, the tools/source_layout.json module list and its declared same-layer edge changed. No packet, persistence or gameplay behavior changed. Checks: Release build, full CTest (1568 tests, 0 failures), tools.module_includes. Refactor: AuthService and server/account_main wiring now use the narrow AccountRepository, CharacterRepository and CharacterStateRepository interfaces (src/persistence/character_repositories.hpp) instead of Store; the shared_ptr<Store> constructor remains as a delegating view until Store is removed. Session, ownership, admission, revocation and roster behavior are unchanged. Checks: Release build, full CTest (1573 tests including the new AuthTest.CharacterOwnerFollowsSelection, 0 failures), tools.module_includes, and the disposable-cluster PostgreSQL and reconnect tools. Refactor: the server builds one repository set (apps/repositories.cpp) over a single memory or PostgreSQL store and hands each service only the members it uses; WorldListener::set_repositories replaces set_mail_store and WorldState::repositories replaces mail_store - each session path uses its own repository member with the same unset-store refusal behavior, and startup order and messages are unchanged. Checks: full CTest (1573, 0 failures), the mail and market smoke tools, and the disposable-cluster PostgreSQL and reconnect tools.

## Client preferences, exploration REST and feedback

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Client-exclusive data/hotkeys, fog persistence, adventure-object REST and development feedback.

**Current implementation**

- Hot-key quick slots: GET /api/front/CharHotKeyLoadReq/<char_id>/<n> answers CharHotKeys and PUT /api/front/CharHotKeySaveReq/<char_id>/<n> stores or clears one CharHotKey for the session's selected character; loads answer for any character of the session's account and realm, because the hosted server logged client loads from the lobby before CharSelectReq that the client does not repeat after selection (Bearer token, application/protobuf), persisted in schema 21 outside the world-progress revision. Contract from static client analysis (dumps/ida_research/hotkeys-20261026).
- World-map fog: GET /api/front/CharFogAreaLoadReq/<char_id> returns FogAreaLoadRes and PUT /api/front/CharFogAreaSaveReq/<char_id> merges FogAreaSaveReq discoveries for the authenticated selected character. Migration 25 persists discoveries independently of gameplay revisions; repeated, delayed and empty saves cannot erase areas. Matching-build static client discovery sends one newly revealed id.
- GM reveal_map (alias unlock_map) merges every positive unique id in the verified FogArea catalog into the issuing GM character only (1063 in the researched export), through the same atomic character/realm-owned union. Repeated reveals and delayed client saves preserve the set, independently of gameplay revisions. The character must be reselected to invoke the recovered fog load path; no live refresh opcode is claimed.
- Offline exploration guide: tools/build_exploration_places.py joins verified Zone/Map tables with authored discovery, NPC-spawn and trade-parking positions. It retains all 405 named Zone rows plus 6 authored trading posts (411 destinations), with 307 same-ArcheWorld teleport commands. Exact discovery anchors, approximate bounding-box/map-layer matches and missing anchors are labeled separately; no safe landing or dungeon compatibility is claimed. tools/export_client_data.py regenerates the guide alongside full exports.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Client-exclusive data, adventure-object REST and development feedback routes are not served; their URLs/verbs are unverified.
- The hot-key path segment after the character id (always 1) has an unknown meaning; no original-client hot-key trial has been performed.
- Fog discovery remains client-reported except the explicit GM reveal; server polygon/travel authority and Adventure Progress objective counters are separate unfinished work. Catalog-backed saves reject unknown ids through the shared strictly validated FogArea index; extracting that index preserves the prior REST methods, response bodies, bounds and merge contract. Catalog-free REST still validates positive ids/counts only, while GM reveal requires the verified catalog. Original-client fog rendering and live deployment are unverified; already-lost discoveries cannot be reconstructed.
- Client discovery depends on dialogue lifecycle (2026-10-27): the client reveals and saves fog only from its one-second, 5100 cm locality-cell tick, which is suspended while any FX5DirectingManager bit is set. An NPC/station conversation sets bit 1 on DialogueStartRes and clears it only after a DialogueEndNoti naming the local player's wire unit. Hosted release 0.2.1 still builds ProcessingSession with the raw character ID, so a crafting-station dialogue left one live client in that state: fog saves stopped for the rest of the process (world re-entry did not reset it). The source correction is the crafting wire-unit change; it is not deployed and original-client fog acceptance after it is unverified. Affected players must restart the game client.

**Evidence and verification**

Lobby hot-key load (2026-10-27): HotKeyRestTest.RejoinLoadsOwnedSlotsBeforeSelectionButSavesOnlyAfterIt covers an unselected owned load, a foreign-character refusal and selection-gated saves. Static client analysis establishes hot-key and fog URLs, verbs, bearer headers, protobuf bodies and incremental fog saves. Hot-key synthetic checks cover load/save/clear/refusals. Fog Release verification on 2026-10-26: all seven focused cases passed, including catalog validation and isolated PostgreSQL concurrent merge/reopen/capacity rollback; native HTTP save/load retained every discovery across one server restart and one PostgreSQL restart. Existing memory/native login integrations passed. Child tests use the documented OpenSSL diagnostic. Original-client rendering and live deployment remain unverified. Additional 2026-10-26 author-run checks: eight fog cases passed with a disposable PostgreSQL cluster, including catalog-wide GM reveal and delayed-save/reopen preservation; the cluster was stopped. NativeWorld.GmMapRevealPersistsOnlyTheIssuingCharacterOverTls passed with two synthetic authenticated connections, proving ordinary-player refusal and issuing-GM-only persistence. The focused chronicles-exploration-tests target passed 24 cases (optional PostgreSQL skipped there and passed separately); all seven exporter checks passed. Exploration exporter checks cover all named catalog entries, exact versus approximate anchors, missing coordinates, deterministic ordering and script-data escaping; browser search/filter/visited and copy fallback were exercised. Release chronicles-server built. An unrelated missing nui_statue.hpp blocked the concurrently edited broad test target; no full-suite or original-client acceptance claim. Other preference routes have shapes only. Fog stall investigation 2026-10-27 (observed local-client behavior on the hosted 0.2.1 service, read-only): server fog REST answered every load/save with HTTP 200 and stored rows matched the client's discovered set; the client stopped saving 14 ms after a crafting-station DialogueStartReq whose DialogueEndNoti named the raw character ID. ReadProcessMemory showed FX5DirectingManager bits = 1, X5ConversationManager active and closing on a doodad target, a frozen locality timer and an unchanged cell while the player moved. ## Emotes, social animations and selfie mode

**Feature status: IMPLEMENTED.**

Emote execution and its error codes, emote and selfie notifications to nearby players, Basic and granted emotion ownership with persistence, the entry snapshot and GM grants. PC2S_StartSocialMotionReq is outside the client contract: this build never sends it.

**Current implementation**

- EmotionExecReq (20063) is checked in order: loaded map and catalog row (Emotion_InvalidData), ownership (Emotion_NotOwned), death (Emotion_Dead), skill in progress (Emotion_UsingSkill), gathering or tutorial interaction (Emotion_Interaction), riding or a movement mode other than Normal/Crouching (Emotion_NonGroundIdle) and GameVariable EmotionCooltimeSec since the last accepted emote, less a 200 ms arrival allowance (Emotion_Cooltime). A refusal answers EmotionExecRes{ec} to the requester only and does not start the cooldown.
- An accepted emote answers an empty EmotionExecRes (Success), which the client needs to play its own emote, and sends EmotionExecNoti{unit_id, emotion_cms_id, tick, pos, yaw} to every client that sees the player: server position and tick, requested yaw when finite within +/-360 degrees.
- Emotion.jsonl rows and EmotionCooltimeSec load at startup. Basic rows are always owned, matching the client's own seeding; other categories need a grant. Grants persist in WorldProgress.owned_emotions (table emulator_character_emotions, schema version 27, never removed) in the memory and PostgreSQL stores.
- WorldCharEmotionsNoti lists granted emotions once per connection after the first StartPlayingRes, before the guild snapshot; a Basic-only character receives the observed empty message. The GM text command emotion_add <emotion_id> commits a non-Basic grant and sends EmotionsUpdateNoti.
- SelfieModeReq (20064) state changes send SelfieModeNoti{unit_id, enter} to current viewers; repeated reports send nothing and entry is ignored while dead or outside a loaded map. A shared registry replays SelfieModeNoti{enter=true} after the UnitAddNoti for later viewers; map loads and disconnects clear it silently.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- PC2S_StartSocialMotionReq has no wrapper, opcode or sender in this client build (only a packet-logging name and RTTI), so it is not handled.
- The exported catalog has only Basic emotions and no item, quest or shop grants an emotion; the GM command is the only grant source and refuses every exported id.
- Emotion_Reaction (hit reactions or crowd control) is not modeled; looping emotes (13, 14) are not replayed to later viewers and the end of a loop is not tracked.
- Candidate: the client's Basic category byte, the local-actor meaning of the notification guard and the error-code order. Emulator policy: the cooldown allowance, server position, ignoring selfie entry while dead and replaying selfie state.
- No official emote, selfie or grant exchange was captured and no original-client trial has been performed.

**Evidence and verification**

The whole chronicles-tests run had 786 passed, 74 skipped and one access violation in NativeWorld.BagUnequipWithCarriedWeightAboveDefaultSafeWeightHasNoRefusal that also occurs in test builds made before this change. **Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`PC2S_StartSocialMotionReq`** — Not sent by this client build: no wrapper vtable, opcode or sender; only a packet-logging name and RTTI exist. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:type (x5.cms.EX5SocialMotion); 2:cur_state (x5.cms.EX5Posture); 3:reset_for_only_npc_server (bool)
- **`PC2S_EmotionExecReq`** — Validated against catalog, ownership, life, skill, interaction, ground mode and cooldown; answered with EmotionExecRes. No official request captured; static client contract only. Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:emotion_cms_id (int32); 2:pos (x5.pb.WorldPos); 3:yaw (float)
- **`PC2S_SelfieModeReq`** — State report without a response; repeated reports and entry while dead are ignored (emulator policy). Schema file: `p_c2s.proto`. Fields: 1:enter (bool)
- **`PS2C_EmotionExecRes`** — Empty (Success) for an accepted emote, which the client needs to play it; Emotion_* codes for refusals. Code order is Candidate. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode)
- **`PS2C_EmotionExecNoti`** — Sent to every client that sees the emoting player, with server position and tick. Shape matches the four P1 notifications. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:unit_id (uint64); 2:emotion_cms_id (int32); 3:tick (sfixed64); 4:pos (x5.pb.WorldPos); 5:yaw (float)
- **`PS2C_SelfieModeNoti`** — Sent to current viewers on a state change and after UnitAddNoti to later viewers (emulator policy). Not captured officially. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:unit_id (uint64); 2:enter (bool)
- **`PS2C_WorldCharEmotionsNoti`** — Once per connection after the first StartPlayingRes; lists granted emotions, empty for Basic-only characters as in every capture. Schema file: `p_s2c.character.proto`. Fields: 1:emotions (repeated x5.pb.EmotionData)
- **`PS2C_EmotionsUpdateNoti`** — Sent with a persisted GM emotion_add grant. The exported catalog has no grantable (non-Basic) row, so the path is synthetic-only with shipped data. Schema file: `p_s2c.character.proto`. Fields: 1:emotions (repeated x5.pb.EmotionData)

## Common messages and service announcements

**Feature status: PARTIAL.**

Errors, feature matrix, announcements, lobby updates and remaining service/common schemas.

**Current implementation**

- Recovered generic errors are emitted for selected invalid world/front requests.
- Operator on-screen notice: the console sends PS2C_SystemMessageNoti with free text and a Text, Banner or Popup type to every authenticated character with a known map position. Synthetic encode/decode coverage only.
- The same enabled rotating server-message scheduler can send free-text PS2C_SystemMessageNoti banners at configurable intervals. Operator GET/POST /admin/v1/server-messages edits and persists recurring and welcome settings; disabled messages stay quiet.
- Contextual guide notifications select client-localized text and control-tip cards from the authored contents-guide catalog. Supported location, quest, item, active-weapon, interaction and cutscene conditions are evaluated per session in tutorial and shared worlds.

**Missing behavior and limitations**

- Feature matrix and announcement semantics and other unrelated messages remain incomplete.
- A common error response cannot stand in for the feature-specific success path.
- Official captures set only SystemMessageNoti.key; whether the original client renders free text is unverified. WSF2C_Announce, WSF2C_SystemMessageNoti and WSF2C_LobbyUpdateNoti are not sent.
- Contents-guide support is partial: unresolved authored conditions cannot by themselves establish a match; full-screen Contents cards and durable per-character guide history are not implemented. The original-client layout and behavior have not been validated.

**Payload fields and packet-specific runtime limits**

- **`PS2C_CommonErrorRes`** — Generic error serialization exists for current handlers; this does not implement missing feature operations. Schema file: `p_system.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode); 2:category (x5.pb.EErrorCategory); 3:custom_message (string); 4:is_internal (bool); 11:gmcmd (x5.pb.GmCmd); 12:level_trigger (x5.pb.CommonErrorRes.LevelTrigger); 13:channel_move_cooldown (x5.pb.CommonErrorRes.ChannelMoveCooldown); 15:packet_seq (x5.pb.PacketSeq)
- **`PS2C_SystemMessageNoti`** — Operator notices and enabled recurring server announcements send free text with a display type (scheduled announcements use Banner). Official captures use CMS keys; original-client free-text rendering remains unverified. Schema file: `p_system.proto`. Fields: 1:key (x5.cms.ESystemMessage); 2:text (string); 3:type (x5.cms.EX5SystemMessageType)
- **`PS2C_VisualSignNoti`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:unit_id (uint64); 2:type (x5.pb.VisualSignType)
- **`PS2C_ContentsGuideNoti`** — Sends client-localized text/control-tip guide starts and stops for supported authored conditions. Static client dispatch and synthetic TLS delivery were checked; no official guide packet capture or original-client rendering has been established. Schema file: `p_s2c.proto`. Fields: 1:contents_guide_cms_id (int32); 2:start_trigger (bool)
- **`REST_F2C_ErrorCodeRes`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_f2c.rest.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode)
- **`WSF2C_CommonErrorRes`** — Generic error serialization exists for current handlers; this does not implement missing feature operations. Schema file: `p_system.proto`. Fields: 1:ec (x5.ec.EErrorCode); 2:category (x5.pb.EErrorCategory); 3:custom_message (string); 4:is_internal (bool); 11:gmcmd (x5.pb.GmCmd); 12:level_trigger (x5.pb.CommonErrorRes.LevelTrigger); 13:channel_move_cooldown (x5.pb.CommonErrorRes.ChannelMoveCooldown); 15:packet_seq (x5.pb.PacketSeq)
- **`WSF2C_SystemMessageNoti`** — Sent only as the friend-add alarm key SM_FRIEND_ADD_ALARM (335) to an in-world player. Free text, announcements and other keys are not sent on the front socket. Schema file: `p_system.proto`. Fields: 1:key (x5.cms.ESystemMessage); 2:text (string); 3:type (x5.cms.EX5SystemMessageType)
- **`WSF2C_Announce`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_f2c.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:message (string); 2:display_secs (float)
- **`WSF2C_LobbyUpdateNoti`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_f2c.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:char_creation_restricted (bool)
- **`WSF2C_FeatureMatrixNoti`** — No current runtime path established. Schema file: `p_f2c.ws.proto`. Fields: 1:values (repeated x5.pb.frontwebsocket.FeatureMatrixNoti.ValuesEntry)
